Note the manifest is fetched **twice** (both GETs for the same digest succeed and return 200), then the process fails with zero further log lines — no blob-copy progress, no additional debug output of any kind. This means the failing call is inside a function that returns an error without logging anything, most likely something in the `containers/image` OCI-artifact copy path used specifically for the WSL disk-image artifact (as opposed to a normal layered image pull, which does log blob-copy progress).

### Describe the results you expected

`podman machine init` downloads the ~236MB `podman-machine.x86_64.wsl.tar.zst` artifact and proceeds to import it into WSL, as it does successfully on other machines.

### What I verified to rule out environment causes

- **Not a filesystem/permissions/AV problem**: I manually wrote a file to the exact path from the debug log (`...\machine\wsl\cache\24672f84....tar.zst`) using plain PowerShell `Out-File` — it succeeded instantly.
- **Not a WSL problem**: WSL2 itself works fine on this host (an unrelated distro runs normally; `wsl --version` reports a healthy install).
- **Not stale config**: no `CONTAINERS_*`/`PODMAN_*` env var overrides; `.local/share/containers` and its subfolders are ordinary directories, not symlinks/junctions; `containers.conf`/`storage.conf` are empty (defaults).
- **Not a 6.0.2 regression**: downgrading the CLI to 5.8.6 (clean MSI uninstall + reinstall) reproduces the *exact same* error shape, just against the 5.8 tag's manifest digest instead of 6.0's.

### Workaround that confirms the issue is isolated to the pull step

I manually replicated the registry calls with `curl` (auth token → OCI index → platform-specific manifest → blob digest `sha256:136d18cda8e767721e9f1a7c4fa8e3f70973a83b72dddc9dcb7acbfd502ed37e`, 247644831 bytes), downloaded the blob directly, verified its SHA256 matched the manifest exactly, and placed it at the cache path Podman itself computes (`...\machine\wsl\cache\<manifest-digest>.tar.zst`). With the file already present, `podman machine init --now` immediately succeeded — treated it as a cache hit, imported it into WSL, and started the machine normally. This confirms the bug is specifically in Podman's own download/write step for this artifact, not in registry access, auth, or WSL import.

```

Version:      5.8.6
API Version:  5.8.6
Go Version:   go1.26.5
OS/Arch:      windows/amd64
```
(Also reproduced on 6.0.2, Git Commit b28edb9ad70ce4317dc762ee9ce0a6d081d154e9, built 2026-07-22.)

### Output of `podman info` (post-workaround, machine running)

```
provider: wsl
Host.OS: linux
Host.Arch: amd64
```

title: pkg/bindings: keep auth fields out of the query string
body:
When podman remote runs kube play, manifest add/modify/inspect or image
pull/push/search, it copies Authfile, Username and Password into the query
string of the request URL. The server does not read them there, it takes the
credentials from the X-Registry-Auth header instead, so the copies in the URL
serve no purpose.
Commit cfdca82938 added schema:"-" to these fields for image pull and push so
that ToParams leaves them out. The same tag was never added to the other
options, so this adds it.
InspectOptions.SkipTLSVerify had the same problem. Tagging it also lets me
drop the two params.Del("SkipTLSVerify") calls, which never removed anything
because ToParams stores keys in lower case and Del is case sensitive.
The tests in pkg/bindings/test/types_test.go now check that these fields do
not appear in the query string.

title: libpod: delay volume unmount in Export() until stream Close()
body: ## Description Ran into a bug in `Volume.Export()` (`libpod/volume.go`) - `v.unmount(false)` was deferred inside the function itself, which means the volume got unmounted right away, before the caller actually had a chance to read from the returned `io.ReadCloser`. Depending on timing you'd get truncated or empty exports. Fix is a new `volumeExportReadCloser` wrapper that holds off on `v.unmount(false)` until the consumer calls `Close()` on the tar stream, so the unmount only happens once the read is actually done. Also fixed up the error paths so if tar creation fails partway through, the volume still gets unmounted properly instead of leaking a mount. ## Verification Ran the existing volume tests first: `go test -tags "exclude_graphdriver_btrfs libsqlite3 systemd libsubid seccomp" -v ./libpod -run TestVolume` — passed. Then did a manual end-to-end check: 1. Created a named volume `test_export_vol` 2. Wrote test data to `/data/testfile.txt` 3. Exported it - `./bin/podman volume export test_export_vol --output test_export_vol.tar` 4. Checked the tar was non-empty and contained `testfile.txt` with expected content ("Bug 1 Fix Verified") Signed-off-by: Mandar Joshi

title: events: logfile: do not immediately stop tail when until is in the past
body:
<!-- Please include the 'why' behind your changes if no issue exists -->
### Fixes
Fixes #29579

### Description
When using `events_logger = "file"`, invoking `podman events` with `--until` set to a timestamp or duration in the past caused the logfile reader to stop immediately before historical events could be collected from the file.

This occurred because `time.Until(untilTime)` evaluates to a non-positive duration when `untilTime` is in the past, causing the background timer goroutine in `EventLogFile.Read` to immediately call `t.Stop()`, closing `t.Lines` concurrently during startup.

This PR checks `time.Until(untilTime) > 0` before launching the timer goroutine. Filtering for past events already continues to function accurately via `generateEventUntilOption` in `applyFilters`.

### Tests
- Added unit test `TestEventLogFileReadUntilInPast` in `libpod/events/logfile_test.go` verifying historical event reads when `--until` is in the past without streaming.
- Signed-off with DCO.

Signed-off-by: K J sundeep kumar <sundeep8967@gmail.com>

title: specgen: ensure keep-id overrides image USER
body:
Fixes #29600

#### What this PR does / why we need it
When running a container with `--userns=keep-id`, `s.User` retained the image's default `USER` directive if no explicit `--user` flag was passed. This caused downstream spec generation to retain the image user instead of mapping to the host user running Podman.

In `namespaces.go` file where `s.User == ""` (it is already populated before when running the `container.go` file) therefore we need another check to see if it matches `s.User == imageUser`.

Added tests too in `test/e2e/run_userns_test.go` file

title: log: expose conmon log rotation options through REST API and CLI
body:
## Description

- Fixes #29543 

conmon 2.2.0 added support for `--log-rotate` and `--log-max-files`, but Podman didn't expose them via `--log-opt` or the REST API.

This patch adds `max-file` and `log-rotate` to `--log-opt`:
- `--log-opt max-file=<n>`: max rotated log files to retain (implicitly sets rotation)
- `--log-opt log-rotate=true|false`: explicitly enable/disable log rotation


**Example:**
```sh
podman run -d \
  --log-driver k8s-file \
  --log-opt max-size=10mb \
  --log-opt max-file=5 \
  nginx
```

### Testing:

``` 
# Unit tests
go test -v -tags linux ./pkg/specgenutil/... -run TestLogOpt

# Manual smoke test (requires conmon >= 2.2.0)
podman run -d --log-driver k8s-file \
  --log-opt max-size=1mb --log-opt max-file=3 \
  --name test-rotate alpine sh -c 'while true; do echo hello; done'
podman inspect test-rotate --format '{{.HostConfig.LogConfig.Config}}'

# Expected: map[max-file:3]
podman rm -f test-rotate
```
Note: --log-rotate and --log-max-files require conmon >= 2.2.0.

title: fix(api): nil check Memory.Limit before dereference in stats handler

labels.name: kind/api-change
labels.description: Change to remote API; merits scrutiny

body:
Fixes #29627

When a container is created with `--memory-reservation` but without `--memory-limit`, the OCI spec has a non-nil `Memory` object with a nil `Limit` pointer. The compat stats handler dereferences `*resources.Memory.Limit` without checking for nil first, causing a panic that returns a 500 error to the client.

Add a nil check for `resources.Memory.Limit` before dereferencing it.

### How to reproduce

```
podman run -d --name t --memory-reservation 10m --entrypoint sleep alpine 60
curl -s --unix-socket /run/podman/podman.sock 'http://d/v1.41/containers/t/stats?stream=false'
```

### Test plan

Added a regression test in `test/apiv2/19-stats.at` that creates a container with `--memory-reservation` only and verifies the stats endpoint returns 200 without panic.

### Test result

N/A — will be verified by CI once authorized.

title: specgen: ensure keep-id overrides image USER
body:
Fixes #29600

#### What this PR does / why we need it
When running a container with `--userns=keep-id`, `s.User` retained the image's default `USER` directive if no explicit `--user` flag was passed. This caused downstream spec generation to retain the image user instead of mapping to the host user running Podman.

In `namespaces.go` file where `s.User == ""` (it is already populated before when running the `container.go` file) therefore we need another check to see if it matches `s.User == imageUser`.

title: Fix: conmon and pasta processes left in control group when running po…
body:
Hi everyone,

This PR fixes issue #29582 - conmon and pasta processes being left in the
control group when running podman from a systemd user service.

## The Problem

When running `podman` commands from a systemd user service (like `deployer.service`),
the `conmon` and `pasta` processes would end up in the parent service's control
group. This caused two main issues:

1. Systemd would hang while waiting for these processes to exit when stopping/restarting
   the service (default 60 second timeout)
2. With `--restart=always`, the containers would get restarted unexpectedly

## Root Cause

In `libpod/oci_conmon_linux.go`, the `moveConmonToCgroupAndSignal()` function
had a check for the `INVOCATION_ID` environment variable. When running under
systemd as a service, this check was setting `mustCreateCgroup = false`, which
prevented conmon from being moved to its own systemd scope (`libpod-conmon-<ID>.scope`).
As a result, conmon remained in the parent service's control group.

## The Fix

Removed the INVOCATION_ID condition (5 lines deleted from
`libpod/oci_conmon_linux.go`). Now conmon is always moved to its own scope
when cgroups are enabled, regardless of whether running under systemd as a service.

The pasta process scope management was already handled separately in
`vendor/go.podman.io/common/libnetwork/internal/rootlessnetns/netns_linux.go`
which moves pasta to `user.slice/rootless-netns-<random>.scope` when
`systemd.RunsOnSystemd()` is true.

## Changed Files

- `libpod/oci_conmon_linux.go` - Removed INVOCATION_ID

## Testing

This is a Linux/systemd-specific fix. The change ensures conmon processes are
properly scoped and won't prevent systemd user services from being restarted
or stopped cleanly.

title: kube: Add support for securityContext.seccompProfile.*

labels.name: kind/feature
labels.description: Categorizes issue or PR as related to a new feature.

body:
### Feature request description

Historically, configuring the seccomp profile in Kubernetes was done using annotations, specifically:
* `seccomp.security.alpha.kubernetes.io/pod`
* `container.seccomp.security.alpha.kubernetes.io/<containerName>`

This is the mechanism currently supported by podman play kube (see https://github.com/podman-container-tools/podman/issues/8130 for more information).

Meanwhile, Kubernetes introduced a dedicated syntax (in v1.19) using the `securityContext.seccompProfile.type` & `securityContext.seccompProfile.localhostProfile` fields (both at the pod level and container level). At the same time, the old annotations were deprecated.

In v1.27, Kubernetes completely removed support for the annotations (see [this entry in the changelog for v1.27](https://kubernetes.io/blog/2023/03/17/upcoming-changes-in-kubernetes-v1-27/#support-for-deprecated-seccomp-annotations)).

Would it be possible to add support for the new fields in podman?

### Suggest potential solution

Proposed transition plan:
* In podman 6.x:
  * Add support for the `securityContext.seccompProfile.type` & `securityContext.seccompProfile.localhostProfile` fields
  * If both the annotations & fields are used, the values in the fields take precedence.
  * Mark the old annotations as deprecated in the docs
* In podman 7.x:
  * Drop support for the old annotations completely

### Have you considered any alternatives?

Using the annotations currently works in podman, but prevents reusing the same YAML file to deploy an app to a Kubernetes cluster (the deployment will work, but the annotations will be silently ignored, which could be a security problem).

### Additional context

More information on the seccomp filtering feature in Kubernetes can be found at https://kubernetes.io/docs/tutorials/security/seccomp/

The systemd word-escaping helpers in `pkg/systemd/parser/split.go` — `escapeWords`

title: Rootless explicit single-ID mapping produces empty intermediate OCI root

labels.name: kind/bug
labels.description: Categorizes issue or PR as related to a bug.

body:
### Issue Description

Rootless Podman fails during OCI initialization when using explicit single-ID UID/GID mappings. Podman successfully mounts the container image's overlay filesystem at the normal rootless storage merged path, but the generated OCI configuration gives crun a root.path under /var/tmp/intermediate-mountpoint-<uid>.<n>. During the observed failure, crun cannot see the image filesystem through that path.

The first observed failure is while crun tries to open /var/tmp/intermediate-mountpoint-<uid>.<n>/etc/hosts, which returns No such file or directory. A /run/.containerenv failure can occur later, but /etc/hosts failing first indicates that this is not specific to .containerenv.

The container uses an intentionally narrow mapping:

--uidmap=65532:1:1

--gidmap=65532:1:1

--user=65532:65532

The generated OCI spec contains those same one-entry UID/GID mappings. The failure occurs during podman container init; the container workload is never started.

Environment: Kali Linux/Debian-based, amd64, rootless Podman with native overlay on ext4. Podman 5.8.3+ds1-1, crun 1.28-1, conmon 2.1.13+ds1-2.

Is this a known issue with Podman's rootless intermediate-root staging when explicit UID/GID mappings deliberately leave container UID/GID 0 unmapped? If it has already been fixed upstream, which commit and first Podman release contain the fix?

### Steps to reproduce the issue


1. On a rootless Podman installation, create an inert container using explicit single-ID mappings:

   podman create \
     --name single-id-repro \
     --network=none \
     --uidmap=65532:1:1 \
     --gidmap=65532:1:1 \
     --user=65532:65532 \
     --read-only \
     <IMAGE> \
     <INERT_COMMAND>

2. Initialize the container with runtime debug logging, but do not start it:

   podman --log-level=debug \
     --runtime-flag=debug \
     --runtime-flag=log=/tmp/crun-single-id-repro.log \
     container init single-id-repro

3. Observe that OCI initialization fails before the container workload starts. In the reproduced case, crun reports:

   open `/var/tmp/intermediate-mountpoint-<uid>.<n>/etc/hosts`:
   No such file or directory

4. Inspect the generated OCI config.json. It identifies:

   root.path = /var/tmp/intermediate-mountpoint-<uid>.<n>

   while the UID/GID mappings remain:

   container UID 65532 -> host/intermediate ID 1, size 1
   container GID 65532 -> host/intermediate ID 1, size 1

5. Podman debug output shows that the image overlay was successfully mounted separately at its normal rootless storage `merged` path.

6. Do not issue `podman start`. Remove the inert reproducer afterward:

   podman rm --force --ignore single-id-repro

### Describe the results you received

podman container init fails before the container process starts.

Podman successfully mounts the populated image overlay at its normal rootless-storage merged location, but the generated OCI specification gives crun a root path under /var/tmp/intermediate-mountpoint-<uid>.<n>.

That intermediate root does not contain the expected image filesystem. The first observed crun failure is resolving:

/var/tmp/intermediate-mountpoint-<uid>.<n>/etc/hosts

which returns No such file or directory.

The generated OCI configuration still contains the requested single-entry UID/GID mappings (65532 -> 1, size 1) and process identity 65532:65532.

The workload itself is never executed.

### Describe the results you expected

podman container init should successfully prepare the OCI container without starting the workload.

The OCI root.path supplied to crun should expose the populated image root filesystem, including directories such as /etc and /run, so that OCI mount targets such as /etc/hosts can be prepared successfully.

If this explicit single-ID UID/GID mapping is unsupported, Podman should instead reject the configuration with a clear mapping-related error rather than handing crun an intermediate root that does not contain the image filesystem.

### podman info output

```yaml
Podman version: 5.8.3+ds1-1
crun version: 1.28-1
conmon version: 2.1.13+ds1-2

OS: Kali Linux (Debian-based)
Architecture: amd64
Mode: rootless
Storage driver: overlay (native overlay)
Backing filesystem: ext4
OCI runtime: crun
```

### Podman in a container

No

### Privileged Or Rootless

Rootless

### Upstream Latest Release

No

### Additional environment details

Kali Linux (Debian-based), amd64. Podman is running rootless directly on the host, not inside a container. Storage uses native overlay on ext4. OCI runtime is crun. The reproducer intentionally uses explicit single-ID UID/GID mappings and leaves container UID/GID 0 unmapped.

### Additional information

The failure appears to occur at the handoff between Podman's rootless intermediate-root staging and crun.

Podman debug evidence showed the real image overlay mounted successfully at its normal .../overlay/<layer>/merged location, while the generated OCI root.path pointed to /var/tmp/intermediate-mountpoint-<uid>.<n>. That intermediate root did not expose the expected image filesystem when crun performed OCI initialization.

The first observed failure was /etc/hosts, before /run/.containerenv, so the issue does not appear to be .containerenv-specific.

I have not worked around the problem by broadening the UID/GID mappings, mapping container root, changing host permissions, or modifying the image.

I have also not reproduced this against the latest upstream Podman release yet.

Is this a known intermediate-root staging issue? If it has already been fixed upstream, could you point me to the fixing commit and the first release containing it? I can provide sanitized OCI config.json and Podman/crun debug excerpts if useful.

title: Security: Prevent API DoS via unbounded memory read in manifests handler
body:
In `pkg/api/handlers/libpod/manifests.go`, the API endpoint reads the incoming HTTP request payload directly into memory using `io.ReadAll(r.Body)`.

Because there is no upper bound enforced on the reader, a malicious client or a faulty script could send an infinitely streaming or excessively large payload (e.g., several gigabytes) to this endpoint. This forces the Podman daemon to blindly load the entire payload into memory, which can lead to rapid resource exhaustion, an Out-Of-Memory (OOM) crash, and a complete Denial-of-Service (DoS) for the API. 

This can be easily mitigated by wrapping the request body in an `io.LimitReader` to enforce a reasonable maximum manifest size limit before calling `io.ReadAll`. 

I would be happy to submit a quick Pull Request to add an `io.LimitReader` and close this attack vector if maintainers agree!

title: `--userns=keep-id` does not override image `USER` as documented

labels.name: kind/bug
labels.description: Categorizes issue or PR as related to a bug.

body:
### Issue Description

When running an image that defines a `USER`, `podman run --userns=keep-id` keeps using the image-defined user instead of running the container process as the invoking host user.

This appears to contradict the Podman documentation for `keep-id`, which states that the container init process runs with the current user's UID and that this overrides the image's `USER` instruction unless `--user` is explicitly specified [[reference](https://github.com/podman-container-tools/podman/blob/main/docs/source/markdown/options/userns.container.md?plain=1#L63)].

I first noticed this behavior with Podman 5.8.4, but I can reproduce it with a source build of `main` as reported in the dedicated section below.


### Steps to reproduce the issue

Steps to reproduce the issue
1. Create an image defining a non-standard user, e.g.
```
$ cat Containerfile
FROM fedora:43
RUN useradd --uid 1001 appuser 
USER 1001

$ podman build -t user-override .
STEP 1/3: FROM fedora:43
STEP 2/3: RUN useradd --uid 1001 appuser 
--> cb69dcfa699f
STEP 3/3: USER 1001
COMMIT user-override
--> 812e937fa17e
Successfully tagged localhost/user-override:latest
812e937fa17ed7db783ff5eadfe6c9eedcf04842b655498d7ad850927d61142d
```
2. Run the image with a rootless user that has a different host uid from the one set in the Containerfile, and use `--userns=keep-id`
```
$ id
uid=1000(amadonna) gid=1000(amadonna) groups=1000(amadonna),...
$ podman run --rm --userns=keep-id localhost/user-override:latest id
```

### Describe the results you received

With no options, the container runs as the `USER` from the Containerfile, as expected
```
$ podman run --rm localhost/user-override:latest id
uid=1001(appuser) gid=1001(appuser) groups=1001(appuser)
```

With the `--userns=keep-id` option, the Containerfile `USER` still wins (auxiliary groups are modified though)
```
$ podman run --rm --userns=keep-id localhost/user-override:latest id
uid=1001(appuser) gid=1001(appuser) groups=1001(appuser),1000(amadonna)
```

### Describe the results you expected

A similar behavior as when there is no specific user entered in the Containerfile, e.g.:
```
$ podman run --rm fedora:43 id
uid=0(root) gid=0(root) groups=0(root)

$ podman run --rm --userns=keep-id fedora:43 id
uid=1000(amadonna) gid=1000(amadonna) groups=1000(amadonna)
```

Reusing the earlier example:
```
$ podman run --rm --userns=keep-id localhost/user-override:latest id
uid=1000(amadonna) gid=1000(amadonna) groups=1000(amadonna)
```

### Additional information

I used an LLM to survey the Podman source code in relation to this behavior and here is a summary of its analysis:

> The likely cause is the interaction between these two code paths:
> 
> * `pkg/specgen/generate/container.go`: `CompleteSpec()` copies `inspectData.Config.User` into `s.User` when `s.User` is empty.
> * `pkg/specgen/generate/namespaces.go`: the `specgen.KeepID` handling only applies the invoking user's UID/GID when `s.User == ""`.
> 
> By the time the `keep-id` logic runs, `s.User` may already contain the image's `Config.User`, so the code can no longer distinguish an image-provided `USER` from an explicitly supplied `--user`. As a result, the image user prevents the `keep-id` process-user override from being applied.
> 
> The relevant condition appears to be the `if s.User == ""` check in the `specgen.KeepID` branch of `namespaceOptions()`. The intended condition seems to be whether the user was explicitly overridden by the caller, rather than whether the resolved `s.User` field is empty.
> 
> I verified that this code pattern is still present in Podman 6.1.0.

title: test/system: fail loudly when _prefetch cannot fetch or load an image
body:
_prefetch runs two commands bare, so a failure in either is invisible at the
point it happens.

The third and final 'podman pull' retry runs $cmd directly rather than through
run, so its exit status is never checked. If all three attempts fail, _prefetch
returns as though it succeeded and leaves either no cache entry or a partial
one behind.

The skopeo copy that loads the cached archive into containers-storage has the
same problem. If it fails, the image is simply absent.

Either way the test that asked for the image carries on and fails later with an
unrelated-looking 'image not found', pointing at the test rather than at the
fetch that actually broke. That is expensive to debug because the symptom and
the cause are in different places.

Check the status of both, remove a partial archive so the next run refetches
rather than loading a truncated one, and die with the real reason.

title: test/e2e: keep containerfile out of the build context
body:
I was going through the rerun history to work out why `podman image rm - concurrent with shared layers` keeps coming back, and got stuck because the log gives you nothing:

```
[FAILED] BuildImage session output: "STEP 1/2: FROM ... STEP 2/2: RUN touch rmtest:0 COMMIT rmtest:0"
Expected <int>: 1 to match exit code: <int>: 0
```

the build reached COMMIT and then exited 1, and the reason is nowhere in the job output. the assert only prints `OutputToString()`, which is stdout, so build errors on stderr get dropped. second commit adds stderr there.

first commit is what I noticed while reading that helper. it writes its generated Containerfile into `p.TempDir` and then passes `p.TempDir` as the build context, so concurrent builds walk a directory the others are still writing into. that test starts 10 builds in goroutines. running just the file layout:

```
entries each build saw in its own context: [10 10 5 10 10 10 7 10 6 6]
```

`--file` takes an absolute path so the Containerfile does not need to sit in the context. TempDir stays the context since some tests drop files there for COPY and ADD, and the new test checks both halves.

I cant claim this fixes the flake, with stderr dropped there is no record of what actually failed.

title: pkg/machine/hyperv: detach 9p server from parent console

labels.name: No New Tests
labels.description: Allow PR to proceed without adding regression tests

body:
<!--
Thank you for contributing to Podman!
-->

### Description

On Windows, when starting a Hyper-V machine in CMD.EXE or PowerShell, the background 9p server (`podman.exe machine server9p`) was started without detached process creation flags. Because `podman.exe` is a console subsystem application, Windows automatically attached it to the caller's console session. Closing the CMD.EXE/PowerShell window sent a console close event and terminated the 9p server process, causing 9p volume mounts (such as `/etc/containers`) in the VM to fail with input/output errors.

This change:
1. Configures `SysProcAttr` with `CREATE_NEW_PROCESS_GROUP | DETACHED_PROCESS` on the 9p server command so it runs detached from the terminal session.
2. Decouples standard handles by redirecting `Stdin`, `Stdout`, and `Stderr` to `os.DevNull` (when debug file logging is not enabled) to prevent terminal sessions from hanging on exit due to open console handles.

Fixes: #29573

<!-- Thanks for sending a pull request! -->


The generated bindings filename was built with `strings.TrimRight(srcFile, ".go")`,
which treats `".go"` as a cutset and strips any trailing run of `.`, `g`, `o`
characters rather than the `.go` suffix. Every current `//go:generate` caller
passes `types.go` (trimmed to `types` either way) so today's output is correct,
but a directive in a file whose base name ends in `g`, `o` or `.` — e.g.

filename. Switches to `strings.TrimSuffix`, which removes exactly the suffix.

### moby/go-archive: Crafted tar archive can write outside the extraction directory
[CVE-2026-17106](https://nvd.nist.gov/vuln/detail/CVE-2026-17106) / [GHSA-hfg8-hc9c-6c3h](https://redirect.github.com/advisories/GHSA-hfg8-hc9c-6c3h)

<details>
<summary>More information</summary>

#### Details
##### Summary
The tar extraction routines in `moby/go-archive` (`Unpack`, `UnpackLayer`, `Untar`/`UntarUncompressed`, and the `ApplyLayer` helpers) do not confine filesystem operations to the destination directory. A crafted archive can create or overwrite files **outside** the intended destination. 

##### Details
The extractor decides where each archive entry lands using lexical string checks and then performs the filesystem operation on a path that is resolved by the OS, so a links introduced by the archive can be followed out of the destination directory.

##### Impact
An attacker who controls the contents of archive can create or overwrite files at arbitrary paths writable by the extracting process.

##### Workarounds
Only extract trusted archives.

#### Severity
- CVSS Score: 7.1 / 10 (High)
- Vector String: `CVSS:4.0/AV:L/AC:L/AT:P/PR:N/UI:A/VC:H/VI:H/VA:H/SC:N/SI:N/SA:N`

title: `pasta` and `conmon` processes are sometimes left in calling process' control group
body:
Software versions - Container host - Podman: 5.8.3 - conmon: 2.1.12 - pasta: commmit `587980c` - systemd: 257.13 - Running rootless - Development machine - Podman: 5.8.3
I have a web service (herein called *deployer*) which invokes Podman (using Node.js' `child_process.spawnSync()`) to create, start and stop containers. The *deployer* service is managed as a systemd unit. Note that in control group paths, I've used */.../* as a shorthand for */sys/fs/cgroup/user.slice/user-33.slice/user@33.service/*. **Problem:** When I attempt to stop or restart the *deployer* service, systemd hangs while waiting for all remaining processes in the control group */.../app.slice/deployer.service* to exit. This never happens, since the `conmon` and `pasta` processes created by Podman when *deployer* starts containers are left in the control group. *conmon* is not moved to its own *libpod-conmon-\.scope* control group as it usually is. After 60 seconds, systemd kills the `conmon` and `pasta` processes, killing the containers they support. With `--restart=always` set on the containers, they are restarted. That said, no `pasta` process is created when restarting them, making the containerised application inaccessible over the network. When running Podman in an SSH session, the `pasta` process lands in the control group */.../user.slice/podman-\.scope* and becomes a child of the system instance of systemd (PID 1). This allows the shell to exit without killing *pasta* or waiting for it to exit. That said, this transient control group is only supposed to live as long as the `podman` process does, but is kept alive by *pasta*. In some cases—I forget exactly which—the user instance of systemd complains in the journal about "left-over process[es]": ```txt Aug 11 02:20:15 systemd[993]: podman.service: Found left-over process 3323 (pasta) in control group while starting unit. Ignoring. Aug 11 02:20:15 systemd[993]: podman.service: Found left-over process 3927 (pasta) in control group while starting unit. Ignoring. Aug 11 02:20:15 systemd[993]: podman.service: Found left-over process 24491 (pasta) in control group while starting unit. Ignoring. Aug 11 02:20:20 systemd[993]: podman.service: Unit process 3323 (pasta) remains running after unit stopped. Aug 11 02:20:20 systemd[993]: podman.service: Unit process 3927 (pasta) remains running after unit stopped. Aug 11 02:20:20 systemd[993]: podman.service: Unit process 24491 (pasta) remains running after unit stopped. ``` **Possible fix:** Explicitly move any spawned support processes (e.g., `conmon`, `pasta`, `slirp4netns` perhaps) to a dedicated control group like *conmon* sometimes is; *libpod-support-\.scope* may be a more accurate name. --- I've tested several different methods of invoking Podman and recorded the parent processes and control groups of the spawned processes. I've left notes ("⚠️") wherever I think behaviour may not be correct. 1. Running Podman on development machine using remote system connection. > `podman` → SSH connection → `sshd-session` → `podman.socket` → `podman.service` → ...
Details ⚠️ ```sh podman run \ --connection=foo \ --rm \ --detach \ --publish=1234:1234 \ alpine sleep 1000 podman run \ --connection=foo \ --rm \ --tty \ --interactive \ --publish=1234:1234 \ alpine ``` | Process | Parent process | Control group | |-|-|-| | `podman` | `systemd` (user instance) | */.../app.slice/podman.service* | | `conmon` | `systemd` (user instance) | */.../user.slice/libpod-conmon-\.scope* | | `pasta` | `systemd` (user instance) | */.../app.slice/podman.service*
⚠️ Being daemonless, Podman's service unit should only live as long as the `podman` process. | | `sleep`/`sh` | `conmon` | */.../user.slice/libpod-\.scope/container* |
1. Running Podman on the host via SSH session.
Details ⚠️ ```sh podman run \ --rm \ --detach \ --publish=1234:1234 \ alpine sleep 1000 podman run \ --rm \ --tty \ --interactive \ --publish=1234:1234 \ alpine ``` | Process | Parent process | Control group | |-|-|-| | `podman` | `sshd-session` → `zsh` | */.../user.slice/podman-\.scope* | | `conmon` | `systemd` (PID 1)
⚠️ All other methods cause this process to be parented by the user instance of systemd, not PID 1. | */.../user.slice/libpod-conmon-\.scope* | | `pasta` | `systemd` (PID 1)
⚠️ *See above.* | */.../user.slice/podman-\.scope*
⚠️ Being transient, Podman's scope unit should only live as long as the `podman` process. | | `sleep`/`sh` | `conmon` | */.../user.slice/libpod-\.scope/container* |
1. Running Podman on the host from a user service (*deployer*).
Details ⚠️ ```sh podman run \ --rm \ --detach \ --publish=1234:1234 \ alpine sleep 1000 ``` | Process | Parent process | Control group | |-|-|-| | `podman` | `node` | */.../app.slice/deployer.service* | | `conmon` | `systemd` (user instance) | */.../app.slice/deployer.service*
⚠️ This process prevents the *deployer* service from being restarted without killing containers. | | `pasta` | `systemd` (user instance) | */.../app.slice/deployer.service*
⚠️ *See above.* | | `sleep`/`sh` | `conmon` | */.../user.slice/libpod-\.scope/container* |
1. Running Podman with `--cgroup-parent` on the host from a user service (*deployer*). ⚠️ This option seems to have no effect, even with an explicit `--cgroups` option. Is the example below incorrect?
Details ⚠️ ```sh podman run \ --rm \ --detach \ --publish=1234:1234 \ --cgroups=enabled \ --cgroup-parent=user.slice \ alpine sleep 1000 ``` | Process | Parent process | Control group | |-|-|-| | `podman` | `node` | */.../app.slice/deployer.service* | | `conmon` | `systemd` (user instance) | */.../app.slice/deployer.service*

title: events: fix premature tail termination on past --until in logfile backend
body:
Fixes #29579 

## What this PR does / why we need it

When using the file-based events backend (`events_logger = "file"`), invoking `podman events` with an `--until` timestamp or relative duration in the past (e.g., `--until 10m` or `--until <timestamp>`) caused `EventLogFile.Read` to spawn a background goroutine:

```go
go func() {
    time.Sleep(time.Until(untilTime))

    t.Stop()
}()
```

Since `untilTime` is in the past, `time.Until(untilTime)` returns a negative duration, causing `time.Sleep` to return immediately and call `t.Stop()`. This prematurely killed the tail reader before any historical events could be read from `events.log`.

This PR fixes the issue by:

1. Parsing `untilTime` upfront before launching the reading goroutine.
2. Checking each event's timestamp against `untilTime` inside the reader loop. When an event exceeds the boundary, the reader cleanly stops.
3. Adding deferred `t.Stop()` cleanup when the reading goroutine terminates.
4. Adding unit tests in `libpod/events/logfile_test.go` covering past `--until` boundaries and verifying that events before the cutoff are correctly returned.

## How to verify it

Run the following tests:

```bash
go test -v -count=1 ./libpod/events/ -run "TestReadEventsWithPastUntil|TestReadEventsWithUntilBeforeAllEvents"
```

## Which issue(s) this PR fixes

Fixes #<REPLACE_WITH_YOUR_ISSUE_NUMBER>

---

* [x] `go vet ./libpod/events/...` passes with 0 errors

  * `TestRotateLog`

  * `TestRenameLog`

  * `TestReadEventsWithUntilBeforeAllEvents`
* [x] Commit signed off with DCO (`git commit -s`)

title: events: logfile backend drops historical events when --until is in the past

labels.name: kind/bug
labels.description: Categorizes issue or PR as related to a bug.

body:
### Issue Description

When using the file-based events backend (`events_logger = "file"` in `containers.conf`), invoking `podman events` with an `--until` option set to a timestamp or relative duration in the past (e.g. `--until 10m` or `--until 2025-01-01T00:00:00`) causes the tail reader to terminate immediately before historical events can be read from `events.log`.

In `libpod/events/logfile.go` (`EventLogFile.Read`):
```go
if len(options.Until) > 0 {
    untilTime, err := util.ParseInputTime(options.Until, false)
    if err != nil {
        return err
    }
    go func() {
        time.Sleep(time.Until(untilTime))
        if err := t.Stop(); err != nil {
            logrus.Errorf("Stopping logger: %v", err)
        }
    }()
}
```
When untilTime is in the past:

`time.Until(untilTime)` evaluates to a negative ` time.Duration`.
In Go, `time.Sleep(d)` returns immediately when ` d <= 0`.
The background goroutine immediately invokes `t.Stop()`.
`t.Stop()` closes the `t.Lines` channel concurrently as the event reading loop is starting, prematurely aborting event collection from disk.
Additionally, when `untilTime` is in the future, the spawned goroutine sleeps without selecting on `ctx.Done()`, causing a goroutine leak if the client cancels the context early.

### Steps to reproduce the issue

Steps to reproduce the issue
1. Configure Podman to use file-based event logging by adding to `containers.conf`:

```
[engine]
events_logger = "file"
```

2. Generate container events (e.g., run `podman run --rm alpine true` multiple times).
3. Query historical events with a past `--until` boundary 
```
podman events --stream=false --since 1h --until 1m
```


### Describe the results you received

No events are printed to stdout (or the output is prematurely terminated after reading 0–1 lines) because `t.Stop()` closes the tail channel immediately upon startup.

### Describe the results you expected

Podman should parse the event log and output all recorded events that occurred between `--since` and `--until`.


### podman info output

```yaml
host:
  arch: amd64
  buildahVersion: 1.40.0
  conmon:
    package: conmon-2.1.12-1.fc41.x86_64
    path: /usr/bin/conmon
    version: 'conmon version 2.1.12, commit: '
  distribution:
    distribution: fedora
    version: "41"
  eventsLogger: file
  ociRuntime:
    name: crun
    package: crun-1.20-1.fc41.x86_64
    path: /usr/bin/crun
    version: crun version 1.20
  os: linux
```

### Podman in a container

No

### Privileged Or Rootless

Rootless

### Upstream Latest Release

Yes

### Additional environment details

Occurs on any OS/environment using `events_logger = "file"` (including rootless Linux, macOS remote, and containerized Podman setups).


### Additional information

- Code location: `libpod/events/logfile.go` (around lines 119–130)
- The event filter `generateEventUntilOption` in `libpod/events/filters.go` already filters out events occurring after `untilTime`. Terminating the reader stream should be synchronized with reading through events rather than an uncoordinated background timer killing `tail.Tail`.

## Description
This PR addresses a race condition in the server-side connection teardown for podman-remote exec.

For fast-executing commands, the server sometimes completes the httpCon.Close() before the bufio.ReadWriter finishes flushing to the network. This causes the kernel to send a TCP RST instead of a graceful FIN, which forces the remote client to drop data still sitting in its receive buffer.

Adding an explicit httpBuf.Flush() in hijackWriteErrorAndClose() ensures all output has left the Go buffer before the socket is torn down, preventing the truncated/missing output flake described in #25855.

## Summary

Related to #28868.

The terminated-build prune test sends `SIGKILL` to the process running the build. In remote tests, that process is `podman-remote`, so killing it terminates the client while the server-side build may continue.

As a result, the remote version of this test does not exercise the same scenario as the local test, where `SIGKILL` terminates the actual build process.

## Changes

Skip `podman system prune --build clean up after terminated build` for remote runs using `SkipIfRemote()`.

The existing local coverage is unchanged.

This change is intentionally limited to the test behavior. It does not attempt to fix server-side build cancellation. The related prune race was handled separately in #29279, while remote build cancellation is being worked on in `containers/buildah#7007`.

## What does this PR do?

Replaces the fixed 250ms sleep used to synchronize `TestLockSemaphoreActuallyLocks` with channel-based synchronization.

The test now waits until the goroutine has successfully acquired the semaphore before attempting to acquire the same semaphore from the main test goroutine.

## Why?

The previous test relied on a fixed time delay to assume that the goroutine had acquired the semaphore. This introduces a timing dependency that can be sensitive to scheduling conditions, particularly in slower or loaded CI environments.

The new synchronization waits for the actual semaphore acquisition instead of relying on an arbitrary delay.

The existing one-second lock-holding delay and elapsed-time assertion are unchanged.

title: [Bug] Docker-compatible API endpoint returns plaintext secrets

labels.name: kind/bug
labels.description: Categorizes issue or PR as related to a bug.

body:
### Issue Description

Docker's API guarantees that `GET /secrets/{id}` returns only metadata, never secret content.

The `showsecret` parameter is useful on the Libpod-native endpoint, but on the compat endpoint it breaks the Docker API contract. Tools and proxies that rely on Docker API semantics (e.g., docker-socket-proxy) assume this endpoint is safe to expose because Docker never returns secret data from it.

### Steps to reproduce the issue


1. Start the Podman API service:
   ```bash
   podman system service unix:///tmp/podman.sock --time 120 &
   ```
2. Create a secret:
   ```bash
   echo -n "my-password" | podman secret create test-secret -
   ```
3. Inspect via compat endpoint with `showsecret`:
   ```bash
   curl -s --unix-socket /tmp/podman.sock "http://d/secrets/test-secret?showsecret=true"
   ```

### Describe the results you received

```json
{"ID":"...","SecretData":"my-password","Spec":{"Name":"test-secret",...}}
```
The compat endpoint should ignore the `showsecret` parameter and return only metadata (matching Docker behavior):

```json
{"ID":"...","Spec":{"Name":"test-secret",...}}
```

The `showsecret` parameter should continue to work on the Libpod-native endpoint (`/libpod/secrets/{name}`), where Docker API semantics are not expected.

ed

### Describe the results you expected

Not seeing the secrets in plaintext

### podman info output

```yaml
Reproduced on:
- Podman 4.9.3 (Ubuntu 24.04)
- Podman 5.8.6
- Podman 6.1.0
```

### Podman in a container

No

### Privileged Or Rootless

Privileged

### Upstream Latest Release

Yes

### Additional environment details

Additional environment details

### Additional information

The fix should be either in `pkg/api/handlers/compat/secrets.go`, the compat handler should ignore the `showsecret` query parameter:

```go
// compat handler: do not honor showsecret (matches Docker API behavior)
opts.ShowSecret = false
```

or, just log somewhere in the docs that the secrets will be visible as plain text.

title: cmd/rootlessport: handle dual stack sockets right
body:
<!-- Thanks for sending a pull request! -->
With podman 6 we switch the main libpod port bind logic used as rootful
over to bind dual stack sockets correctly and no longer default the host
ip to 0.0.0.0.

So -p 8080:8080 should create one dual stack socket that binds all
addresses. While -p 0.0.0.0:8080:8080 -p [::]:8080:8080 should create
two sockets binding v4 and v6 respectively.

Because the go std lib always defaults to dual stack the second case
currently fails with EADDRINUSE which is wrong, so fix that to pass the
right protocol.

This is also how pasta works already so this makes everything consistent
now.


---

cmd/rootlessport: remove wsl workaround

Having a special wsl work around in the code always felt wrong to me.
This does nothing to fix the pasta or rootful port binding behavior.

To actually fix this for all we can set the new podman 6
default_host_ips containers.conf option in the WSL machine-os image by
default:

[network]
default_host_ips = ["0.0.0.0", "::"]

That should make all code paths bind two sockets which WSL needs as it
is unable to recognize a dual stack ipv6 socket for ipv4 as well.

ref https://github.com/podman-container-tools/podman/issues/29377

---

docs: document hostIP for --publish better

Document the default_host_ips option here to make it more visible. And
clarify the default v4/v6 bind behavior.

title: docs: clarify that --ulimit size limits are in bytes

labels.name: documentation
labels.description: Issue or fix is in project documentation

body:
Fixes: #25236

`--ulimit` values are passed through unchanged: `units.ParseUlimit()` is a plain
`strconv.ParseInt` (no scaling, no suffixes), the result lands in
`specs.POSIXRlimit`, and the runtime applies it via `setrlimit(2)` — where size
limits are byte-valued. So `--ulimit memlock=4096` correctly sets 4096 bytes.

The confusion comes from the display side: the `ulimit` shell builtin rescales
several resources when printing (kbytes for `-d`, `-l`, `-m`, `-s`; 512-byte
blocks for `-c`, `-f`), so 4096 bytes prints as `4`. `msgqueue` is also
byte-valued and prints raw, which shows the same pipeline with a different
display divisor.

As discussed in the issue, changing the units would silently shift every
existing memlock/stack/core/fsize/rss configuration by 1024x and break parity
with the Docker CLI, `containers.conf` `default_ulimits`, Quadlet `Ulimit=`, and
the kube ulimit annotation. So this is docs-only — **no behavior change.**

- `options/ulimit.md` (run, create, update, `podman-container.unit.5`): states
  the units are those of `setrlimit(2)`, adds a per-type unit table, a worked
  `memlock=4194304` -> `ulimit -l` = 4096 example, and notes that unit suffixes
  are not accepted.
- `options/ulimit.image.md` (build, farm build): short note that size limits are
  bytes, with a cross-reference to `podman-run(1)`.

Verified with `make docs` and by rendering the generated man pages; also ran
`hack/man-page-checker` and `hack/markdown-preprocess.t`.

Follow-up (happy to do separately if wanted): the parse error for
`--ulimit memlock=4096kb` currently surfaces only `strconv.ParseInt: parsing
"4096kb": invalid syntax`, which says nothing about units. Mentioning bytes
there would catch the first-time guess at the moment it happens.

title: kube: share memory backed emptyDir between containers in a pod
body:
An emptyDir with `medium: Memory` was turned into a per-container tmpfs mount, so every container in the pod got its own empty filesystem. Anything an init container wrote was gone by the time the regular container looked at it, even though the mount did show up as tmpfs. Kubernetes says an emptyDir is shared by all containers in the pod.

Plain emptyDirs already behave correctly because they become anonymous named volumes, which the whole pod shares. This makes the memory backed case take the same path, with `volume-opt=type=tmpfs` so it stays on tmpfs. The local volume driver already understands that option, and it fills in the device from the type. `sizeLimit` was being dropped on the floor, it now goes through as the tmpfs `size` option.

This is smaller than what the reporter suggested in the issue (a pod scoped volume kept mounted by the infra container). Reusing the existing named volume path looks like it is enough, but I would rather be told if I am missing a reason it is not.

Testing: added an e2e case where two containers share one memory emptyDir, one writes and the other reads it back, and it also checks the mount is still tmpfs. Extended the existing unit test for the sizeLimit plumbing. I could not run the e2e suite locally since I do not have a Linux podman runtime here, so that part is only compiled and vetted and CI will be the first real run. Unit tests, `go vet ./test/e2e/` and `golangci-lint` (2.12.2, the version pinned in the Makefile) are clean.

Fixes: #29555

title: Performance: Upgrade `filepath.Walk` to `filepath.WalkDir` to avoid expensive stat calls
body:
There are a couple of lingering usages of `filepath.Walk` in the codebase. 

`filepath.Walk` is known to be inefficient because it makes an expensive `os.Stat` system call on every single file and directory it encounters. Since Go 1.16, `filepath.WalkDir` has been available, which uses `os.ReadDir` under the hood to bypass these expensive system calls entirely.

Currently, `filepath.Walk` is still being used in:
1. `pkg/api/handlers/libpod/quadlets.go`
2. `pkg/api/handlers/compat/images_build.go`

These instances should be modernized to use `filepath.WalkDir` instead. This is a well-known Go performance best practice, and it is especially beneficial during operations that scan directories (like image builds or quadlet processing) on file systems with many files.

I would be happy to submit a quick Pull Request to clean these two instances up if maintainers agree!

title: podman kube play: emptyDir medium: Memory is not shared between init and regular containers

labels.name: kind/bug
labels.description: Categorizes issue or PR as related to a bug.

labels.name: triaged
labels.description: Issue has been triaged

body:
### Issue Description

When using `podman kube play` with a Kubernetes `emptyDir` volume configured as `medium: Memory`, the volume is mounted as tmpfs, but data written by an init container is not visible to the regular container in the same pod.

The expected Kubernetes behavior is that the `emptyDir` volume is shared by all containers in the pod and survives the termination of the init container.

With Podman 6.1.0-rc1, the `/run/secret` mount is correctly reported as tmpfs, but the data written by the init container is missing when read by the regular container.

A local patch that models the memory-backed emptyDir as a pod-scoped tmpfs volume kept mounted by the infra container fixes the issue.

### Steps to reproduce the issue

1. Use Ubuntu 24.04 with rootless Podman 6.1.0-rc1.
2. Run `./setup-6.1.0.sh` to install the unpatched Podman packages.
3. Run `./test.sh`.
4. The test creates an isolated Podman storage, pulls `busybox:latest`, and runs `podman kube play tmpfs-test.yaml`.
5. The init container writes `Secret-Data-123` to `/run/secret`.
6. The regular container reads `/run/secret` and reports the filesystem type and contents.
7. Observe that `/run/secret` is mounted as `tmpfs`, but the data written by the init container is missing.
8. The test reports:
   `DATA: MISSING`
   `[FAIL] init data NOT shared (DATA=MISSING) — the tmpfs patch is missing`


### Describe the results you received

The test fails because the emptyDir tmpfs is not shared correctly between the init container and the regular container.
The observed output is:
DATA: MISSING
FSLINE: tmpfs                tmpfs       11243020         0  11243020   0% /run/secret

[FAIL] init data NOT shared (DATA=MISSING) — the tmpfs patch is missing

### Describe the results you expected

The init container writes `Secret-Data-123` to `/run/secret`, and the regular container should be able to read the same data from the same `emptyDir` volume.

The volume should remain available for the lifetime of the pod, and `/run/secret` should be backed by tmpfs with the configured 64 MiB `sizeLimit`.

### podman info output

```yaml
host:
  arch: amd64
  buildahVersion: 1.45.0
  cdiSpecDirs:
  - /etc/cdi
  - /var/run/cdi
  cgroupControllers:
  - cpu
  - memory
  - pids
  cgroupManager: systemd
  cgroupVersion: v2

title: docs(tutorials): add complete uninstall and cleanup guide
body:
## What does this PR do?

Adds a comprehensive tutorial guide (`docs/tutorials/uninstall.md`) explaining how to completely reset, purge, and uninstall Podman, its virtual machines, container storage, networks, and configuration files across Linux, macOS, and Windows. Also updates `docs/tutorials/README.md` to link the new guide.

## Why?

Users seeking a clean re-installation, version downgrade/upgrade, or complete software removal previously lacked documented commands and paths for residual files and directories.

Fixes #18034

## Testing

Verified rendered markdown formatting, code block syntax, and internal documentation links.

title: docs: update ROADMAP.md for 2026 milestones
body:
## What does this PR do?

Updates `ROADMAP.md` to:
- Mark completed milestones in 2025 Q3 (Podman 5.6 release and Podman 6 HLD).
- Add the 2026 Q1/Q2 roadmap section (Podman 5.7, 5.8, Podman 6.0 planning, Quadlet/machine enhancements).
- Link to the public GitHub Milestones page and issue tracker for live feature tracking.
- Fix minor typographical errors (`importantance` -> `importance`, `RESTFUl` -> `RESTful`).

## Why?

The roadmap had not been updated past 2025 Q3 and left older release milestones unchecked.

Fixes #28288

## Testing

Verified rendered markdown formatting and file links.

body:
### What does this PR do?
Adds `hack/ci/ci_reporter.py` and its test suite `hack/ci/ci_reporter_test.py` to format failure analysis and flake reports into GitHub Actions Step Summaries, deduplicated GitHub Issues, and PR triage comments.

### Why?
Implements **Phase 3: Mitigation & Reporting** of **Issue #29265**.

### How?
- **GitHub Step Summaries**: Generates formatted markdown tables for `$GITHUB_STEP_SUMMARY` with flake alert banners, metric overviews, and collapsible individual failure logs.
- **Deduplicated Issue Tracking**: Computes deterministic SHA-256 fingerprints (`<!-- ci-flake-fingerprint: <hash> -->`) from job names and categories to update existing open flake issues rather than creating duplicate issue spam.
- **PR Comment Triage**: Generates concise, factual triage comments adhering strictly to `LLM_POLICY.md`.
- **Safety Controls**: Includes `--dry-run` flag, max issues batch limit (`--max-issues`), and rate limiting.
- **Testing**: 20 unit tests with mocked GitHub REST API interactions; registered in `make .check-self-tests`.

title: ci: add agentic CI failure analyzer
body:
### What does this PR do?
Adds `hack/ci/ci_agentic_analyzer.py` and its unit test suite `hack/ci/ci_agentic_analyzer_test.py` to provide optional LLM-assisted root cause analysis for CI failures that deterministic pattern matching cannot fully explain.

### Why?
Implements **Phase 2: Agentic Analysis Engine** of **Issue #29265**.

### How?
- **Zero Third-Party Dependencies**: Connects to OpenAI-compatible LLM endpoints using Python stdlib (`urllib.request`, `json`, `dataclasses`). No external SDKs required.
- **Security & LLM Policy Compliance**:
  - Treats all CI logs as untrusted data with strict bounds checking (max context caps).
  - All credentials/tokens are redacted prior to analysis.
  - Enforces structured JSON output schema validation (`refined_category`, `root_cause`, `is_flake_assessment`, `suggested_action`).
  - Graceful fallback: when no `CI_LLM_API_KEY` is provided, the tool automatically retains the deterministic classification without error.
  - Supports `--dry-run` to inspect prompts without invoking external APIs.
- **Testing**: 31 unit tests with mocked LLM responses (zero external API calls during testing); registered in `make .check-self-tests`.

title: ci: add CI flake detector
body:
### What does this PR do?
Adds `hack/ci/ci_flake_detector.py` and its unit tests `hack/ci/ci_flake_detector_test.py` to analyze cross-run CI failure history and distinguish intermittent test flakes from deterministic bugs.

### Why?
Directly implements **Phase 4: Flake Detection** of **Issue #29265**. A single test failure may be a genuine bug, but intermittent failures across different commits with identical symptoms indicate environmental or timing-dependent flakiness.

### How?
- **Multi-Signal Flake Model**: Computes a weighted flake score (0.0 to 1.0) combining:
  1. *Commit Diversity (30%)*: Same failure across $\ge 5$ distinct commits indicates flakiness.
  2. *Category Correlation (25%)*: Environmental categories (network, infra, timeout) push score up; pure test assertions push score down.
  3. *Temporal Spread (20%)*: Failures spanning multiple days indicate persistent background flakes.
  4. *Failure Rate (15%)*: Failure frequency relative to total job executions.
  5. *Retry Signal (10%)*: Failures occurring on retry attempts (`run_attempt > 1`).
- **Structured Flake Reports**: Outputs per-job summaries, signal breakdowns, failure counts, and recent failure samples.
- **Testing**: 34 unit tests covering flaky scenarios, deterministic bugs, retries, and category weighting; registered in `make .check-self-tests`.

title: ci: add deterministic failure classifier
body:
### What does this PR do?
Adds `hack/ci/ci_failure_classifier.py` and unit tests `hack/ci/ci_failure_classifier_test.py` to categorize normalized CI failures into structured, actionable categories before introducing AI/LLM layers.

### Why?
Supports **Issue #29265** (*"LFX Mentorship Program: Agentic CI Flake Categorization and Analysis"* - Phase 3: Failure Classification).

Before applying LLMs, deterministic pattern matching reliably and reproducibly classifies the vast majority of well-understood CI failures (panics, timeouts, OOM, infra issues, network errors, test assertions).

### How?
- **14 Priority Rules across 12 Categories**:
  - `panic` (priority 100), `timeout` (90), `resource_exhaustion` (85), `infrastructure_failure` (80), `network_error` (70), `image_pull_failure` (65), `container_runtime_error` (60), `build_failure` (55), `dependency_failure` (50), `permission_error` (45), `test_assertion_failure` (40), `unknown` (0).
- **Priority-Based Conflict Resolution**: Specific and fatal errors (panics, timeouts) take precedence over general test assertion failures.
- **Evidence Extraction**: Records exact matched text and confidence score for transparency.
- **Testing**: 34 unit tests covering every category with realistic log fixtures; registered in `make .check-self-tests`.

title: ci: add GitHub Actions log retriever and normalizer
body:
### What does this PR do?
Adds `hack/ci/ci_log_retriever.py` and its test suite `hack/ci/ci_log_retriever_test.py` to download raw job logs from the GitHub Actions API, sanitize and normalize log noise, and extract bounded failure context into structured `FailureRecord` objects.

### Why?
Directly supports **Issue #29265** (*"LFX Mentorship Program: Agentic CI Flake Categorization and Analysis"* - Phase 2: Log Retrieval & Normalization).

While PR #29544 retrieves CI run and job metadata, raw CI logs contain thousands of lines of ANSI escape sequences, GitHub Actions timestamp headers, workflow grouping tags, and potential credentials. This PR provides a clean normalization pipeline to isolate the exact failure sections (Ginkgo test failures, BATS failures, or Go panics) for downstream analysis.

### How?
- **Standard Library Only**: Uses Python stdlib (`urllib.request`, `json`, `dataclasses`, `re`, `zipfile`) — zero third-party dependencies.
- **5-Stage Normalization Pipeline**:
  1. Strip ANSI escape sequences.
  2. Remove GitHub Actions ISO timestamp line prefixes.
  3. Remove GitHub Actions group command markup (`##[group]`, `##[endgroup]`).
  4. Strip logformatter `[+NNNs]` timestamps.
  5. Redact secrets, auth tokens (`ghp_`, bearer headers), and embedded URL credentials while preserving legitimate 40-char git SHAs and image digests.
- **Failure Extraction**: Extracts bounded context (5 lines before, 30 lines after) around failure markers (`[FAIL]`, `not ok N`, `panic:`).
- **Testing**: Added 36 unit tests in `hack/ci/ci_log_retriever_test.py` with mock logs and zip archives; registered in `make .check-self-tests`.

### Usage Examples
```bash
# Retrieve and normalize logs for a single run
./hack/ci/ci_log_retriever.py --run-id 31813098642

# Pipe from ci_run_collector for batch extraction
./hack/ci/ci_run_collector.py --branch main --status failure --limit 5 --json | \
    ./hack/ci/ci_log_retriever.py --stdin

title: ci: add GitHub Actions CI run data collector
body:
### What does this PR do?
Adds `hack/ci/ci_run_collector.py` and its unit test suite `hack/ci/ci_run_collector_test.py` to retrieve and structure workflow run, job, and step data from the GitHub Actions REST API.

### Why?
Directly supports **Issue #29265** (*"LFX Mentorship Program: Agentic CI Flake Categorization and Analysis"* - Phase 1: Data Ingestion Pipeline).

Currently, CI failure summaries in Podman (`github_log_summary.py`) only parse locally formatted HTML logs for single runs. To analyze recurring failures, track intermittent flakes across commits, or categorize failures, a foundational tool is needed to retrieve and structure cross-run CI data from the GitHub API.

### How?
- **Standard Library Only**: Uses Python standard library (`urllib.request`, `json`, `dataclasses`, `argparse`) — zero third-party dependencies.
- **Resilience**: Implements exponential backoff on 5xx/network errors, pagination handling, and explicit GitHub rate-limit detection (`X-RateLimit-Reset`).
- **CLI & Module**: Can be run from the command line (with `--branch`, `--status`, `--limit`, `--run-id`, `--json`) or imported as a module.
- **Testing**: Added 21 unit tests in `hack/ci/ci_run_collector_test.py` with mocked API responses (no network calls required during testing) and registered in `make .check-self-tests`.

### Usage Examples
```bash
# List recent failed runs on main branch
./hack/ci/ci_run_collector.py --branch main --status failure --limit 10

# Inspect a specific run ID
./hack/ci/ci_run_collector.py --run-id 31813098642

# Output structured JSON for piping
./hack/ci/ci_run_collector.py --branch main --status failure --json

title: Expose conmon log rotation options through the REST API

labels.name: kind/feature
labels.description: Categorizes issue or PR as related to a new feature.

body:
### Description

As of conmon 2.2.0, conmon supports log rotation via `--log-rotate` and `--log-max-files`. 
However, Podman does not currently expose these options through its rest api. This means that users managing containers through the rest api cannot configure conmon's log rotation settings directly.

Podman's rest api should be updated to support these arguments.

### Work-around

It is possible to work around this by overriding `conmon_path` via a `container.conf.d` drop-in and using a wrapper that injects the arguments.

title: farm: add --quiet/-q flag to podman farm list
body:
The command feature 'farm' is really helpful when it comes to building multi-architecture container images, with a build out on various different CPU architecture machines (e.g. amd64, arm64 etc.). With this we essentially produce a multi-architecture image useable on many different kinds of machines. Once those farms are built, we can list them out (ls) in a human readable format.

Essentially, when we do a 'podman farm list', it will print out every field (e.g. name, connections, default etc.). What --quiet & -q flags does is it cuts the noise by ONLY printing the names of the farms, rather than all the other farms list metadata.

Benefits of having this feature in the future is for automation and scripts to just pull the farm names from the list. This is mostly important for the CI pipelines to loop over.

title: hack/ci: fix log summary for non-int ginkgo suites
body:
#### Checklist

Ensure you have completed the following checklist for your pull request to be reviewed:

- [x] I have read and understood our contributing guidelines and will not have more than two open PRs as a new contributor.
- [x] PR description, commit message, and GitHub comments are human-written, per LLM Policy
- [x] Certify you wrote the patch or otherwise have the right to pass it on as an open-source patch by signing all commits. (`git commit -s`).
- [ ] Referenced issues using `Fixes: #00000` in commit message (if applicable)
- [x] Tests have been added/updated (or no tests are needed)
- [x] Documentation has been updated (or no documentation changes are needed)
- [ ] All commits pass `make validatepr` (format/lint checks)
- [x] Release note entered in the section below (or `None` if no user-facing changes)

`github_log_summary.py` decided whether a log was ginkgo or bats by looking at the
file name — `if 'int-' in file_path`. `logformatter` decides from the log contents
instead, so the two disagree for any ginkgo suite whose `TEST_NAME` does not begin
with `int`.

The bindings suite is one of those. It is ginkgo, it runs in the `small-tests`
matrix, and `run_bindings` pipes it through `logformatter`. Feeding one and the same
ginkgo log through the summary under two names:

| file name | summary output |
|---|---|
| `int-local-root-fedora-current.log.html` | full failure block — test name, source location, timeline |
| `bindings-root-fedora-current.log.html` | `1 Failed` |

So when bindings fails, the "Output failure log as GITHUB_STEP_SUMMARY" step prints a
bare count and nothing else, at the one moment the summary is meant to be useful.

Detect the format from the content instead. The `log-failed` class is only emitted on
the ginkgo path; the logrus handler emits log *levels*, so it can never produce
`failed`.

Two smaller things in the same file:

- The script only summarized `sys.argv[1]`, while the workflow passes a glob. Each job
  writes one html file today, so nothing is lost in practice, but any further file was
  silently dropped. It now walks every argument.
- The entry point is guarded on `__main__`, which is what makes the script importable
  and therefore testable.

Added `hack/ci/github_log_summary.t`, the first test for this script, run from
`.check-self-tests` alongside `logformatter.t`. It covers ginkgo detection for both
`int-` and non-`int-` names, bats logs, and a ginkgo log with no failures. Reverting
only the detection line fails exactly one of the four, so it does discriminate.

title: machine/wsl: unregister shared net-usermode dist on machine rm
body:
Fixes #29480

The `podman-net-usermode` WSL distribution is shared across all
machines using `--user-mode-networking`, but `podman machine rm`
never unregistered it — only the machine's own WSL distro was
removed, leaving `podman-net-usermode` behind indefinitely.

This adds a check in `WSLStubber.Remove()`: if the removed machine
had user-mode networking enabled, it now looks at the other
configured machines and only unregisters `podman-net-usermode` if
none of them still need it.

Tested manually on Windows:
- single machine with `--user-mode-networking`: `podman machine rm`
  now also removes `podman-net-usermode` from `wsl --list`
- two machines both using `--user-mode-networking`: removing one
  leaves `podman-net-usermode` intact for the other

title: libpod: report locks that DeallocateAllLocks failed to remove
body:
`DeallocateAllLocks()` declares `lastErr` and returns it, but never assigns to it. When `os.Remove()` fails on a lock file, the function logs a line and carries on, so it always returns `nil` and the caller is told every lock was freed.

The log line is not helpful either: `"Deallocating lock %s"` is formatted with the path only. It never mentions that anything failed and drops `err`, so the reason — `EACCES`, `EROFS`, `EBUSY`, `ENOTEMPTY` — is lost.

The user-visible effect is on `podman system renumber`, which calls `FreeAllLocks()` before it reassigns lock IDs (`libpod/runtime_renumber.go`). With the file lock backend, a renumber that could not clear the old lock directory can still report success and go on to allocate new locks. The file backend is the default on FreeBSD, and it is selected on Linux by `lock_type = "file"` in `containers.conf`.

The unused `lastErr` dates back to commit `827ac0859f96` (`lock: new lock type "file"`), which added the backend.

Keep the newest failure in `lastErr` and return it, wrapped with the path so the caller can identify which lock is stuck, and log any failure it supersedes. This follows the same `lastErr` pattern used elsewhere in libpod, for example in `ExecHTTPStartAndAttach()` in `libpod/container_exec.go`. Removal still continues over the remaining locks, and a lock file that is already gone is still skipped, so successful deallocation is unchanged.

The test makes one entry of the lock directory impossible to remove and checks that `DeallocateAllLocks()` returns an error naming it, and that the other locks are freed regardless. A non-empty directory is used to provoke the failure because `os.Remove()` rejects it with `ENOTEMPTY` rather than a permission error, which keeps the test working in both root and rootless test environments.

title: hack/ci: pass --remote to bud tests
body:
The `bud remote` job runs the same local binary as `bud local`. Both jobs from run 31847250452 on main print the identical bats invocation:

```
sudo env TMPDIR=/var/tmp PODMAN_BINARY=/var/tmp/podman-container-tools/podman/bin/podman PODMAN_SERVER_LOG= REMOTE= ...
```

`bin/podman`, not `podman-remote`, and `REMOTE=` empty, in the job named remote.

The remote path in `run-buildah-bud-tests` is gated on `PODBIN_NAME` (line 78), which Cirrus used to set per matrix task. The migration replaced that with a `mode:` matrix key, but `run_bud()` never reads `$MODE` - `run_int`, `run_sys`, `run_machine` and `run_upgrade` all do. `grep -rn PODBIN_NAME` outside vendor finds it only inside `run-buildah-bud-tests` itself and in the treadmill script's Cirrus text.

So `apply-podman-deltas` has 30 `skip_if_remote` and 4 `skip_if_rootless_remote` entries that are currently no-ops, and podman-remote build coverage has been off since the migration.

`--remote` is already an option on the script and sets `PODBIN_NAME=remote` before that gate, so this is one branch in `run_bud`.

Worth saying plainly: this restores coverage rather than being a no-op, so the remote leg may go red on things that have been hidden. Most of the historically broken ones should already be covered by those deltas, but if new failures show up I am happy to iterate on them here or in a follow-up.

title: hack/ci: do not swallow apiv2 failures
body:
The apiv2 bash suite has not gated CI since 66c6da6e84. `run_apiv2` puts both make targets inside one `sh -c "( ... )"` with no `set -e`, so only the last command decides the exit status and `make localapiv2-bash` is discarded. `set -eo pipefail` at the top of runner.sh is the outer bash and does not reach into that inner `sh`.

It is failing right now on main. Run 31847250452, job `apiv2 rootless fedora-current`, conclusion success, log line 3089:

```
make: *** [Makefile:762: localapiv2-bash] Error 17
```

Same thing in the three earlier green main runs I checked (31687097967, 31540756565, 31514570842), each with plan `1..2191` and `Error 17`.

I used an accumulator rather than `set -e` so the python half still runs when the bash half fails - otherwise we would lose that half of the report on every failure. Checked the shapes on bash 5.2: the current one exits 0 when the first target fails, this one exits 1 and still runs both.

I have not looked into the 17 failures themselves yet, they look like three clusters in 26-containersWait and 27-containersEvents. Happy to open a separate issue for those once this gates again.

title: Performance: Replace `strings.ToLower() ==` with `strings.EqualFold()` to prevent unnecessary allocations
body:
<!--
Thank you for reporting an issue.

This issue tracker is for bugs and issues found within Podman.
Please fill in as much of the template below as you're able.
-->

### Describe the issue

In a few places across the codebase, there are case-insensitive string comparisons being performed using `strings.ToLower(x) == "..."`.

For example:
```go
if strings.ToLower(splitRestart[0]) == "never" {
```
This pattern allocates a brand new, fully lowercased string on the heap solely for the purpose of the comparison. In hot paths like CLI argument parsing or configuration evaluation, this causes unnecessary garbage collection and memory overhead.


### Expected Behavior
These checks should be replaced with strings.EqualFold(a, b), which performs the case-insensitive comparison directly in-place without making any heap allocations.

```go
if strings.EqualFold(splitRestart[0], "never") {
```

This is a standard Go performance best practice. I would be happy to submit a quick Pull Request to clean these up if maintainers agree!

title: test/system: fix healthcheck since race
body:
I filed #29353 after this test came up as the most frequent failure in the rerun history I have been going through, and the diagnosis came out of the journal artifacts of two failed jobs: the unhealthy event fires 19ms and 60ms before the `--since` timestamp the test captures, so the events window can never contain it. With a 1s interval the third failure can fire while the "First failure" checks are still running.

81fceb48d already moved this capture before the systemctl checks for the same reason, but it still sits after the trigger. This drops it and reuses the timestamp taken before the touch. I think that is safe because the wait loop only matches the last event, and the assertion table already accepts FailingStreak 3-6.

cc @Luap99

title: pkg/api/handlers/compat: populate IPAM IPRange in network inspect

labels.name: kind/api-change
labels.description: Change to remote API; merits scrutiny

body:
Fixes: #28378

The Docker-compat `network inspect` endpoint left `IPAM.Config[].IPRange`
empty even when the network was created with an IP range — the conversion
had a literal `// TODO add range`. Docker stores the range as a single CIDR
(`netip.Prefix`) while podman stores start/end lease IPs, so this
reconstructs the CIDR by inverting what the create path does
(`netutil.First/LastIPInSubnet`), and leaves `IPRange` unset when the lease
range is not CIDR-aligned (no single Docker CIDR exists — safe degradation).

title: api/auth: fix localhost-address matching to prevent userinfo bypass

labels.name: kind/api-change
labels.description: Change to remote API; merits scrutiny

body:
## Summary

Fixes #29506.

The docker-compat `/auth` endpoint (`pkg/api/handlers/compat/auth.go`) decides whether to skip TLS verification ("support for local testing") using plain string-prefix checks:

```go
strings.HasPrefix(authConfig.ServerAddress, "https://localhost/") ||
strings.HasPrefix(authConfig.ServerAddress, "https://localhost:") ||
strings.HasPrefix(authConfig.ServerAddress, "localhost:")
```

This is bypassable with URL userinfo syntax: `https://localhost:password@evil.example` (or the bare form `localhost:password@evil.example`) matches the `"https://localhost:"` / `"localhost:"` prefixes, but the real host is `evil.example`, not `localhost`. Any server address crafted this way gets `skipTLS = true`, disabling TLS verification for a host that isn't actually localhost.

## Fix

Replaced the prefix checks with `isLocalhostServerAddress()`, which parses the address with `net/url` (adding a `https://` scheme first if the address is a bare `host[:port]`) and checks only `u.Hostname()` against `"localhost"` (case-insensitive), never the userinfo section.

## Test plan

- Added `pkg/api/handlers/compat/auth_test.go` with 18 cases covering: all previously-matched legitimate forms (bare host, `https://` with/without port/path/trailing-slash, case-insensitivity), the userinfo bypass (with and without scheme, with a path), and non-matches (unrelated hosts, subdomain lookalikes, query-string lookalikes, `http://` scheme, loopback IP by address rather than name).
- `go vet` and `go test -c` pass on the changed package.
- Cross-compiled `cmd/podman` for Linux (`CGO_ENABLED=0 GOOS=linux go build`) to confirm the change builds cleanly in the real target environment.

title: domain/filters: accept "dead"/"restarting" as status filter values
body:
## Summary

Fixes #28904.

The libpod and Docker-compat `containers/json` API docs advertise
`status=(created, restarting, running, removing, paused, exited, dead)`
as valid values for the `status` list filter, but Podman has no
`define.ContainerStatus` corresponding to Docker's `dead` or
`restarting` states. As a result, `GenerateContainerFilterFuncs` and
`GenerateExternalContainerFilterFuncs` rejected these two values
outright with `unknown container state: ...: invalid argument`,
surfaced by the API as a 500.

This PR accepts `dead` and `restarting` as valid filter values without
erroring, matching the documented API contract, while leaving the
actual state-matching logic untouched: since no container ever reports
`dead` or `restarting`, the filter simply matches zero containers for
those values instead of failing the request. Other invalid values are
still rejected as before.

## Test plan

- Added `pkg/domain/filters/containers_test.go` covering: `dead`/`restarting` no longer error, known-good values (`created`, `running`, `paused`, `exited`, `stopped`) still work, and genuinely unknown values (`not-a-real-status`) are still rejected.
- `go vet ./pkg/domain/filters/...` and `go test -c ./pkg/domain/filters/...` pass.
- Cross-compiled `cmd/podman` for Linux to confirm the change builds cleanly in the real target environment.
