### [`v1.10.0`](https://redirect.github.com/sirupsen/logrus/releases/tag/v1.10.0)

[Compare Source](https://redirect.github.com/sirupsen/logrus/compare/v1.9.4...v1.10.0)

### Logrus v1.10.0

This release focuses on substantial performance improvements, concurrency correctness, and better interoperability with modern Go logging APIs.

#### 🚀 Performance

Major improvements across `TextFormatter`, entry handling, and common logger paths:

- \~17% lower geomean runtime across the benchmark suite
- \~27% higher geomean formatter throughput
- Common enabled logging paths are \~30–44% faster
- `WithError` is \~40% faster
- Chained fields are \~46% faster
- `TextFormatter` paths are up to \~40% faster
- Allocation counts are reduced by \~25–74% across measured `TextFormatter` cases, with the largest reductions in colored output

The improvements also show up in complete logger paths:

- Logger + `TextFormatter` is \~31% faster, with \~24% fewer allocations
- Logger + `JSONFormatter` is \~21% faster, with \~10% fewer allocations

`JSONFormatter` itself remains largely unchanged in runtime performance, with small allocation reductions.

#### 🔄 `log/slog` interoperability

v1.10 adds bidirectional interoperability between Logrus and Go's `log/slog`:

- A Logrus `slog` hook can forward existing Logrus entries to an `slog` logger.
- `hooks/slog.NewHandler` implements `slog.Handler`, allowing `log/slog` records to use an existing Logrus logger and its hooks, formatter, and output.
- The handler preserves levels, fields, groups, context, record timestamps, and optionally caller information.
- Caller reporting is configured per handler, without requiring Logrus's logger-wide `ReportCaller` option.
- Custom `slog` levels can be mapped to Logrus levels.
- The hook and handler can be combined, providing a practical path for incrementally migrating from Logrus to `log/slog` without requiring an all-at-once transition.

This allows applications to migrate their logging API and logging backend independently: existing Logrus call sites can start using an `slog` backend, while new `slog` code can continue using an established Logrus setup.

#### 🔒 Concurrency & Correctness

- Fix reentrant logging deadlocks, including logging from within `MarshalJSON` or formatter code.
- Fix generic `Log`, `Logf`, `Logln`, and `LogFn` methods unexpectedly panicking when called with `PanicLevel`, contrary to their documented behavior.
- Eliminate race conditions in entry and formatter paths.
- Improve locking boundaries around formatters and hooks.

#### ➕ Added

- `TextFormatter` now automatically enables colors on Windows terminals with ANSI support, matching behavior on other platforms.
- `Entry.Caller` can now be set explicitly and is preserved across derived entries. When caller reporting is enabled, Logrus only detects and populates caller information when none was provided, allowing custom caller detection and wrapper-aware logging without adding additional caller configuration APIs.
- Add minimal, composable logging interfaces for each log level, allowing consumers to depend on narrower interfaces and making logging implementations easier to substitute or adapt.
- Expand CI verification to include TinyGo and every cross-compile target reported by go tool dist list, improving coverage across alternative toolchains and platforms.

#### ⚠️ Behavioral Changes

- Minimum supported Go version is now **1.23**.
- `TextFormatter` now renders `[]byte` as raw/quoted strings instead of numeric slices.
  If you relied on the previous slice-of-ints output, convert explicitly before logging.
- `TextFormatter` now uses dim cyan for debug output and dim white for trace output in colorized TTY output.
- `Entry.HasCaller` is now deprecated in favor of checking `Entry.Caller` directly. A `//go:fix inline` directive was added so existing uses can be updated automatically.
- `MutexWrap`, which was unintentionally exposed as public API, is deprecated. It remains available as an alias for compatibility but should not be used directly.

***

v1.10 is primarily a performance, correctness, and interoperability release with no intentional breaking public API changes.

title: Performance: Hoist regexp.MustCompile out of functions

labels.name: No New Tests
labels.description: Allow PR to proceed without adding regression tests

body:
<!-- Thanks for sending a pull request! -->

Replaces `regexp.MustCompile` with `regexp.Delayed` from `go.podman.io/storage/pkg/regexp` for global regular expressions. This avoids compiling regular expressions during the global init scope, improving startup performance for all commands.
Additionally, where possible (such as in quadlet, mac-helper, and ps), the regex engine was stripped entirely and replaced with faster `strings` and loop checks to avoid any regex overhead altogether. 
Tests are kept using `regexp.MustCompile` where applicable.

title: Performance: Move regexp.MustCompile out of function bodies to package level
body:
### Description

In Go, `regexp.MustCompile` is an expensive operation that parses and compiles a regular expression. When placed inside a function body, the regex is recompiled every single time the function is called, which creates unnecessary CPU and memory overhead.

There are currently several places in the codebase where `regexp.MustCompile` is used inside functions instead of being declared as a package-level global variable. For example, in `libpod/oci_util.go` and `pkg/systemd/quadlet/unitdirs.go`.

I would like to help optimize this by hoisting these `regexp.MustCompile` calls to package-level variables so they are compiled exactly once at startup. 

Would the maintainers be open to a PR addressing this?

title: pkg/trust: parseUids can panic on malformed GPG uid/pub lines
body:
`parseUids` in `pkg/trust/policy.go` reads the colon-delimited GnuPG key
listing and, for each line starting with `uid:` or `pub:`, does:

```go
uid := strings.Split(line, ":")[9]
```

The index `[9]` assumes every `uid`/`pub` record has at least 10
colon-separated fields. GnuPG's `--with-colons` output does not guarantee
that — records can legitimately have fewer fields — so a short line makes
this panic with `index out of range [9] with length N`.

Since this data comes from `gpg` output parsed at runtime, a malformed or
truncated record can crash podman instead of being skipped.

**Fix:** guard the field count and skip records that are too short before
indexing field 9.

**Environment:** any (parsing bug, platform independent).

title: Fix empty detach keys being interpreted as default detach keys

labels.name: kind/api-change
labels.description: Change to remote API; merits scrutiny

body:
Fixes #28193
As mentioned in the issue and the linked PR #28405, the problem was string doesn't hold necessary information to conclude if detached keys were passed as `''` or omitted. So, the obvious fix was to change the `input.DetachKeys` to *string.

If default key is omitted, in `exec.go` we assign `libpodConfig.DetachKeys` to `&config.DefaultDetachKeys`.

title: Inaccurate host matching logic in `pkg/api/handlers/compat/auth.go`
body:
`pkg/api/handlers/compat/auth.go` uses `strings.HasPrefix(authConfig.ServerAddress, "https://localhost:")`.

That could plausibly be bypassed using an `https://localhost:password@other-host.example` syntax; at least for cleanliness, we should parse URLs properly (while allowing for non-URLs?).

But first of all, should the special case exist?

title: Refactor: Remove redundant err.Error() calls in formatting strings
body:
### Description

In Go, when passing an `error` to formatting functions like `fmt.Errorf` or `logrus.Warnf`, explicitly calling `.Error()` is redundant and generally considered an anti-pattern. The formatting verbs (like `%s`, `%v`, `%q`) automatically invoke the `Error()` method on objects that implement the `error` interface.

There are currently many places in the codebase where `err.Error()` is unnecessarily called inside formatting functions. For example:

```go
// Current
logrus.Warnf("could not release port allocation (%d): %s", newPort, err.Error())

// Proposed
logrus.Warnf("could not release port allocation (%d): %v", newPort, err)

title: fix(api): bound how long a client may take to send request headers

labels.name: kind/api-change
labels.description: Change to remote API; merits scrutiny

body:
The API service's http.Server sets only IdleTimeout, which covers the wait between requests on a keep-alive connection. Nothing bounds the read of the request headers themselves, so a client that connects and sends a partial header block - "GET /_ping HTTP/1.1\r\nHost: x\r\n" with no terminating CRLF - is never disconnected.

Each connection held this way pins a file descriptor and a goroutine in the service for as long as it runs, and nothing limits how many of them a client may open; against a server configured exactly as this one is, 100 out of 100 half-open connections were still held after the API idle window had passed. With "podman system service --time=0" they are held for the lifetime of the process, until it runs out of descriptors and stops serving legitimate clients. This is reachable by anyone who can open a connection to the service, which matters most when it is bound to TCP ("podman system service tcp://...") rather than to a unix socket.

Set ReadHeaderTimeout to 30 seconds. ReadTimeout and WriteTimeout stay unset on purpose: they cover the whole request and would break attach, exec, events, logs and image push/pull, which stream for as long as the client wants them to. ReadHeaderTimeout does not have that problem, because net/http clears the read deadline once the headers have been read and again when a handler hijacks the connection. It bounds HTTP/1.x header reads.

Move the http.Server construction into newHTTPServer() so this can be tested without a libpod runtime. The tests cover a connection stalled mid-header (now closed), the same server with no ReadHeaderTimeout (still held - the regression this guards against), and a hijacked connection that streams well after the header timeout has elapsed (unaffected).

title: Architecture: fetch WordPress blog data at build time instead of client-side

labels.name: kind/feature
labels.description: Categorizes issue or PR as related to a new feature.

body:
### Feature request description

BlogArticlesList currently obtains recent Podman blog posts through the useBlogPosts React hook. The hook performs a client-side request to the WordPress REST API from useEffect() after the page has loaded.

This means the homepage and Features page depend on an external API request during runtime to populate content that is otherwise static and can be determined during the Docusaurus build.

Currently the rendering path is:

Page load
  |
React hydration
  |
useEffect()
  |
WordPress API request
  |
setState()
  |
BlogArticlesList renders

For a statically generated site, this introduces an unnecessary runtime dependency for content that could be resolved during the build.

Why this matters

If the WordPress API is unavailable, slow, rate-limited, or unreachable from a user's network, the latest-post section cannot be populated even though the rest of the site is available.

It also means the blog cards are not part of the initial generated HTML and require JavaScript execution and a subsequent network request before becoming available.

### Suggest potential solution

Move the WordPress API request into the Docusaurus build process and expose the resulting blog metadata to the page at build time.

for eg. 

WordPress REST API
        |
Docusaurus build
        |
generated blog metadata
        |
BlogArticlesList

The generated data should contain only the fields currently required by ArticleCard, such as:

post ID
title
author
author URL
date
featured image
post URL
excerpt

The React component can then become a presentational component that receives already-available data rather than managing its own network request and loading state.

Expected outcome

The latest blog posts should be available as part of the generated site without requiring a client-side WordPress API request after page load.

### Have you considered any alternatives?

There are 2 approaches that we can discuss:

1. API response validation + typed boundary

Right now useBlogPosts.ts essentially does:

const jsonData = await rawData.json();
setData(jsonData);

There is no validation that the WordPress response actually conforms to the BlogPost interface.

The TypeScript interface gives the compiler an expected shape, but it does not validate runtime JSON.

That creates a genuine boundary problem:

External API
     |
untrusted JSON
     |
TypeScript assertion/assumption
     |
React components

A stronger architecture would be:

External API
     |
validate/normalize
     |
BlogPost[]
     |
React

We can use a lightweight schema validator or a custom normalization function.

2. Centralize/cachе WordPress API data

BlogArticlesList is used in multiple places. The homepage renders it with:

<BlogArticlesList limit={4} ... />

while the Features page renders it separately with:

<BlogArticlesList
  limit={2}
  ...
/>

Because the hook performs its own fetch() for every mounted instance, the architecture can potentially produce multiple independent requests to the same external service.

We can instead introduce a shared data layer:

                                    
WordPress API -> cache/data layer -> Homepage, Features
                           

rather than:

Homepage → WordPress API
Features → WordPress API

This is especially interesting because the data is external and relatively slow-changing.

Since This is related to architecture, I would like to get views of maintainers on it before moving forward

title: events: fix goroutine leak with until flag in file backend
body:
<!--
Thanks for submitting a pull request!

Please make sure you've read and understood our contributing guidelines.
-->

**- What I did**
Fixed a goroutine and memory leak in the file events backend when using the `--until` flag. 

Previously, `libpod/events/logfile.go` spawned an unmanaged goroutine using `time.Sleep(time.Until(untilTime))` that ignored `context.Context` cancellation. If a client disconnected early (e.g. dropped API connection or `Ctrl+C`), the goroutine was orphaned and continued sleeping in the background.

I replaced the blocking `time.Sleep` with a `time.NewTimer` and a `select` block that listens for `ctx.Done()`. This ensures the goroutine exits immediately if the client cancels the request, properly freeing system resources and preventing an API denial-of-service vector.

**- How I did it**
- Replaced `time.Sleep` with `time.NewTimer`.
- Added a `select` statement listening to `<-ctx.Done()` and `<-timer.C`.

**- How to verify it**
1. Run `podman system service`
2. Fetch events via the API with a far-future until parameter: `curl -v --unix-socket /run/user/1000/podman/podman.sock "http://d/v4.0.0/libpod/events?until=9999h"`
3. Terminate the curl request (`Ctrl+C`).
4. Verify via pprof or logging that the background routine is destroyed and no longer sleeping.

**- Description for the changelog**
```release-note
Fixed a goroutine leak in the event logger that occurred when an event stream using the `--until` flag was prematurely cancelled by the client.

**- Fixes** 
Fixes #29491

title: fix(api): prevent file descriptor leak in quadlet uploads

labels.name: kind/api-change
labels.description: Change to remote API; merits scrutiny

body:
## Problem

`processMultipartQuadlets()` can leak file descriptors when processing multipart
quadlet uploads.

The function currently defers `part.Close()` and `file.Close()` inside the loop
that processes each uploaded file. These deferred calls are only executed when
`processMultipartQuadlets()` returns, so all opened files remain open while the
rest of the multipart request is being processed.

For requests containing a large number of quadlet files, this can exhaust the
available file descriptors and cause the request to fail with `too many open
files`.

## Fix

Move the processing of each multipart part into a separate helper function.
The helper closes both the multipart part and the created file before returning,
so only the current file remains open while processing the request.

This keeps the existing behavior and error handling unchanged while preventing
file descriptors from accumulating across uploaded parts.

## Testing

- Added a regression test covering large multipart uploads with a low file
  descriptor limit.
- Verified the test fails with the old implementation due to `too many open
  files`.
- Verified the test passes with the fix.
- Ran the `pkg/api/handlers/...` test suite.
- Ran `gofumpt`.
- Ran `golangci-lint`.

title: Goroutine leak in event logger when using `--until` with dropped contexts

labels.name: kind/bug
labels.description: Categorizes issue or PR as related to a bug.

body:
### Issue Description

When fetching events with the `--until` flag on a system using the `file` events backend, `libpod/events/logfile.go` spawns an unmanaged, blocking goroutine that ignores `context.Context` cancellation. 

```go
	if len(options.Until) > 0 {
		// ...
		go func() {
			time.Sleep(time.Until(untilTime))
			if err := t.Stop(); err != nil {
				logrus.Errorf("Stopping logger: %v", err)
			}
		}()
	}
```
Because `time.Sleep` is not context-aware, if a client cancels the request (e.g., `Ctrl+C` on the CLI, or a dropped HTTP connection on the REST API), the goroutine is orphaned and continues sleeping in the background.

If running Podman as a service (podman system service), a client that repeatedly polls GET /events?until=<far-future> and drops the connection will cause a silent goroutine leak, stacking up sleeping routines and wasting resources.

### Steps to reproduce the issue



**Steps to reproduce the issue**
```markdown
1. Start the Podman API service (`podman system service`).
2. Send a request to the events endpoint with a far-future until parameter: `curl -v --unix-socket /run/user/1000/podman/podman.sock "http://d/v4.0.0/libpod/events?until=9999h"`
3. Immediately cancel the curl request (press `Ctrl+C`).
4. The background goroutine in `logfile.go` remains asleep, waiting out the 9999h timer even though the context was cancelled.


### Describe the results you received

The goroutine uses an un-interruptible `time.Sleep` which causes a memory/goroutine leak when requests are terminated early by the client.


### Describe the results you expected

The goroutine should use a `timer` and `select` on `ctx.Done()` so it exits immediately when the parent request is cancelled, properly freeing system resources.

title: quadlet: handle missing HOME in rootless configuration lookup
body:
## Summary

This addresses [#29284](https://github.com/podman-container-tools/podman/issues/29284), where rootless Quadlet files can be discovered by
`podman quadlet list` but are not loaded by the systemd user generator in the
reproduced `systemd-homed` setup.

I reproduced the issue on Fedora CoreOS 44 using a disposable user created with
`homectl`. The actual user-generator environment was:

```text
HOME=/
XDG_CONFIG_HOME=
XDG_RUNTIME_DIR=/run/user/60104
```

Rootless Quadlet uses `os.UserConfigDir()` to determine the user's configuration
directory. With `HOME=/` and no `XDG_CONFIG_HOME`, this resolves to `/.config`,
so the user's actual `~/.config/containers/systemd` directory is not searched.

User lookup still returns the correct home directory:

```text
quadtest:x:60104:60104:quadtest:/home/quadtest:/bin/bash
```

The change reuses Podman's existing `GetRootlessConfigHomeDir()` path when the
rootless home environment is unusable. For the reproduced `HOME=/` case, the
helper resolves the rootless user's UID using `rootless.GetRootlessUID()` and
uses the home directory returned by the user database.

Normal Quadlet lookup continues to use `os.UserConfigDir()`, and explicit
`XDG_CONFIG_HOME` behavior remains unchanged.

Fixes: #29284

## Reproduction

I created a disposable `systemd-homed` user and placed `pgsql.container` and
`pgsql.pod` under:

```text
/var/home/quadtest/.config/containers/systemd/
```

Before the fix:

- `podman quadlet list` discovered both files but reported them as `Not loaded`.
- `/usr/libexec/podman/quadlet -dryrun -user` from the user's normal login environment generated both units correctly.
- `systemctl --user daemon-reload` generated neither unit.

The actual environment observed for `podman-user-generator` was:

```text
uid=60104
user=quadtest
home=/
xdg_config_home=
xdg_runtime_dir=/run/user/60104
```

Running Quadlet manually with the same `HOME=/` environment reproduced the
discovery failure, narrowing the issue to rootless config-directory resolution
in the generator environment.

## Testing

Added `TestGetRootlessConfigHomeDirWithRootHome` in the Linux util tests to
cover the `HOME=/` regression.

The relevant package tests pass:

```text
$ go test ./pkg/util ./pkg/systemd/quadlet -count=1
ok      go.podman.io/podman/v6/pkg/util
ok      go.podman.io/podman/v6/pkg/systemd/quadlet
```

`git diff --check` also passes.

During the original reproduction, I also built the patched Quadlet binary and
exercised the systemd user-generator path. After:

```text
systemctl --user daemon-reload
```

the previously missing units were generated:

```text
/run/user/60104/systemd/generator/pgsql.service
/run/user/60104/systemd/generator/pgsql-pod.service
```

`make validatepr` was also attempted, but `golangci-lint` was killed with exit
137 on the 2 GB validation VM, so the full validation did not complete.

## Scope

The change is limited to rootless Quadlet source-directory lookup when the
systemd user generator does not receive a usable home directory.

It does not change:

- normal `HOME` handling
- explicit `XDG_CONFIG_HOME` handling
- rootful Quadlet discovery
- `podman quadlet install`

## Summary

The step summary for failed CI jobs is empty when the failing suite is `bindings`. `github_log_summary.py` selects the Ginkgo or Bats parser from the log filename, treating only `int-` logs as Ginkgo. This PR fixes a bug where `podman machine cp` events would fail to deserialize in the remote API path because the `events.Copy` status was missing from `libpod/events/events.go:StringToStatus()`.

title: Copy event status emitted by podman machine cp is missing from StringToStatus

labels.name: kind/bug
labels.description: Categorizes issue or PR as related to a bug.

body:
### Issue Description

The `events.Copy` status (value: `"copy"`) is defined in `libpod/events/config.go` and is actively emitted during `podman machine cp` operations via `newMachineEvent(events.Copy, ...)` in `cmd/podman/machine/cp.go`. 

However, the authoritative mapping function `StringToStatus` in `libpod/events/events.go` completely lacks a `case` for `"copy"`. 

Because `StringToStatus` enforces the contract that every emitted event status must be deserializable, its omission breaks event processing paths that rely on it. Specifically, in the remote API path (`pkg/domain/entities/events.go:25`), when `ConvertToLibpodEvent` attempts to parse an incoming event with `Action = "copy"`, `StringToStatus("copy")` returns the error `unknown event status "copy"`. This causes `machine cp` events to be silently dropped or generate errors when interacting with Podman over the remote API or via tunneling.


### Steps to reproduce the issue

1. Initiate a `podman machine cp` command (which internally emits an `events.Copy` machine event).
2. Concurrently monitor the event stream via the remote REST API (or any path that triggers `ConvertToLibpodEvent` in `pkg/domain/entities/events.go`).
3. Note that the event conversion fails internally because `StringToStatus("copy")` returns an error, rather than mapping to `events.Copy`.

*(Alternatively, simply inspect `StringToStatus` in `libpod/events/events.go` and observe that `Copy` is missing from the switch statement).*


### Describe the results you received

When the `Action` field of an event is `"copy"`, `StringToStatus` returns an error:
`unknown event status "copy"`

This causes the event to fail conversion and be dropped in the remote client/API path.


### Describe the results you expected

`StringToStatus("copy")` should return the `events.Copy` constant without error, just as it does for all other emitted event statuses (like `Start`, `Stop`, `Init`, `Remove`, etc.), ensuring events can be successfully serialized and deserialized across all API boundaries.

body:
### Issue Description

The command `podman machine stop` shuts down the VM process and kills gvproxy or win-sshproxy. But if the VM is killed using another client (e.g. `wsl --shutdown`), gvproxy and win-sshproxy aren't killed. This becomes problematic when the machine is restarted and the 

### Steps to reproduce the issue

Steps to reproduce the issue with Hyperv:
1. `podman machine init --provider=hyperv --now`
2. `Stop-VM -Name "podman-machine-default"`
3. `podman machine start`

Steps to reproduce the issue with WSL:
1. `podman machine init --now`
2. `wsl --shutdown`
3. `podman machine start`




### Describe the results you received

On HyperV:

Manually killing the gvproxy/win-sshproxy process and stopping/starting the machine solves the problem

### Describe the results you expected

At very least, we should handle the case of a gvproxy/win-sshproxy orphan at machine start. Either by reusing it or killing the existing instance and running a new one. Ideally, we should register a hook to kill gvproxy/win-sshproxy when the VM is killed (if the provider supports a shutdown hook).

title: pkg/specgen: fix volume string splitting for destination drive letter
body:
#### Description

When volume strings contain Windows-style drive letters in both the source and destination paths (e.g. C:\src:C:\dst:ro or C:\src:C:\src), SplitVolumeString in pkg/specgen and pathsFromVolume in pkg/machine/vmconfigs previously only recombined the drive letter scheme for the source path (parts[0] + parts[1]). This left the destination drive letter split across separate array elements, resulting in volume parsing errors or destination path corruption.

This patch updates both functions to check whether the destination path segment also begins with a single-letter Windows drive scheme and recombines parts[1] and parts[2] accordingly.

Fixes #29386

labels.name: kind/bug

body:
### Issue Description

`Secret` is a first-class event type in Podman. When secrets are created or removed (`podman secret create` / `podman secret rm`), secret events are emitted and logged to the Podman event backend with `e.Type = events.Secret`.

However, attempting to filter the event stream by secret name or ID using `podman events --filter secret=<name>` returns an error: `Error: SECRET is an invalid filter`.

Upon checking the codebase:
- `events.Secret` (`"secret"`) is explicitly defined in `libpod/events/config.go`.
- Secret operations record events in `libpod/events.go`.
- `--filter type=secret` works, but filtering by specific secret attributes via `--filter secret=...` fails because `generateEventFilter` in `libpod/events/filters.go` lacks a `case "SECRET":` handler, and shell autocompletion in `cmd/podman/common/completion.go` lacks `"secret="` mapping.


### Steps to reproduce the issue

1. Create a dummy secret:
   $ podman secret create mysecret - <<< "supersecretdata"
2. Try to stream events filtered by secret name:
   $ podman events --filter secret=mysecret
3. Observe the command failure.


### Describe the results you received

Error: SECRET is an invalid filter


### Describe the results you expected

`podman events --filter secret=mysecret` should filter and display events matching `mysecret` by name or ID prefix without throwing an invalid filter error, consistent with `--filter container=...`, `--filter image=...`, `--filter pod=...`, `--filter volume=...`, and `--filter network=...`.

title: Refactor: Replace %v and %s with %w for error wrapping in fmt.Errorf
body:
### Description

Go 1.13 introduced error wrapping, which allows callers to inspect the original error using `errors.Is` and `errors.As`. To wrap an error using `fmt.Errorf`, you must use the `%w` verb.

Currently, across the `podman` codebase, there are many instances where errors are being formatted using `%v` or `%s` instead of `%w`. This converts the error to a simple string and breaks the error chain, making it harder for upstream callers to handle specific error types correctly.

Here are a few specific examples where this currently exists:

1. `pkg/machine/gvproxy.go`:

title: hyperv: add timeout to vsock ready wait
body:
## Problem

When you run `podman machine init` or `podman machine start` on Windows (HyperV), Podman has to wait for the guest VM to say "I'm ready" through a socket connection called hvsock.

The function `HVSockRegistryEntry.ListenSetupWait()` in `pkg/machine/hyperv/vsock/vsock.go` starts a background goroutine (`sockets.ListenAndWaitOnSocket`) that waits for the guest to connect and say it's ready, then just does `return <-errChan`. This blocks with no timeout at all. So if the guest VM is still running but never actually reaches the point where it signals ready (say some service inside the guest hangs), there is simply no way for this wait to end on its own. Nothing above it in the code has a timeout either, so the whole thing can hang forever.

I checked this myself by testing `sockets.ListenAndWaitOnSocket` directly against a real `net.Listener` that never gets connected to, no Hyper-V or actual guest VM involved, and confirmed it never returns.

## Proposed fix

Take the actual waiting part out into its own small function, `waitForReady(errChan, timeout)`, and add a timeout using `time.After`. If the wait goes on longer than `readyTimeout` (5 minutes), it stops waiting and returns a clear error instead of hanging forever.

5 minutes gives plenty of extra time for a normal, healthy boot to finish. I pulled 10 real successful `podman machine init --now` runs from Podman's own Hyper-V CI (run 31508856317), and they cluster tightly between 15.8s and 19.4s, so 5 minutes is generous headroom over that without hanging with no end.

## Testing done so far

I tested `waitForReady` by itself, covering three cases: it works normally, it passes through an error correctly, and it times out correctly. None of these tests need real Hyper-V.

I also added a fourth test that recreates the actual bug using a real `net.Listener` that never connects, and confirms the new timeout makes it return instead of hanging like before.

All of this runs natively on Windows, and both `go vet` and `go test` pass without any issues.

I have not been able to test this against a real Hyper-V guest VM end to end since I don't have that setup. This fix is only for the waiting logic itself, which doesn't depend on any specific platform, but the full `podman machine init` flow on an actual Hyper-V host should still be checked by CI or by a reviewer who has a Windows machine set up for it.

I'd like to open a PR with this fix, wanted to check the direction here first since I can't fully verify the real-VM path myself.

- [x] [Release note](https://github.com/kubernetes/community/blob/master/contributors/guide/release-notes.md) entered in the section below (or `None` if no user-facing changes)

This fixes Windows remote builds with `--secret` when localapi maps the build context to a Linux path for a Podman machine.

`prepareSecrets` previously used `ContextDirectory` to create temporary secret files on the Windows client. After localapi translated that field, it contained the machine-visible Linux path instead of the original Windows path. Windows therefore could not create the temporary secret file.

The change preserves the original client path in `ClientContextDirectory` before replacing `ContextDirectory` with the machine-visible path. `prepareSecrets` uses the client path for local temporary files, while `ContextDirectory` remains the path used by the machine.

Regression tests cover the localapi path mapping and temporary secret-file placement.

Fixes #29223

title: build: add --no-cache-filter flag for per-stage cache control

labels.name: kind/api-change
labels.description: Change to remote API; merits scrutiny

body:
Add the --no-cache-filter flag to podman build and podman farm build. This flag allows users to specify individual build stages for which the build cache should be ignored, rather than disabling cache for all stages with --no-cache.

The flag accepts stage names or indices as a comma-separated list:
  podman build --no-cache-filter stage1,stage2 .

When --no-cache is also specified, an error is returned since the flags are mutually exclusive.

Changes:
- Register --no-cache-filter StringSlice flag in CLI build flags
- Add mutual exclusion validation with --no-cache in ParseBuildOpts
- Add NoCacheFilter field to entities.BuildOptions
- Add nocachefilter query parameter to compat API BuildQuery
- Add nocachefilter serialization in remote API client bindings
- Add swagger documentation for the nocachefilter parameter
- Create option documentation (no-cache-filter.md)
- Add @@option no-cache-filter to podman-build and podman-farm-build
- Add Ginkgo integration test for mutual exclusion validation
- Add BATS system test for mutual exclusion validation

Note: Actual per-stage cache invalidation requires an upstream containers/buildah change to add NoCacheFilter to define.BuildOptions. The Podman-side plumbing is complete and ready for that integration.

Fixes: #29391

<!-- Thanks for sending a pull request! -->

### Summary

This PR adds the `--no-cache-filter` flag to `podman build` and `podman farm build` to allow users to specify targeted build stages that should bypass the build cache, while preserving cached layers for all other stages in a multi-stage build.

Example usage:

```bash
podman build --no-cache-filter stage1,stage2 .
```

---

### Adopted Approach & Rationale

I adopted a two-phase architecture approach to ensure clean separation between Podman's CLI/API surface and Buildah's low-level image executor:

**Phase 1 — Podman CLI & API Plumbing (This PR):**

- Added `--no-cache-filter` as a `StringSlice` flag in `cmd/podman/common/build.go`.
- Enforced mutual exclusion validation in `ParseBuildOpts()` — attempting to pass both `--no-cache` and `--no-cache-filter` together returns exit code 125 with: `Error: cannot specify --no-cache with --no-cache-filter`.
- Threaded `NoCacheFilter []string` through `entities.BuildOptions` across both the local ABI path and the remote REST API path (`pkg/api/handlers/compat/images_build.go` and `pkg/bindings/images/build.go`).
- Added swagger API parameter documentation, man page option template (`docs/source/markdown/options/no-cache-filter.md`), and integration tests.

**Phase 2 — Upstream Buildah Integration (Coordinated follow-up):**

- Upstream `containers/buildah` currently lacks per-stage cache filtering in `define.BuildOptions` and `imagebuildah/executor.go`.
- As a stopgap, `NoCacheFilter` is carried in Podman's own `entities.BuildOptions` and CLI parser wrappers. Once the corresponding Buildah PR adds `NoCacheFilter` to `define.BuildOptions`, the Podman API handler will wire this field directly into Buildah's executor — no further Podman-side changes needed beyond removing the local stopgap field.

---

### Changes

| File | What changed |
|------|-------------|
| `cmd/podman/common/build.go` | Added `NoCacheFilter` field to `BuildFlagsWrapper`, registered `--no-cache-filter` flag, added mutual exclusion check against `--no-cache`, wired through to `entities.BuildOptions` |
| `pkg/domain/entities/types/types.go` | Added `NoCacheFilter []string` to `BuildOptions` struct |
| `pkg/api/handlers/compat/images_build.go` | Added `NoCacheFilter` to `BuildQuery` struct with `schema:"nocachefilter"` tag, added TODO for buildah wiring |
| `pkg/bindings/images/build.go` | Added `nocachefilter` URL parameter serialization in `prepareParams()` |
| `pkg/api/server/register_images.go` | Added swagger documentation for the `nocachefilter` query parameter |
| `docs/source/markdown/options/no-cache-filter.md` | **New file** — option documentation for `--no-cache-filter` |
| `docs/source/markdown/podman-build.1.md.in` | Added `@@option no-cache-filter` |
| `docs/source/markdown/podman-farm-build.1.md.in` | Added `@@option no-cache-filter` |
| `test/e2e/build_test.go` | Added Ginkgo integration test for mutual exclusion validation |
| `test/system/070-build.bats` | Added BATS system test for mutual exclusion validation |

---

### Tests & Verification

The implementation has been verified locally across all levels:

**1. Validation & Linting (`make .validatepr`):**
- Passed `gofumpt` code formatting and `golangci-lint` across all target build environments (linux, windows, darwin).
- Passed pre-commit validation, swagger schema validation, man-page cross-reference checks, and shell script linting.

**2. Unit Testing:**
- `go test -v ./cmd/podman/common ./pkg/domain/entities/...` — all tests pass.

**3. Ginkgo Integration Test (`make localintegration`):**
- Added E2E spec in `test/e2e/build_test.go` testing `--no-cache` and `--no-cache-filter` mutual exclusion.
- Result: `SUCCESS! -- 1 Passed | 0 Failed`.
- The test runs `podman build --no-cache --no-cache-filter stage1` against a real Containerfile and asserts exit code 125 with the expected error message.

**4. Direct CLI Validation:**
- Ran `./bin/podman build --no-cache --no-cache-filter stage1 /dev/null`.
- Output: `Error: cannot specify --no-cache with --no-cache-filter` (exit code 125).

**5. BATS System Test:**
- Added test in `test/system/070-build.bats` asserting exit code 125 and matching the error string for `--no-cache` + `--no-cache-filter` conflict.

---

title: [macOS arm64] v6.0.2 release pkg matches GitHub digest but pkgutil reports invalid signature
body:
### Issue description

The official Podman v6.0.2 macOS arm64 installer matches the size and SHA-256
published by GitHub's release API, but macOS reports an invalid Installer
package signature.

Asset identity:

- release: `v6.0.2`
- asset ID: `485432449`
- file: `podman-installer-macos-arm64.pkg`
- size: `74,802,386` bytes
- SHA-256:
  `5a1d97f98f626cdb82dbd9932cf43102d1e9b6621627085fec2dcadf59743930`

Environment:

- macOS 15.3 (`24D60`)
- Apple Silicon / `arm64`
- Darwin `24.3.0`

### Verification performed

```console
$ pkgutil --check-signature podman-installer-macos-arm64.pkg
Package "podman-installer-macos-arm64.pkg":
   Status: invalid signature
```

The file size and SHA-256 were checked before this command. The package was not
installed or expanded, and none of its scripts or binaries were executed.

### Workflow evidence

- annotated tag target:
  `b28edb9ad70ce4317dc762ee9ce0a6d081d154e9`; GitHub tag verification is
  `valid`
- release workflow run: `29887033210`, attempt 1, conclusion `success`
- macOS installer job: `88819584126`, conclusion `success`
- exposed steps `Create Keychain`, `Build and Sign ARM`, and `Artifact` all
  report `success`

At the exact tag, `release-build-artifacts.yml` supplies a Developer ID
Installer identity and runs `make ARCH=aarch64 notarize`. `package.sh` uses
`productsign --timestamp`, and the Makefile submits with `notarytool --wait`
before stapling the ticket.

### Expected result

`pkgutil --check-signature` should report a valid Developer ID Installer chain
for the exact release asset, consistent with the successful signing and
notarization workflow.

### Clarification requested

Could maintainers please confirm:

1. the expected Developer ID Installer certificate subject/team ID;
2. the expected `pkgutil --check-signature` and
   `spctl -a -vv -t install` results for this exact SHA-256;
3. the notarization request result/identifier and whether its ticket was
   stapled to the uploaded bytes;
4. whether asset ID `485432449` is the exact output of macOS job `88819584126`;
5. whether the asset is known-bad and, if so, whether a separately versioned
   corrected immutable artifact will be published;
6. whether signed checksums or a GitHub artifact attestation are available.

I found no existing issue or Discussion for this exact asset hash or Apple
Installer signature failure. Issues #22887 and #24558 concern older incomplete
`shasums` files, not package-signature validity.

title: hack/ci: pass -r to limactl copy for directory copies
body:
## Description

`hack/ci/ci.sh` calls `limactl copy` twice on directories — the repo directory being copied into the VM at line 30, and the logs directory being copied back out at line 40. `limactl copy` uses the underlying host transport (scp or rsync) and without `-r`, `scp` refuses a directory with `is not a regular file`, which matches what @mtrmac reported in #29425. It happens to work in CI (likely the rsync path) but breaks in local VMs (scp path).

Small fix: add `-r` to both `limactl copy` directory calls so they're always recursive regardless of the underlying transport.

Fixes #29425

## Testing

Shell change only, no Go build affected. Local-VM reproducer requires an environment where limactl uses the scp transport — happy to iterate if @mtrmac or @timcoding1988 can confirm on the exact setup that failed.

title: systemd: set /run/podman mode via DirectoryMode instead of tmpfiles
body:
Fixes: #27145

The tmpfiles rule creates `/run/podman` at boot, so `DirectoryMode=` on `podman.socket` never applies and a drop-in silently does nothing. Moving the mode into the socket unit keeps the same 0700 default and makes it overridable.

Tested with the drop-in from the issue. `DirectoryMode=0755` plus `SocketGroup=` gives a 755 directory and a 660 socket with that group. Without a drop-in it stays 0700, same as before.

Two notes:

`contrib/systemd/user/podman.socket` is a symlink to this file, so the rootless socket gets `DirectoryMode=0700` too. `$XDG_RUNTIME_DIR` is already 0700 and `resolveAPIURI()` also uses 0700, so this just makes systemd match podman.

`nv-proxy.sock` shares the directory, so netavark would need the same change in its own repo.

body:
### Issue Description

## brief

`Dockerfile RUN` nix flake fail with

```console
error: this system does not support the kernel namespaces that are required for sandboxing; use '--no-sandbox' to disable sandboxing
```

Seems due to `Dockerfile RUN` environment `unshare(CLONE_NEWNS)` failure.

## TODO

1. `Dockerfile RUN` environment `unshare(CLONE_NEWNS)` failure, is this a bug?

2. How to safely allow `unshare(CLONE_NEWNS)`?

3. If impossible to safely allow `unshare(CLONE_NEWNS)`, are there safe alternatives, or safe suggestions?

### Steps to reproduce the issue

https://github.com/loynoir/reproduce-nix-16186


### Describe the results you received

`Dockerfile RUN` nix flake fail with

```console
error: this system does not support the kernel namespaces that are required for sandboxing; use '--no-sandbox' to disable sandboxing
```

Seems due to `Dockerfile RUN` environment `unshare(CLONE_NEWNS)` failure.


### Describe the results you expected

`Dockerfile RUN` nix flake OK

### podman info output

```yaml
podman version 5.8.4
```

### Podman in a container

No

### Privileged Or Rootless

None

### Upstream Latest Release

Yes

### Additional environment details

Additional environment details

### Additional information

## background

`nix derivation` is similar to `PKGBUILD` `build()` function + `package()` function.

`nix derivation` create chroot jail, only which have fixed hash output , able to access network.

In normal cases, `non fixed output derivation` should be offline.

But when within flake within dockerfile, `non fixed output derivation` unexpectedly able to access network.

This seems caused by nix think `Dockerfile RUN` environment lack of kernel namespaces.

```console
error: this system does not support the kernel namespaces that are required for sandboxing; use '--no-sandbox' to disable sandboxing
```

But basic namespace test seems OK.

```console
#7 [3/6] RUN ls /proc/self/ns/cgroup && echo namespace OK
#7 CACHED
```

https://github.com/NixOS/nix/issues/16186#issuecomment-5193724577

xokdvium seems suggest this is caused by `Dockerfile RUN` environment `unshare(CLONE_NEWNS)` failure.

```console
0.184 unshare(CLONE_NEWNS)                    = -1 EPERM (Operation not permitted)
11.85 clone(child_stack=0x71f6e378eff0, flags=CLONE_NEWUSER|SIGCHLD) = -1 EPERM (Operation not permitted)
11.85 munmap(0x71f6e368f000, 1048576)         = 0
11.85 mmap(NULL, 1048576, PROT_READ|PROT_WRITE, MAP_PRIVATE|MAP_ANONYMOUS|MAP_STACK, -1, 0) = 0x71f6e368f000
11.85 clone(child_stack=0x71f6e378eff0, flags=CLONE_NEWNS|CLONE_NEWPID|SIGCHLD) = -1 EPERM (Operation not permitted)
```

https://github.com/opencontainers/image-spec/issues/1331#issuecomment-5199600655

Also, cyphar seems suggest `CLONE_NEWUSER` might be dangerous.

> The kernel also requires `CAP_SYS_ADMIN` for all namespaces other than `CLONE_NEWUSER` but that is explicitly blocked by container runtimes because it has led to many kernel 0days that could be used as container escapes in the past.

> Some container runtimes let you adjust the security profile for builds, others don't -- consult their documentation.

I opened QA in `moby/buildkit` and `podman-container-tools/podman`.

https://github.com/moby/buildkit/discussions/7023

https://github.com/podman-container-tools/podman/discussions/29400

title: Flake: macOS arm64 lima setup fails with "retrieved architecture x86_64 does not match target architecture arm64"

labels.name: kind/bug
labels.description: Categorizes issue or PR as related to a bug.

body:
### Issue Description

markdown
## Description

The `sys local rootless fedora-current / lima` CI job intermittently fails on `macos-15-arm64` runners with an architecture mismatch error during Lima VM setup. The failure occurs before any Podman tests can run, causing the `Total Success` aggregator job to fail and requiring maintainers to trigger re-runs manually.

Filing this as a CI flake report rather than a local reproducer — no `podman version` / `podman info` output applies since the failure happens before Podman itself is invoked in the job.

## Reproducer

Observed in CI run [#31171540579](https://github.com/containers/podman/actions/runs/31171540579), job `sys local rootless fedora-current / lima`, on PR #29417.

The failure was resolved on re-run — a strong indicator this is a flake rather than a code regression.

## Failing Output

Fatal error: retrieved architecture x86_64 does not match target architecture arm64
Error: PANIC: retrieved architecture x86_64 does not match target architecture arm64


The failure occurs during Lima VM provisioning, before Podman itself is invoked.

## Environment

- Runner: `macos-15-arm64`
- Provider: Lima (macOS VM manager)
- Target OS: `fedora-current`
- Job: `sys local rootless fedora-current / lima`

## Impact

- Every PR touching code paths that trigger the mac-lima matrix is at risk of hitting this
- The `Total Success` aggregator fails when this job fails, blocking merge signals
- Maintainer time is spent re-running jobs to distinguish this flake from real failures
- No searchable issue or PR currently references this error string, suggesting the flake is present but has been treated as noise rather than reported

## Hypothesis on Root Cause

The error message indicates that a downloaded or cached Fedora cloud image is `x86_64` when the runner is `arm64`. Three candidate root causes worth investigating:

1. **Image URL / architecture selection bug** — the code choosing which cloud image to download may default to `x86_64` under some conditions instead of detecting the runner's arch
2. **Cache reuse across architectures** — a previously cached `x86_64` image may be reused when the runner requests `arm64`, without an architecture check on cache lookup
3. **Environment/config drift** — `GOARCH`, Lima's config, or an environment variable is being set to `x86_64` in a code path that should honor the host arch

Investigating which of these is the actual cause requires reproducing locally on an arm64 Mac and inspecting the Lima setup logs earlier in the job (before the fatal error).

## Categorization

This fits a **configuration/environment mismatch** flake category rather than an infrastructure blip, race condition, or network timeout. Distinguishing signals:

- The error string is deterministic and specific — not a generic timeout or connection error
- The failure occurs at setup time, not during test execution — no test flakiness patterns (retries, timing sensitivity) apply
- The failure resolves on re-run — indicating state (cached image, env var) rather than code being the difference between runs

For an automated triage pipeline, this class of failure is high-signal: the error string is unique enough that a simple pattern match could categorize it correctly, and the "resolves on re-run" pattern is a strong indicator that the underlying state (not the code) needs attention.

## Suggested Next Steps

- Confirm reproducibility by scanning historical CI runs for the same error string
- Instrument the Lima setup path to log the arch-detection decision and any cache-hit metadata
- If confirmed as caching-related, add an arch check on cache lookup and invalidate cross-arch entries

Happy to help investigate further or contribute a fix if pointed in the right direction.

title: libpod: fix Batch sharing container state with the original container
body:
`Batch()` builds a new `Container` so the batch function operates on a copy, but it assigned the state pointer directly:

```go
newCtr.state = c.state
```

Both containers therefore pointed at the same `ContainerState`, so every state change made inside the batch function was applied to the container `Batch()` was called on, defeating the copy.

This copies the state instead. A plain struct copy is not enough, because libpod modifies the maps held by the state in place (adding/removing exec sessions, dropping bind mounts, ...) and those would still be shared. `ContainerState.copy()` clones the maps and the service pod slice; the values stored in the maps remain shared, which is fine as libpod replaces rather than mutates them.

A regression test covers both the plain fields and the in-place map/slice modifications.

title: docs: Build Volume= only supports host directories
body:

title: rootless: --pids-limit=-1/0 sets cgroup pids.max=1 instead of unlimited
body:
## Description

`podman run --pids-limit=-1` (and `--pids-limit=0`) are documented/intended to mean "unlimited" pids for the container. Instead, on a rootless setup with cgroup v2 + the systemd cgroup manager, the container's cgroup ends up with `pids.max` literally set to `1` — meaning the container can host exactly one process. Any attempt to fork a second process inside the container fails immediately with `Resource temporarily unavailable`.

Omitting `--pids-limit` entirely (falls back to the `containers.conf` default of 2048) or passing any explicit positive number works correctly.

This reproduces both with and without `--privileged`, so it isn't specific to privileged mode.

## Steps to reproduce

```console
$ podman run -d --rm --pids-limit=-1 docker.io/library/alpine:latest sleep 30
<cid>

$ podman exec <cid> sh -c 'sh -c "echo forked-ok"'
sh: can't fork: Resource temporarily unavailable

$ podman inspect <cid> --format '{{.State.Pid}}'
<pid>
$ awk -F: '{print $3}' /proc/<pid>/cgroup
/user.slice/user-1000.slice/user@1000.service/user.slice/libpod-<cid>.scope
$ cat /sys/fs/cgroup/user.slice/user-1000.slice/user@1000.service/user.slice/libpod-<cid>.scope/pids.max
1
```

Compare with a positive limit, which behaves correctly:

```console
$ podman run -d --rm --pids-limit=4096 docker.io/library/alpine:latest sleep 30
<cid>
$ podman exec <cid> sh -c 'sh -c "echo forked-ok"'
forked-ok
$ cat /sys/fs/cgroup/.../libpod-<cid>.scope/pids.max
4096
```

And with the flag omitted (default):

```console
$ podman run -d --rm docker.io/library/alpine:latest sleep 30
$ cat /sys/fs/cgroup/.../libpod-<cid>.scope/pids.max
2048
```

## Full table

| `--pids-limit` value | resulting cgroup `pids.max` | fork works inside container? |
|---|---|---|
| (omitted) | `2048` | yes |
| `-1` | `1` | **no** |
| `0` | `1` | **no** |
| `4096` | `4096` | yes |

## Expected behavior

`--pids-limit=-1` (and per the docs, `0`) should result in `pids.max` being set to `max` (unlimited), not `1`.

## Environment

```
$ podman version
Client:       Podman Engine
Version:      4.9.3
API Version:  4.9.3
Go Version:   go1.22.2
OS/Arch:      linux/amd64

$ podman info --format '{{.Host.OCIRuntime.Name}} {{.Host.OCIRuntime.Version}}'
runc runc version 1.4.3
commit: v1.4.3-0-gbb14dabe
spec: 1.3.0

$ podman info --format 'CgroupVersion={{.Host.CgroupsVersion}} CgroupManager={{.Host.CgroupManager}}'
CgroupVersion=v2 CgroupManager=systemd

$ cat /etc/os-release
NAME="Linux Mint"
VERSION="22.3 (Zena)"

$ uname -r
6.17.0-1030-oem
```

Rootless podman, invoked directly (`podman run ...`), no extra wrapping beyond a plain user session (no container manager, no Docker-compat shim).

## Additional context

This silently breaks any workload that relies on `--pids-limit=-1`/`0` meaning "unlimited" — in our case, a dev-container entrypoint using `dumb-init` as PID 1 failed at its very first `fork()` with `[dumb-init] Unable to fork. Exiting.`, which took some digging to trace back to the cgroup `pids.max=1`. Related but distinct from #11782 (which was about `-1` being rejected outright) and #13891 (which is the opposite failure — the limit being silently *ignored*, `pids.max` staying `max`, in rootless mode). Here the flag is accepted and *does* take effect, just with the wrong numeric value.

### Issue Description

I am currently stuck on Ubuntu 24 LTS and thus with podman 4.9.3. Please give a holler if this is fixed in a newer version, then I can go pester my admin to update me further "with due cause".

[Asked about it on Stack Exchange last week to no replies so far.](https://superuser.com/q/1939377/563952)

Trying to run a container with RHEL 9.5 and _no_ apparmor on my Ubuntu 24 LTS host with (as far as I know) vanilla apparmor settings, rsyslog inside the container fails, because all the custom file paths it has configured (e.g. `/etc/my/rsyslog.conf`, `/tmp/dev_log`, etc.) are being blocked by _the host system's_ apparmor.

In `sudo dmesg` I see that apparmor sees the files in question, as if they were part of the host filesystem - no wonder then, that it blocks them. E.g.
```

```

How do I get podman to isolate the container as the black box it is supposed to be? Why would host apparmor even see these files or their using process and _why would it see the in-container path!?!?_

### Steps to reproduce the issue

1. start a container without apparmor

- Container should be a blackbox, outside of podman neither the in-container rsyslog nor the in-container file nor any in-container path should be visible to apparmor _or any other program_, unless explicitly forwarded.

title: libpod: resolve volume paths per entry when copying archive to stopped container
body:
<!-- Thanks for sending a pull request! -->

#### What this PR does

Updates `copyFromArchive` when copying a tar archive into a stopped container that has mounted volumes or bind mounts.
Previously, calling `PUT /containers/{id}/archive?path=/` on a stopped container resolved the destination root strictly to the container's rootfs layer. `copier.Put` extracted entries targeting `/mymount/...` directly into the underlying rootfs storage layer instead of the volume storage directory (`_data`). When the container subsequently started, the volume was mounted over `/mymount`, hiding the extracted files.

This PR updates `copyFromArchive` for stopped containers with volumes/mounts to resolve the exact host storage destination (volume directory or bind mount source) per archive entry via `c.resolvePath()`. Also adds an API v2 regression test in `23-containersArchive.at`.

title: Rootless Quadlet network cleanup fails during systemd user manager shutdown

labels.name: kind/bug
labels.description: Categorizes issue or PR as related to a bug.

labels.name: network
labels.description: Networking related issue or feature

labels.name: triaged
labels.description: Issue has been triaged

body:
### Issue Description

During an orderly reboot, the generated service for a rootless Quadlet container attached to a custom bridge network exits with status 125. The systemd user manager stops Podman's pasta and pause scopes while the generated service is still cleaning up. Teardown sees that pasta has stopped and tries to recreate its scope, which systemd rejects because the exit transaction is already queued. Netavark then tries to start Aardvark DNS, but that scope is also rejected and cleanup fails. Explicitly running `systemctl --user stop repro.service` succeeds with status zero, and the service recovers on the next boot.

### Steps to reproduce the issue

1. On a disposable systemd host with persistent journald storage, install Podman 6.0.2 with netavark 2.0.0, Aardvark DNS 2.0.0, and pasta. Create a rootless user with subordinate UID and GID ranges, then enable lingering for it:

   ```console
   sudo loginctl enable-linger podman-repro
   ```

2. In a normal login session as `podman-repro`, pull the image and create the Quadlet directory:

   ```console
   podman pull quay.io/libpod/alpine@sha256:fa93b01658e3a5a1686dc3ae55f170d8de487006fb53a28efcd12ab0710a2e5f
   mkdir -p ~/.config/containers/systemd
   ```

3. Create `~/.config/containers/systemd/repro.network`:

   ```systemd
   [Network]
   NetworkName=quadlet-shutdown-repro

title: libpod: fix PruneBuildContainers early return and size overflow
body:
## What does this PR do?

Fixes two bugs in `PruneBuildContainers()`:

### 1. Early return aborts entire pruning loop

`ContainerDirectory()` failure caused `return`, stopping the loop. One bad container prevented all remaining containers from being pruned.

**Fix**: Changed to `continue` so pruning proceeds past individual failures, matching the existing pattern for `fileutils.Exists()` on line 1329.

### 2. `report.Size` set to garbage on error

`report.Size = uint64(size)` ran unconditionally, even when `ContainerSize()` returned an error. A negative `int64` error value cast to `uint64` silently overflows to a very large number.

**Fix**: Only set `report.Size` when `ContainerSize()` succeeds.

## How was this tested?

- Verified the fix compiles: `GOOS=linux go build -tags containers_image_openpgp ./libpod/...`
- Verified `make binaries` succeeds
- Code review of the 3-line change

Signed-off-by: nishantbkl3345-ship-it <nishantbkl3345-ship-it@users.noreply.github.com>

title: events: logNeedsRotation uses rune count instead of byte length for content size calculation

labels.name: kind/bug
labels.description: Categorizes issue or PR as related to a bug.

body:
## Issue Description

While reviewing the event logfile rotation implementation in `libpod/events/logfile.go`, I noticed an issue in how `logNeedsRotation()` computes the size of incoming event content:

```go
filesize := uint64(file.Size())
contentsize := uint64(len([]rune(content)))
if filesize+contentsize < limit {
    return false, nil
}
```
`file.Size()` returns the on-disk file size in bytes, but `contentsize` is calculated by converting the string to []rune and counting Unicode code points.

**This causes two issues:**

1. **Unit mismatch on multi-byte UTF-8 data**: If event payloads contain multi-byte characters (in container labels, annotations, or names), `len([]rune(content))` returns fewer units than the actual byte length written to disk by `writeString()`. This causes the rotation check to underestimate the total size and allows the logfile to grow beyond `LogFileMaxSize` before rotation triggers.
2. **Unnecessary allocations**: Converting `content` to `[]rune` allocates a new slice on the heap on every single event write just to check its length.

## Steps to reproduce the issue

1. Configure `events_logfile_max_size` in `containers.conf` to a small threshold (e.g., 500 bytes).
2. Generate container/pod events that include multi-byte UTF-8 characters in labels or names (e.g., `podman run --rm --label "desc=测试容器数据" alpine true`).
3. Inspect `logNeedsRotation()` behavior in `libpod/events/logfile.go` when calculating `contentsize`.

## Describe the results you received

`logNeedsRotation()` measures `contentsize` in character/rune count (`len([]rune(content))`), mixing bytes (`file.Size()`) with rune counts, which underestimates the true byte footprint of multi-byte UTF-8 events and allocates a temporary slice on every event write.

## Describe the results you expected

`logNeedsRotation()` should calculate `contentsize` as byte length using `uint64(len(content))` to match `file.Size()` in bytes, avoiding both undercounting of multi-byte characters and unnecessary heap allocations from `[]rune` conversions.

title: macOS/libkrun: gvproxy SIGKILLed under load (Podman Desktop proven responsible; second unidentified killer) — machine left "running" but dead
body:
## Issue Description

On macOS (arm64, libkrun machine), `gvproxy` gets **force-killed (SIGKILL)** under load, leaving the Podman machine reporting "Currently running" while every `podman` CLI call fails with connection refused. `krunkit` stays alive. Nothing restarts gvproxy.

With Podman Desktop running, Endpoint Security (eslogger) proves the kill comes from Podman Desktop itself. But gvproxy also dies with Podman Desktop fully quit — so there is a second, unidentified killer.

## Evidence

**eslogger capture (Endpoint Security, exit event):**
```json
{
  "event": { "exit": { "stat": 9 } },
  "process": {
    "signing_id": "gvproxy",
    "executable": { "path": "/opt/podman/bin/gvproxy" },
    "responsible_audit_token": { "pid": 903 },
    "parent_audit_token": { "pid": 1 }
  }
}
```
`stat:9` = SIGKILL. `responsible_audit_token.pid=903` = Podman Desktop.

**Timeline (watchdog logging every few seconds):**
- Deaths at 10:57, 11:25, 11:38 with Podman Desktop running (machine recreated in that window).
- Death at 12:21 with Podman Desktop **quit** (quit at 11:53, verified no process) — after ~26 min of mixed load (periodic `podman pull`/`run` every 3 min + heavy traffic through forwarded ports). krunkit alive.
- Overnight: gvproxy survived ~22 h mostly idle, died at 10:30 during a `podman compose up -d`.

**Ruled out:** no crash report in `~/Library/Logs/DiagnosticReports`; no jetsam/memorystatus (host 24 GiB, krunkit RSS ~1.9/3.7 GiB); nothing in the unified log; guest kernel log shows no panic/lockup; guest did not reboot during the controlled window (`last reboot`, `journalctl -k`); Zincati is disabled in the VM.

**Correlations:** gvproxy is stable at rest (15+ min to 22 h), and dies under CLI/network load — all podman CLI ops transit through gvproxy's forwarded socket, image pulls through its NAT, and heavy forwarded-port traffic (S3 uploads to a container) preceded two of the deaths.

## Steps to reproduce

1. `podman machine start` (libkrun machine; happens both when started from CLI and from Podman Desktop).
2. Exercise the machine: `podman pull` + `podman run` every few minutes, optionally sustained traffic through a published port (e.g. large HTTP uploads to a container).
3. Within ~10–30 min: gvproxy disappears; `podman ps` → connection refused; `podman machine ls` still says "Currently running".

## Expected behavior

gvproxy should not be SIGKILLed; if it dies, podman should detect it and either restart it or mark the machine as broken (instead of "running").

## Versions

- Podman client 6.0.2 (also observed on 5.8.3) — installed from the official installer (`/opt/podman/bin`)
- gvproxy v0.8.9 (latest gvisor-tap-vsock release)
- krunkit 1.3.2 (latest), libkrun provider
- Podman Desktop 1.29.1
- macOS arm64, 24 GiB RAM; machine: 6 CPU / 3.7 GiB / libkrun
- Guest: Fedora CoreOS (machine-os), Zincati disabled

## Related issues

- #22053 — "gvproxy process exited after a while" (same symptom triad: machine "running", hypervisor alive, gvproxy gone), closed as not reproducible in 2024.
- #28746 — libkrun/gvproxy lifecycle (gvproxy exits, never restarted), closed as not reproducible.
- freedomofpress/dangerzone#1187 — issue only occurs when the machine is started from Podman Desktop, not from the CLI (matches our A/B where Desktop is one proven killer).

## Additional notes

- Quitting Podman Desktop stops the whole machine (gvproxy + krunkit) — expected per podman-desktop#15867, but it means Desktop both kills gvproxy during use *and* owns the machine lifecycle.
- We could not identify the second killer (the one acting with Podman Desktop quit); a follow-up eslogger capture is planned. If maintainers have a hypothesis (a podman client helper? a launchd job?), we can test it.

title: machine/wsl: detect native systemd as running
body:
<!-- Thanks for sending a pull request! -->
This fixes the way we find systemd for Windows Subsystem for Linux distributions that use systemd.

Now we look for a systemd process that starts with /lib/systemd/systemd.. In my Windows Subsystem for Linux environment systemd is running as the main process and it uses /usr/lib/systemd/systemd. So the current way of checking does not. Podman might think systemd has stopped incorrectly.

title: fix: align volume event filter to match by name or ID prefix
body:
This PR fixes a bug in how volume events are filtered, making the behavior consistent with all other resource filters.

Currently, the `VOLUME` filter only performs a prefix match on the volume name (`strings.HasPrefix(e.Name, filterValue)`). This means that filtering by a volume ID (e.g. `podman events --filter volume=<id>`) silently fails and returns zero events because there's no fallback to check the ID.

This updates the `VOLUME` filter logic in `libpod/events/filters.go` to match the exact same pattern already used for `CONTAINER`, `IMAGE`, `POD`, and `ARTIFACT` filters:
1. Check for an exact name match first.
2. Fall back to an ID prefix match.

Fixes #29398

**Release Note**

Fixed a bug where filtering events by volume ID (`podman events --filter volume=<id>`) would silently return no results. The volume filter now correctly matches by exact name or ID prefix, consistent with other resource filters.

title: podman events --filter volume=<id> silently drops events (inconsistent with other filters)

labels.name: kind/bug
labels.description: Categorizes issue or PR as related to a bug.

body:
## Issue Description

While looking through the events filtering code in `libpod/events/filters.go`, I noticed that the `VOLUME` filter behaves differently than all the other filters (`CONTAINER`, `IMAGE`, `POD`, `ARTIFACT`).

For other resources, the filter checks for an exact name match first, and then falls back to checking if the ID starts with the filter string. However, for `VOLUME`, it only does a `strings.HasPrefix` check on the name, and completely omits the ID check.

Because of this, filtering volume events by volume ID silently fails and returns zero events. Also, filtering by a partial name prefix works when it probably shouldn't (since other filters require an exact name match).

## Steps to reproduce the issue

Steps to reproduce the issue
1.Create a volume:
```bash
podman volume create myvol
```
2.Trigger an event for it (e.g., mount it to a temporary container):
```bash
podman run --rm -v myvol:/data alpine touch /data/file
```
3.Get the volume's ID/Mountpoint hash (or just grab any part of its internal ID):
```bash
VOL_ID=$(podman volume inspect myvol --format '{{.Mountpoint}}' | sha256sum | cut -c1-8)
```
4.Try to filter events by that ID:
```bash
podman events --filter volume=$VOL_ID --since 1h
```


## Describe the results you received

No events are returned when filtering by the volume ID. Additionally, filtering by a partial name like `podman events --filter volume=myv` returns events, which is inconsistent with how container/image name filters work.

## Describe the results you expected

Filtering by volume ID should return the relevant events, just like it does for containers, images, and pods. The name match should probably be exact as well.

## Proposed Fix
libpod/events/filters.go (around line 73), the VOLUME case should be updated to match the pattern used by the other resources:

```diff
case "VOLUME":
		return func(e *Event) bool {
			if e.Type != Volume {
				return false
			}
-			// Prefix match with name for consistency with docker
-			return strings.HasPrefix(e.Name, filterValue)
+			if e.Name == filterValue {
+				return true
+			}
+			return strings.HasPrefix(e.ID, filterValue)
		}, nil
```

title: libpod: fix format string argument order, store cleanup leak, and avoid panic in WaitForConditionWithInterval
body:
## Description
Fixes critical argument ordering bugs, resource leaks, and panic hazards in `libpod`:

1. **Fix Swapped Errorf Format Arguments (Audit Issue #2)**
   - **File**: `libpod/container_internal.go:208-209`
   - **Fix**: Reordered parameters passed to `fmt.Errorf` so `%q` receives `statusCodeStr` and `%s` receives `c.ID()`.
   - **Before**: `converting exit status code ("abc123container", err) for container invalid_status_code to int: invalid syntax`
   - **After**: `converting exit status code "invalid_status_code" for container abc123container to int: invalid syntax`
   - **Test**: Added `TestHandleExitFile_InvalidStatusCode` in `libpod/container_internal_test.go`.

2. **Fix Deferred Storage Cleanup Leak in `makeRuntime` (Audit Issue #10)**
   - **File**: `libpod/runtime.go:489-497`
   - **Fix**: Updated `defer` in `makeRuntime` to check `runtime.store != nil` instead of unassigned local variable `store` (which was always `nil`). Removed unused `var store storage.Store` declaration.
   - **Effect**: Ensures `runtime.store.Shutdown(false)` is correctly called if `makeRuntime()` fails during subsequent initialization steps.
   - **Test**: Added `TestMakeRuntime_StoreCleanupOnFailure` in `libpod/runtime_test.go`.

3. **Avoid Panic in `WaitForConditionWithInterval` (Audit Issue #4)**
   - **File**: `libpod/container_api.go:736`
   - **Fix**: Return error instead of panicking on empty conditions.

4. **Signed Off**

title: image scp: add --compression-format and --compression-level

labels.name: kind/api-change
labels.description: Change to remote API; merits scrutiny

body:
`podman save` writes docker-archive layers uncompressed, so `podman image scp` puts the whole archive on the wire as is. Today people work around that with `podman save | zstd`, a manual copy and `podman load` on the far side.

This adds `--compression-format` (gzip, zstd) and `--compression-level` so the transfer does it itself. Nothing is needed on the destination: `podman load` detects the compression from the stream and decompresses it.

Compression happens on whichever host produces the archive, so only compressed bytes cross the network:

- **Local source** — the archive is compressed on the fly into the ssh stream feeding the remote `podman image load`, via the c/image compression package. No second temporary file, nothing buffered in full.
- **Remote source** — the archive has to be compressed there, and the only thing we can do on that host is run a command, so the matching compressor is invoked over ssh between the save and the copy. That is also why the format list is limited to algorithms available as a command of the same name.
- **Two users on the same machine** — nothing crosses a network, so a requested format is reported as ignored rather than refused.

Measured on `quay.io/libpod/alpine`, docker-archive goes from 5.85 MB to 2.72 MB with zstd. An oci-archive keeps whatever compression its layers already have, so there the gain is negligible (~98%); the man page records the difference.

Fixes: #23192

```release-note
podman image scp now supports --compression-format and --compression-level to compress the transferred image archive.
```

title: events: add missing support for NETWORK filter
body:
## What does this PR do?

This PR fixes a bug where trying to filter podman events by a network name (like `podman events --filter network=mynet`) would just fail outright with the error `Error: NETWORK is an invalid filter`. 

While looking into this, I noticed that the `Network` event type was fully defined in `config.go` (along with the `connect` and `disconnect` statuses and the `Event.Network` struct field), but the `generateEventFilter` switch statement in `filters.go` completely missed the `NETWORK` case. Anything falling through that switch statement throws an error, which is why filtering network events was broken.

I've added the missing case to `generateEventFilter`, putting it right alongside the logic for volumes and pods. It supports matching by both network name (`e.Network`) and ID prefix (`e.ID`), which keeps it consistent with how Docker behaves when using `--filter network=...`.

Fixes: #29387

## Testing

I couldn't really add a unit test in `logfile_test.go` because the tests there focus strictly on the log rotation mechanics rather than filter logic itself, but this could easily be verified manually:

1. `podman network create mynet`
2. `podman run -d --name mytest --network mynet alpine sleep 300`
3. `podman events --filter network=mynet --no-stream`

Before this PR, step 3 fails immediately. After this PR, it successfully returns the network connect/disconnect events for `mynet`.

title: podman events --filter network=<name> always fails with "NETWORK is an invalid filter"

labels.name: kind/bug
labels.description: Categorizes issue or PR as related to a bug.

labels.name: triaged
labels.description: Issue has been triaged

body:
## Issue Description

When trying to filter podman events by network name or ID (e.g., `podman events --filter network=mynet`), the command unconditionally fails with the error `Error: NETWORK is an invalid filter`. 
This seems to be an oversight in the event filtering logic. The `Network` event type is fully defined (`Network Type = "network"` in `libpod/events/config.go`), and network events like `connect` and `disconnect` are successfully emitted. However, the `NETWORK` case is completely missing from the `generateEventFilter` switch statement in `libpod/events/filters.go`.

## Steps to reproduce the issue

Steps to reproduce the issue
1.1. Create a dummy network and start a container on it:
   ```bash
   podman network create mynet
   podman run -d --name mytest --network mynet alpine sleep 300
```
2.Try to filter the events by the network name:
```bash
podman events --filter network=mynet --no-stream
```



## Describe the results you received

The command immediately errors out:

`Error: NETWORK is an invalid filter`

## Describe the results you expected

It should return the network events (like `connect` and `disconnect`) that match the given network name or ID prefix, which would match Docker's behavior for` --filter network=...`.

If you run `podman events --no-stream --type network` (without the specific name filter), you can see that the events are being tracked perfectly fine, we just can't filter them by name.

## podman info output

```yaml
Client:       Podman Engine
Version:      5.0.0 (or current main branch)
API Version:  5.0.0
OS/Arch:      linux/amd64
```
## Root Cause & Proposed Fix
In libpod/events/filters.go, the generateEventFilter function has cases for CONTAINER, IMAGE, POD, VOLUME, etc., but no NETWORK case. Anything falling through the switch statement returns fmt.Errorf("%s is an invalid filter", filter).

It looks like we just need to add the missing case to generateEventFilter in libpod/events/filters.go:
```go
case "NETWORK":
		return func(e *Event) bool {
			if e.Type != Network {
				return false
			}
			// Prefix match with name or ID for consistency
			if e.Network == filterValue {
				return true
			}
			return strings.HasPrefix(e.ID, filterValue)
		}, nil
```

title: bug: --volume src:dst:mode parser corrupts destination path when src == dst (6.0.2)

labels.name: kind/bug
labels.description: Categorizes issue or PR as related to a bug.

labels.name: remote
labels.description: Problem is in podman-remote

labels.name: macos
labels.description: MacOS (OSX) related

body:
### Issue Description

On Podman 6.0.2, `--volume <src>:<dst>:<mode>` corrupts the destination path when `src` and `dst` are identical: the mode's second character is appended to `dst`, and the intended destination ends up empty inside the container.

- `:ro` → destination gets a trailing `o`
- `:rw` → destination gets a trailing `w`

`--mount type=bind,src=…,dst=…[,readonly]` is not affected and can be used as a workaround. Bug appears specific to the `--volume` argument parser (likely `pkg/specgen/volumes.go` or an upstream caller in the CLI layer).

### Steps to reproduce the issue

Verified on 3/3 attempts against a scratch directory that lives on the host bind-mount surface (`/Users`).

```bash
SCRATCH=/Users/$(whoami)/podman-repro-scratch
mkdir -p "$SCRATCH" && echo "canary" > "$SCRATCH/marker.txt"

podman run --rm --volume "$SCRATCH:$SCRATCH:ro" alpine:latest sh -c "
  echo '--- $SCRATCH (expected: contains marker.txt) ---'
  ls -la '$SCRATCH' 2>&1
  echo '--- ${SCRATCH}o (expected: does not exist) ---'
  ls -la '${SCRATCH}o' 2>&1
"
```

Substitute `:rw` for `:ro` to observe the same corruption with `w` in place of `o`.


### Describe the results you received

```
--- /Users/liam/podman-repro-scratch (expected: contains marker.txt) ---
ls: /Users/liam/podman-repro-scratch: No such file or directory
--- /Users/liam/podman-repro-scratcho (expected: does not exist) ---
total 4
-rw-r--r--    1 root     root             7 Aug  3 19:06 marker.txt
```

The bind lands at `/Users/liam/podman-repro-scratch`**`o`** (mode's second char appended to dst). Intended destination does not exist inside the container.

### Describe the results you expected

The mount should appear at `/Users/liam/podman-repro-scratch` inside the container, populated with `marker.txt`. `/Users/liam/podman-repro-scratcho` should not exist.

`--mount` syntax works correctly:

```bash
podman run --rm \
  --mount "type=bind,src=$SCRATCH,dst=$SCRATCH,readonly" \
  alpine:latest ls -la "$SCRATCH"
```
