title: CI: run logformatter on the windows jobs again
body:
.cirrus.yml was the only thing setting CIRRUS_CI and it went away with 3743b9f806 ("Goodbye Cirrus"). Run-Command in hack/ci/win-lib.ps1 still checks for it before calling Invoke-Logformatter, so on the windows jobs that call just never happens and we get the raw ginkgo output with no html log at all.

winmake.ps1 sources that file and ci.yml calls winmake in four jobs, so this is windows installer, unit, e2e and machine.

I went with a PODMAN_CI set from the workflow instead of checking GITHUB_ACTIONS. GITHUB_ACTIONS is true for anyone running our tests out of their own workflow in a fork and they won't necessarily have perl, saw the same point come up on #29301. The github hosted windows-2025 image ships perl 5.42 so our own jobs are fine.

This only turns the call back on, I didn't touch logformatter itself. #29091 is doing that side for linux and doesn't touch win-lib.ps1, so I don't think these conflict. Happy to rebase if that one lands first.

One thing I left alone on purpose: lines 35-39 of the same file still Remove-Item CIRRUS_COMMIT_MESSAGE / CIRRUS_CHANGE_MESSAGE / CIRRUS_PR_BODY, which are also dead now. That felt like mixing cleanup into a behaviour fix so I skipped it.

I can't run the windows jobs locally, so I'm leaning on CI here to confirm the html log actually turns up.

title: quadlet: do not set RemainAfterExit=yes for volume units by default
body:
fixes #27862

### Summary
Quadlet previously set `RemainAfterExit=yes` by default when converting `.volume` unit files into systemd oneshot services. 

Because `RemainAfterExit=yes` keeps the service unit in the `active (exited)` state, if a volume is deleted (e.g. to update volume options) and a dependent container service is restarted, systemd skips re-executing the volume service since it is already marked active.

### Changes
- Updated `ConvertVolume()` in `pkg/systemd/quadlet/quadlet.go` to pass `false` for `remainAfterExit`.
- Updated Quadlet test fixture assertion in `test/e2e/quadlet/basic.volume`.

### Checklist
- [x] Code is signed off (`git commit -s`)
- [x] Tests pass / modified test updated

title: test/system: increase _check_health timeout to fix CI flake
body:
Ref #29353

### Summary
The `_check_health` test helper in `test/system/220-healthcheck.bats` previously used a 5-second timeout (8 seconds when running parallel). Under heavy parallel load on GitHub Actions CI runners, systemd timers for container healthchecks take longer to execute 3 retries, causing false-positive test timeouts while `FailingStreak` is at 2.

### Changes
- Increased base timeout in `_check_health` to 15s (25s when running in `$CI` or parallel `$PARALLEL_JOBSLOT` jobs).
- Ensures `podman events` polling loop allows sufficient margin for systemd timer execution under CI load without flaking.

title: Quadlet: allow configuring name template for secondary units

labels.name: kind/feature
labels.description: Categorizes issue or PR as related to a new feature.

body:
### Feature request description

Healthchecks fail on my system. I default-deny most of what `systemd-analyze security` checks for and allow services minimal capabilities and system calls. This is only manageable because systemd looks up overrides by left-truncating each unit's name: `foo-bar.service` gets overrides from `foo-.service.d`. This permits me to remove restrictions from all systemd- units, for example. Because podman needs a great deal of access to configure containers, I name all quadlets with a `quadlet-` prefix and override most restrictions.

Podman creates new units to perform health checks using the systemd API. These are named `<container id>-<some hex>.service`. The prefix is essentially random so I can't grant permissions to these. The service never reaches a healthy state, systemd always shows failed units, and the journal gets cluttered. 

### Suggest potential solution

I would like a way to configure the name of these secondary units. Maybe like `<quadlet name>-healthcheck.{service,timer}`. That would get the same overrides the quadlet itself gets. For example, if I have `quadlet-collabora.service` the healthcheck could be `quadlet-collabora-healthcheck.service.d`, which would get overrides in `quadlet-collabora-.service.d` and `quadlet-.service.d`.

### Have you considered any alternatives?

I could turn off default denials but given all the recent zero days I think they're pertinent.

I could use SELinux instead. That is a major undertaking for my server. But even if I do enable SELinux I think default denials are another useful layer.

I could scope the denials and prefix *all* the units on my system, but there are many vendor units I don't want to rename.

I could add drop-ins inside *every* unit on my system but it's easy to slip up and leave a service unrestricted.

### Additional context

title: CI: restore the CI_DESIRED_RUNTIME check
body:
CI_DESIRED_RUNTIME was only set in .cirrus.yml, and that file went away with
3743b9f806 ("Goodbye Cirrus"). The tests that read it are still there though,
so right now both of these just skip on every run:

- test/e2e/info_test.go, "Podman info: check desired runtime"
- test/system/005-info.bats, "podman info - confirm desired runtime"

When the var is empty they check CIRRUS_CI as a fallback, and that's obviously
never set under GHA, so they always hit the skip and the die()/Fail() under it
is unreachable. So the check from #14912 hasn't actually run since we moved off
Cirrus.

You can see it with:

    git show 3743b9f806^:.cirrus.yml | grep CI_DESIRED
    grep -rn CI_DESIRED_RUNTIME --include=*.yml .

So I set the variable in runner.sh and switched both tests to check
GITHUB_ACTIONS instead.

Couple of things I'm not sure about:

I ended up touching ci.sh too. limactl shell doesn't pass the host env into the
VM, so GITHUB_ACTIONS never reaches the tests and they'd have kept skipping
anyway. Passing it in explicitly was the simplest thing I could come up with,
happy to change it if you'd do it some other way. Both vars are in
PRESERVE_ENVS for the same reason, otherwise sudo drops them in the rootful
jobs.

I also hardcoded crun instead of deriving it from OCI_RUNTIME. I did derive it
at first, then realised OCI_RUNTIME is what picks the runtime in the first
place, so the test would just be comparing the value against itself and could
never fail. .cirrus.yml hardcoded it too so I'm guessing that was the point.

Left CI_DESIRED_STORAGE alone even though it's broken the same way. .cirrus.yml
set it to composefs on rawhide but STORAGE_FS there is overlay, and I couldn't
work out which one .Store.GraphDriverName is supposed to match. Can do it as a
follow up, or in here if you tell me which is right.

make validatepr passes. The real test is CI though, the desired runtime tests
should actually run now instead of skipping.

title: Pruning doesn't stop oneshot quadlet units

labels.name: kind/bug
labels.description: Categorizes issue or PR as related to a bug.

body:
### Issue Description

Pruning (`podman system prune`, `podman network prune`, etc.) deletes the resources (network, etc.) without stopping the relevant quadlet systemd units. Subsequently, systemd will believe that resource is still active and proceed to dependents, which will fail as the dependency isn't really active.

A typical setup is a scheduled oneshot container with it's own network, combined with a scheduled pruning job. Pruning will delete the network while leaving the network quadlet unit active (because it's a `Type=oneshot` + `RemainAfterExit=yes`). On the next scheduled start, systemd will believe the network is still active and start the container right away, while the container will fail as the network doesn't actually exist.

A workaround is to make the dependency resource to have `StopWhenUnneeded=yes` under `[Unit]`, if all dependencies are managed by systemd.

### Steps to reproduce the issue

1. Configure with quadlet a oneshot container and its own network with `Network=foo.network`.
1. `systemctl start <container-unit>`
1. At this point, container unit is dead while the network unit remains active.
1. `podman network prune`
1. `systemctl start <container-unit>`

### Describe the results you received

- After `podman network prune`, the network is deleted while the network unit remains active.
- After `systemctl start <container-unit>`, container startup fails due to missing network.

### Describe the results you expected

- After `podman network prune`, the network is deleted and the network unit becomes dead.
- After `systemctl start <container-unit>`, container starts successfully.

Alternatively, there should be a separate quadlet-aware mechanism to prune resources.

title: fix(exec): inherit precreate hook changes in exec sessions
body:
## Problem

A precreate hook that changes the container's process spec, for example one that appends an env var to process.env, is reflected in the running container: the container's init process sees it, podman inspect shows it, and exec capability handling already reads the on-disk spec. But podman exec itself still built its process spec from the container's stored config, which predates the hooks. So env vars added by a precreate hook were missing from exec sessions.

Reproducer (from issue #29347): install a precreate hook that runs jq '.process.env += ["FOO=BAR"]', run a container, then `podman exec <ctr> env` — FOO=BAR is absent even though the container's init process has it.

## Fix

prepareProcessExec now reads the on-disk spec from the bundle (same source as podman inspect and setProcessCapabilitiesExec) instead of the stored pre-hook config, so exec sessions inherit process changes made by precreate hooks. When the on-disk spec does not exist (container never started) it falls back to the stored config, preserving previous behavior.

## Tests

Added a bats regression test in test/system/075-exec.bats: a precreate hook appends PODMAN_HOOK_VAR to process.env, and the test asserts `podman exec printenv PODMAN_HOOK_VAR` returns it.

Fixes #29347

title: Fix --image-volume docs and completion to use 'anonymous'
body:
The man page for --image-volume lists "bind" as an option, and the shell completion offers "bind" too, but the runtime only accepts anonymous, tmpfs and ignore. "bind" is just a legacy alias that is rewritten to "anonymous" during argument parsing, so users who try it against the docs get a confusing mismatch with the error message.

This change:
- updates docs/source/markdown/options/image-volume.md to document "anonymous" as the canonical value (and as the default)
- updates the AutocompleteImageVolume completion in cmd/podman/common/completion.go to suggest the same values the parser actually accepts

Fixes: #27674

title: rootless: fix heap overflow in get_cmd_line_args when /proc/self/cmdline lacks the trailing NUL

labels.name: kind/api-change
labels.description: Change to remote API; merits scrutiny

body:
Fixes the heap overflow described in #29361.

`get_cmd_line_args()` sizes the argv array from the NUL count in `/proc/self/cmdline`, assuming the file ends with a trailing NUL (which mainline kernels guarantee). Non-mainline kernels (e.g. Android vendor kernels — verified on 4.14.190-perf+) can omit the trailing NUL; then `argc` only counts the separators between arguments, the allocation is one slot too small, and the fill loop (`argv[0]` + one entry per separator + the terminating `NULL`) overflows the array by one pointer. The overflowing NULL lands on the glibc top-chunk `size` field, which later aborts in `sysmalloc` (`malloc.c:2601` assertion) or in `unlink_chunk` ("corrupted size vs. prev_size").

This change counts only the NULs *between* arguments and sizes the array for `argv[0]` plus the terminating `NULL` — exact both with and without a trailing NUL.

Verified locally: on the affected kernel, podman built from this branch runs `pull` and starts containers without any allocator workaround.

- [x] Tests pass? — built and exercised on the affected kernel (pull + container run); no project-wide test suite run (device constraints)
- [x] Documentation — none affected

make: *** [Makefile:675: localunit] Error 127
```

The current recipe runs `$(GINKGO)` which is `./bin/ginkgo` but the target only declares `test/goecho/goecho` and `test/version/version` as prereq. Nothing builds ginkgo, so on a fresh clone the binary is missing. `/bin/` is gitignored, so it is never checked in.

The other three targets that use ginkgo all declare `.install.ginkgo`: `ginkgo-run` (line 695), `testbindings` (715) and `system.test-binary` (766). `localunit` is the only one that does not.

But
`hack/ci/runner.sh` already works around this:

 ```bash
 function run_unit() {
     make .install.ginkgo
     $SUDO make localunit
 }
 ```
This makes that first line unnecessary.
I used a file target rather than adding `.install.ginkgo` to the prerequisite list, because `.install.ginkgo` is `.PHONY` and would rebuild on every invocation. That matters here: `run_unit` runs `localunit` under sudo, so an unconditional rebuild would produce a root-owned `bin/ginkgo`. With a file target, make skips the build when the binary is present, which I checked with
 `make -n` on a warm tree (no rebuild commands emitted).
 
 With the fix, ginkgo builds and 64 suites run. 63 pass. The one failure is `pkg/machine/provider TestBadInstalledProviders`, which needs  `qemu-system-x86_64` that I do not have installed locally, and is unrelated to this change.
`make validatepr` passes.

title: Podman Desktop treats running WSL machine as stopped and reassigns SSH port (native systemd detection failure)

labels.name: kind/bug
labels.description: Categorizes issue or PR as related to a bug.

labels.name: remote
labels.description: Problem is in podman-remote

labels.name: windows
labels.description: issue/bug on Windows

body:
On Windows with a **WSL-backed** Podman machine, `podman machine list` / `podman machine inspect` often report **`State=stopped`** even when:

- `wsl -l -v` shows `podman-machine-default` **Running**
- systemd is healthy inside the guest (`systemctl is-system-running` → `running`)
- rootful Podman API works (via SSH or `wsl -d … podman`)

Podman Desktop then treats the machine as stopped and runs **`podman machine start`**, which under **`networkingMode=mirrored`** reassigns the SSH port (guest sshd already visible on Windows loopback), desyncs system connections, and fails with exit **125**. A working stack is damaged by the “fix” Start.

This is a **podman machine (Windows/WSL provider)** bug; Desktop is the common trigger.

## Root cause 1 — false negative in `isRunning()` / `State()`

WSL provider detects “running” approximately as:

```bash
SYSDPID=`ps -eo cmd,pid | grep -m 1 ^/lib/systemd/systemd | awk '{print $2}'`
# numeric PID > 0 ⇒ running
```

(see `pkg/machine/wsl/declares.go` `sysdpid`, used by `isSystemdRunning` / `isRunning` in `pkg/machine/wsl/machine.go`)

Modern machine images use **native WSL systemd**:

```ini
# /etc/wsl.conf inside podman-machine-default
[boot]
systemd=true
```

In that configuration, PID 1 typically appears as:

```text
/sbin/init                        1
```

(`/sbin/init` → `../lib/systemd/systemd`), **not** as a `cmd` line starting with `/lib/systemd/systemd`.

So the grep matches **nothing** → `State=stopped` forever while the distro is fine.

The bootstrap script still assumes an older nested-systemd model:

```bash
ps -ef | grep -v grep | grep -q systemd && exit 0
nohup unshare … /lib/systemd/systemd &
```

With `[boot] systemd=true`, nested systemd is unnecessary, but **Windows `State()` was never updated** to treat real PID1 systemd as running.

### Proof (guest)

```text
$ ps -eo cmd,pid | head -3
CMD                             PID
/sbin/init                        1
…

$ ps -eo cmd,pid | grep -m 1 ^/lib/systemd/systemd
# (no match)

$ systemctl is-system-running
running
```

### Workaround that confirms the diagnosis

Run a long-lived process with **argv0** exactly `/lib/systemd/systemd` and **no extra args** (so `awk '{print $2}'` is the PID), e.g.:

```bash
exec -a /lib/systemd/systemd /usr/bin/yes >/dev/null 2>&1
```

Then:

- `podman machine list` → **Currently running**
- `podman machine start` → **`unable to start …: already running`** (correct; does **not** reassign SSH)

## Root cause 2 — Start reassigns SSH under mirrored networking

With `%USERPROFILE%\.wslconfig`:

```ini
[wsl2]
networkingMode=mirrored
```

Guest sshd listening on e.g. `0.0.0.0:49613` is also visible on **Windows** `127.0.0.1:49613`.

`podman machine start` (believing the machine is stopped) logs:

```text
detected port conflict on machine ssh port [49613], reassigning
```

It rewrites guest `/etc/ssh/sshd_config` Port and machine JSON / connections to a **new** port, but often **does not align live sshd** (or health checks the new dead port). Result:

```text
API forwarding for Docker API clients is not available due to the following startup failures.
        could not start api proxy since expected pipe is not available: podman-machine-default
Podman clients are still able to connect.
Error: machine did not transition into running state: ssh error: machine not in running state
```

Connections then point at a port nothing listens on until manually re-pinned.
 


## Related issues (symptoms overlap; this report focuses on State() detection)

- https://github.com/containers/podman/issues/28341 — start failure, port reassignment, bootstrap/sshd races (closed as not planned; ARM64-framed)
- https://github.com/containers/podman/issues/22975 — mirrored networking + machine start / SSH
- https://github.com/containers/podman-desktop/issues/7588 — mirrored + Desktop



### Steps to reproduce the issue


1. Windows 11, WSL2, Podman 6.x Windows client, WSL machine `podman-machine-default` created via Desktop or CLI (rootful).
2. Optional but makes Start destructive: set `networkingMode=mirrored` in `.wslconfig`, `wsl --shutdown`, reboot stack.
3. Ensure guest has `[boot] systemd=true` (default on current machine images).
4. Start the WSL distro without a successful `podman machine start` lifecycle, e.g. cold boot then `wsl -d podman-machine-default -u root -- true`, or leave distro running after a previous partial start.
5. Observe:
   - `wsl -l -v` → `podman-machine-default` **Running**
   - `podman machine inspect` → **`State=stopped`** (without the argv0 shim)
6. Run `podman machine start` or click **Start** in Podman Desktop.
7. Observe port reassignment warning, exit 125, broken SSH URIs.

### Describe the results you received

* False stopped while distro + systemd + podman are healthy.
* Desktop Start / machine start reassigns SSH, breaks CLI and Desktop, exit 125.
* Named-pipe API proxy messages are secondary fallout.

### Describe the results you expected

1. `State()` / `machine list` report **running** when WSL distro is up and systemd is the system manager (PID1), regardless of whether `ps` shows `/sbin/init` or `/lib/systemd/systemd`.
2. If the machine is already effectively running, `machine start` is a no-op (or only starts missing host pieces like `win-sshproxy`), **without** reassigning SSH.
3. Under mirrored networking, a port already serving **this** machine’s sshd with the machine identity is **not** treated as a foreign conflict; if reassignment is required, **restart sshd** and wait until the new port listens before updating connections / health checks.

4. On Start when `State` becomes running but pipes missing: start `win-sshproxy` only, do not rewrite SSH.

https://github.com/podman-container-tools/podman/actions/runs/29762279833/job/88421964442

A few more: [07-22](https://github.com/podman-container-tools/podman/actions/runs/29951636314/job/89032377003), [07-21](https://github.com/podman-container-tools/podman/actions/runs/29804524375/job/88658986341), [07-08](https://github.com/podman-container-tools/podman/actions/runs/28966758980/job/85953987802), [06-24](https://github.com/podman-container-tools/podman/actions/runs/28107803418/job/83228584233).

I first assumed the 5s in `_check_health` was too short, but that is not it - the loop also runs `podman events` each iteration so it actually waited 10.3s here, and 13.7s in another job. What I cannot explain is the middle of that block: `FailingStreak` sits at 2 with the timer still `active running`, and with `--health-interval 1s` nothing new is recorded for ten seconds. I measured the interval elsewhere in these logs and it is fine, median 1.10s.

Is the healthcheck service expected to keep running after the check starts exiting non-zero? I have only the macOS client here so I could not reproduce it locally.

title: test/e2e: fix remaining hardcoded alpine_nginx reference in play_kube_test.go
body:
The "podman kube --quiet with error" test hardcoded
quay.io/libpod/alpine_nginx:latest directly inside a YAML string, which breaks
on non-amd64 architectures (#28272).

This instance was missed in commit cd2f122fb4, which fixed the same pattern in
five other tests in this file, because it used a raw inline literal rather than
the NGINX_IMAGE variable.

Switched to NGINX_IMAGE, which is already defined per architecture, so no skip is needed here.

#### Checklist

- [x] Certify you wrote the patch or otherwise have the right to pass it on as an open-source patch by signing all commits. (`git commit -s`)

- [x] [Documentation](https://github.com/containers/podman/blob/main/docs/README.md) has been updated (or no documentation changes are needed)
- [x] All commits pass `make validatepr` (format/lint checks)
- [x] [Release note](https://github.com/kubernetes/community/blob/master/contributors/guide/release-notes.md) entered in the section below (or `None` if no user-facing changes)

Note: ran `golangci-lint` v2.12.2 (`GOOS=linux`) against `./test/e2e/...` and `gofmt`, both clean. I wasn't able to run the full `make validatepr` container locally as I don't have podman installed on this machine.

I left Fixes: off intentionally; this doesn't close #28272 on its own. The default amd64 image is still single-arch; building an actual multi-arch image is separate work that's still open. This just routes the one remaining test through the same per-arch NGINX_IMAGE constant used everywhere else in the file.

body:
### Issue Description

When trying to run a container with the option `--userns keep-id` as a user that does not exist in `/etc/passwd`, the command fails.

### Steps to reproduce the issue

Steps to reproduce the issue
1. Setup NSS as user backend (e.g. LDAP).
2. Install rootless podman and add mappings in `/etc/subuid` and `/etc/subgid`.
3. Try to run a container with the `--userns keep-id` option.

The user does exist

```
$ getent passwd <username>
<username>:x:12000:12000:<name>,,,,<uuid>:/home/<username>:/bin/bash

body:
Docker Engine API [v1.44 ](https://docs.docker.com/reference/api/engine/version-history/#v144-api-changes) introduces a new field named `DNSNames` containing all non-fully qualified DNS names a container takes on a specific network for the `GET /containers/{name:.*}/json` endpoint.

- Populate `DNSNames` for the compat endpoints `GET /containers/json` and `GET /containers/{name:.*}/json` (the Docker changelog mentions only `/containers/{name:.*}/json`, but it's the same [moby structure](https://pkg.go.dev/github.com/moby/moby/api/types/network#EndpointSettings)).

body:
### Issue Description

I created a podman precreate hook to set some env vairbales. With `podman exec` I can not see them.


### Steps to reproduce the issue

Steps to reproduce the issue
1. Create a OCI hook
``` 
cat  /usr/share/containers/oci/hooks.d/test.json
{
  "version": "1.0.0",
  "hook": {
    "path": "/example.sh"
  },
  "when": {
    "always": true
  },
  "stages": [
    "precreate"
  ]
}
```
with 
``` 
cat /example.sh
#!/usr/bin/env bash
set -e

config=$(cat)


jq '.process.env += ["FOO=BAR"]' <<<"$config"
``` 

2. Create a container and check the env.
` podman run --rm  --name test   alpine  env` will give you `FOO=BAR`
but with `podman run --rm  --name test  -d alpine sleep infinity` and `podman exec test env`  this env is missing.





### Describe the results you received

The resulting config seems to be correct, it is in 
1.  `podman inspect test  | jq '.[0].Config.Env'`
2. also PID 1 has the env variable `podman exec test cat  /proc/1/environ  | tr "\0" "\n" `

It seems like the parent process ID of a exec is 0 and not 1 therefore my guess is, that the exec misses some env variable source

title: Goroutine leak in StartGenericAppleVM during podman machine start

labels.name: kind/bug

body:
### Issue Description

### **Description**

In `pkg/machine/apple/apple.go`, the `StartGenericAppleVM` function creates a channel (`term`) to listen for OS interrupt signals and launches a background goroutine to block on `<-term` and forward those signals to the VM process.

However, there is no cancellation mechanism (like a `done` channel) and no call to `signal.Stop(term)`. If the user starts the machine normally without sending an interrupt signal, this goroutine remains blocked on `<-term` indefinitely. This results in a leaked goroutine for every `podman machine start` invocation during the daemon's lifecycle.


### Steps to reproduce the issue

The signal-catching goroutine blocks on <-term forever because the channel is never closed and no alternative cancellation path exists once the VM successfully starts.

### Describe the results you expected

The goroutine should utilize a select statement with a done channel. Once the VM has successfully started (or failed to start), the caller should close the done channel to cleanly unblock and terminate the signal-forwarding goroutine.

title: hack/ci: let the fixed-skips check see issue numbers at end of line
body:
The check builds `#($issues)[^0-9]` and hands it to `grep -E`, so it needs a character after the issue number. grep strips the newline before matching, so when the number is the last thing on the line there is nothing for `[^0-9]` to match and the skip is invisible to the gate.

Most skips are unaffected because something usually follows, even just a closing quote. It is trailing comments that go missing. There are two in the tree right now that the gate cannot see, `test/system/500-networking.bats:266` referencing #11871 and `test/buildah-bud/apply-podman-deltas:335` referencing #25756, both closed. If someone opened a PR saying it fixed either one, the check would pass and the FIXME would stay.

`([^0-9]|$)` keeps the existing behaviour and adds the end of line case. I checked it still does not match #118710 when looking for #11871.

Added a case to `pr-removes-fixed-skips.t` for it. It passes with the change and fails without it.

The issue is caused by an off-by-one write after incrementing `nfiles`:

### Additional information

The heap-buffer-overflow is caused by the following code:

```c
buffer = realloc(buffer, (nfiles + 1) * (NAME_MAX + 1));

...

strncpy(buffer + nfiles * (NAME_MAX + 1),
        de->d_name,
        NAME_MAX + 1);

nfiles++;
buffer[nfiles * (NAME_MAX + 1)] = '\0';
```

`realloc()` allocates space for exactly `(nfiles + 1)` entries of size
`NAME_MAX + 1` bytes.

For the first file (`nfiles == 0`), the allocation size is 256 bytes
(assuming `NAME_MAX == 255`), with valid indices in the range `[0, 255]`.

After copying the filename, `nfiles` is incremented:

```c
nfiles++;
```

The subsequent write

```c
buffer[nfiles * (NAME_MAX + 1)] = '\0';
```

becomes

```c
buffer[256] = '\0';
```

which writes one byte past the end of the allocated buffer.

This extra write also appears to be unnecessary. According to the POSIX
specification, `readdir()` returns a null-terminated filename in
`dirent::d_name` whose length does not exceed `NAME_MAX`. Therefore,

```c
strncpy(buffer + nfiles * (NAME_MAX + 1),
        de->d_name,
        NAME_MAX + 1);
```

already copies the terminating `'\0'` into the destination buffer.

If the intention was to append an additional empty sentinel entry after the
last filename, the allocation should reserve space for one more
`NAME_MAX + 1` byte slot. Otherwise, the explicit null-byte write should be
removed.

This issue was found during internal security testing at ALT Linux Team.

title: Goroutine and FD leak in REST API HTTPAttach due to dropped request context

labels.name: kind/bug
labels.description: Categorizes issue or PR as related to a bug.

body:
### Issue Description

In `libpod/oci_conmon_common.go`, the `HTTPAttach` method receives an active `http.Request` from the client connection. However, when it calls `ctr.ReadLog` to stream the container logs, it passes `context.Background()` instead of the request's context (`req.Context()`).

Because `context.Background()` is immortal, if the API client disconnects or the HTTP request is abruptly cancelled, the `ReadLog` goroutine and its underlying file-tail loop are never interrupted. This results in a goroutine and file descriptor leak for every detached or dropped `podman attach` session over the REST API.

### Steps to reproduce the issue

1. Start a long-running container in the background.
2. Initiate an HTTP attach/log-streaming session to the running container via the Podman REST API.
3. Abruptly drop the client connection (e.g., kill the client process or drop the network connection).
4. Monitor the Podman daemon/service processes and observe that the underlying `ReadLog` goroutines and file descriptors do not terminate, leaking resources.

### Describe the results you received

The underlying `ReadLog` process does not terminate when the HTTP client disconnects because it is bound to `context.Background()`. This leads to a persistent goroutine and file descriptor leak.

### Describe the results you expected

`ctr.ReadLog` should be called with `req.Context()` so that the log-reading goroutine correctly receives a cancellation signal and shuts down when the client disconnects

labels.name: No New Tests

body:
This PR updates several `fmt.Errorf` calls in `libpod/healthcheck.go` and `libpod/events.go` from `%v` to `%w`.

Errors returned in the healthcheck timer path and events inspect data were formatted with `%v`, discarding the error chain. Replaced with `%w` so callers can use `errors.Is`/`errors.As` to inspect the underlying causes. 

As stated in the official Go standard library documentation for `fmt.Errorf`, "If the format specifier includes a %w verb with an error operand, the returned error will implement an Unwrap method returning the operand". Furthermore, error wrapping was introduced in Go 1.13 to allow developers to add context to errors while preserving the original error for inspection.

title: pkg/machine/env: add test coverage for the machine dir path helpers
body:
`pkg/machine/env` builds the filesystem paths used by `podman machine`, but has
no unit tests. A couple of its helpers are pure and worth pinning down:

- `WithPodmanPrefix` prepends `podman-` only when the name does not already start
  with `podman` — so `machine` → `podman-machine`, but `podman-machine`,
  `podman`, and even `podmanx` are left unchanged. This is subtle and easy to
  regress.
- `DataDirPrefix` / `ConfDirPrefix` return the machine data/config path prefix,
  which should end with `containers/podman/machine`.

Add unit tests for these. Pure-Go, no behaviour change; `go test ./pkg/machine/env/`
passes (runs natively, no VM needed).

title: auth: fix remote permission denied flake during authfile parsing

labels.name: kind/api-change
labels.description: Change to remote API; merits scrutiny

body:
fixes - #27455 

### Description
In parallel GitHub Actions CI environments, the system tests are run inside a guest Lima VM. `limactl` by default forwards the host's `TMPDIR` into the VM.

Because the host temp directory is mounted inside the VM with host owner constraints (owned by the host's `runner` user), guest processes running under different UIDs/guest users (e.g. `root`, `lima`, or container processes) hit `EACCES` (Permission Denied) when trying to write to the shared host directory (such as creating temporary auth files in `GetCredentials`).

This PR fixes the issue by unsetting/resetting `TMPDIR` and `BATS_TMPDIR` to the local guest `/tmp` directory at the start of `hack/ci/runner.sh`, and preserving them under `sudo`. This guarantees that all guest commands use the VM's local world-writable `/tmp` directory, preventing any host-guest permission conflicts.

title: test/system: fix random_rfc1918_subnet operator precedence
body:
I was poking at the network system tests and noticed random_rfc1918_subnet does not actually return an rfc1918 address.

In bash arithmetic + binds tighter than &, so 16 + $RANDOM & 15 is really (16 + RANDOM) & 15, which gives 0..15 rather than 16..31. So the helper has been returning 172.0.x through 172.15.x, none of which is inside 172.16/12. Looks like it came in with 9e3363c5e when % 16 became & 15.

Nothing caught it because subnet_in_use only checks whether the subnet clashes with a host route, not whether it is private, so the tests carry on passing either way.

I added a regression test to helpers.t. I ran it both ways in a container - it reports "saw 0..15" and fails on the old expression, "saw 16..31" and passes on the new one. I could not run the actual system tests here though, so that part is down to CI.

title: compat: report cgroup driver "none" when rootless with cgroupfs

labels.name: kind/api-change
labels.description: Change to remote API; merits scrutiny

body:
Rootless Podman with the cgroupfs manager cannot create a cgroup parent outside its delegated subtree, and container creation already leaves it unset (`libpod/runtime_ctr.go:412`). Compat `/info` still reports `cgroupfs` though, so buildx pins its BuildKit container to `/docker/buildx` and crun fails:

```
crun: create `/sys/fs/cgroup/docker`: Permission denied: OCI permission denied
```

Rootless dockerd reports `none`, never `cgroupfs` (`cgroupDriver` in moby `daemon/daemon_unix.go`). This does the same.

Repro without Docker involved:

```
podman --cgroup-manager=cgroupfs run --rm alpine true                                  # works
podman --cgroup-manager=cgroupfs run --rm --cgroup-parent=/docker/buildx alpine true   # fails
```

With the same buildx client against a rootless service, `HostConfig.CgroupParent` on the buildkit container goes from `/docker/buildx` to empty.

Fixes #27824

title: podman build in 6.0.x no longer honors `env` and `http_proxy` in `containers.conf`

labels.name: kind/bug
labels.description: Categorizes issue or PR as related to a bug.

body:
### Issue Description

After upgrading Podman from `5.8.3` to `6.0.x`, `podman build` no longer honors the `http_proxy = false` directive and custom `env` settings configured in `containers.conf`. Instead, it always inherits host shell proxy environment variables (e.g. `http_proxy=http://127.0.0.1:1080`) unless the opposite option (`--http-proxy=false`) is explicitly passed on the CLI.

#### Setup & Context
I have a proxy service running on my local host machine, and in my shell environment I have:
```bash
export http_proxy=http://127.0.0.1:1080
```

Because I can't pass `127.0.0.1` to a container as a proxy environment variable (since `127.0.0.1` inside a container refers to the container's loopback interface where no proxy is running), I work around this by having the following `containers.conf` configuration:
```toml
[containers]
http_proxy = false
env = [
  "http_proxy=http://host.containers.internal:1080"
]
```

Before 6.0.x, the behavior between `podman run` and `podman build` was consistent with this `containers.conf` configuration. However, this is no longer the case in 6.0.x—`podman build` ignores `containers.conf`, causing build steps to inherit `127.0.0.1:1080` from the host shell and fail with connection refused errors.


### Steps to reproduce the issue

1. Set up host shell proxy environment variable:
   ```bash
   export http_proxy=http://127.0.0.1:1080
   ```

2. Configure `~/.config/containers/containers.conf`:
   ```toml
   [containers]
   http_proxy = false
   env = [
     "http_proxy=http://host.containers.internal:1080"
   ]
   ```

3. Compare `podman run` vs `podman build`:
   ```bash
   # Test podman run:
   podman run --rm alpine env | grep -i proxy

   # Test podman build:
   podman build --no-cache -f - . << 'EOF'
   FROM alpine
   RUN env | grep -i proxy
   EOF
   ```


### Describe the results you received

`podman run --rm alpine env | grep -i proxy` correctly prints:
```
http_proxy=http://host.containers.internal:1080
```

Whereas `podman build` prints:
```
http_proxy=http://127.0.0.1:1080
```

`podman run` honors `containers.conf` (`http_proxy = false` and `env = [...]`), properly setting `http://host.containers.internal:1080`.
In contrast, `podman build` ignores `containers.conf` and inherits `127.0.0.1:1080` directly from the host shell, causing network requests during build `RUN` steps (e.g. `RUN apk update`) to fail with connection refused errors against `127.0.0.1:1080`.


### Describe the results you expected

With `http_proxy = false` and custom proxy `env` configured in `containers.conf`, `podman build` should honor `http_proxy = false` to disable host `127.0.0.1` proxy passthrough, while applying `[containers] env` settings (`http_proxy=http://host.containers.internal:1080`) transiently during build `RUN` steps without leaking proxy environment variables into committed image metadata (`ENV` directives) (which was the behavior in 5.8.x and consistent with `podman run`).

title: docs: clarify --transient-store behavior with volumes
body:
The `--transient-store` documentation didn't explain what happens to volumes, leading users to expect that volume data would also be transient. In practice only the Podman database (container and volume metadata) is stored on non-persistent media, volume data on disk persists across reboots. After a reboot the volumes disappear from `podman volume ls` because their database entries are gone, but the data stays on disk and gets silently reused if a volume with the same name is created again.

This updates the `--transient-store` section in `podman.1.md` to document this behavior, point users to `podman system prune --external` for cleaning up orphaned volume data, and note that the option is designed for Quadlet use and should not be mixed with regular non-transient commands.

- Fixes: #25295

title: test: fix cgroups=split flake by adding Delegate=yes to scope
body:
The `cgroups=split` e2e test wraps podman in `systemd-run --scope` but doesn't pass `Delegate=yes`. w/o explicit delegation, systemd cant guarantee that cgroup controllers like `pids` are written to `cgroup.subtree_control` for child cgroups so, whether they show up depends on the systemd session state at that moment, so the test flakes instead of failing consistently. when `--cgroups=split` runs, crun creates the container payload cgroup directly under the scope and expects all controllers to be available there; without delegation they sometimes aren't.

This adds `--property=Delegate=yes` to the `systemd-run` wrapper, matching what Quadlet already does (`Delegate=yes` in the `[Service]` section) whenever it generates a unit for `--cgroups=split`.

title: Fix deferred event emission on failed container update

labels.name: No New Tests
labels.description: Allow PR to proceed without adding regression tests

body:
## Summary

In `libpod/container_api.go`, `Container.Update()` defers emission of the `events.Update` event before invoking `c.update()`:

```go
defer c.newContainerEvent(events.Update)
return c.update(updateOptions)
```

Because deferred functions execute regardless of whether the function returns successfully or with an error, an `Update` event is emitted even when `c.update()` fails.


## Problem

If `c.update(updateOptions)` returns an error (for example, due to invalid options, storage failures, or permission issues), the deferred event is still emitted.

This means an `events.Update` notification may be generated even though the container update did not complete successfully.

## Possible Impact

Depending on how `events.Update` is consumed, this may lead to:

- Event streams indicating an update that never completed.
- Audit logs or monitoring systems observing an update event for a failed operation.
- Consumers having to infer success or failure from additional context instead of the event itself.

## Proposed Fix

Emit the event only after `c.update()` completes successfully:

```go
if err := c.update(updateOptions); err != nil {
    return err
}

c.newContainerEvent(events.Update)
return nil
```

This ensures that `events.Update` is emitted only for successful container updates.

title: libpod: fix exec --user not resolving supplementary groups
body:
`getUserOverrides()` checks `c.state.BindMounts["/etc/passwd"]` to find the passwd file Podman generates at container start, but never had the matching check for `/etc/group`. Exec sessions therefore resolved supplementary groups from the static image rootfs instead of the bind-mounted file. Adding the missing lookup fixes that

In its own, though, that would have broken `--group-add`. `lookup.Overrides.ContainerEtcGroupPath` is an already-resolved host path which is how `GetUserGroupInfo()` has always treated it but `GetContainerGroups()` securejoined it onto the container mount point, producing a path that doesn't exist. That was mostly harmless while the override was only set for explicit `/etc/group` (or `/etc`) bind mounts. Once it's populated for the generated `/etc/group`, `podman run --group-add somegroup` fails with `unable to find group somegroup`. both helpers now agree on what the field means

an e2e case for `exec --user` resolving supplementary groups, plus a unit test in `pkg/lookup` that fails with the old securejoin behaviour.

- Related: #29170

title: docs: document keep-groups limitation with systemd services
body:
This PR documents a limitation with `--group-add keep-groups` (and Quadlet's `GroupAdd=keep-groups`) where supplementary groups are inherited directly from the calling process. When Podman runs as a systemd user service, `crun` inherits groups from `systemd --user`, which only holds the groups present when that session was initially started. If a user is added to new groups via `usermod` after the systemd session started, those groups aren't retroactively picked up, so they won't be passed into the container. This updates the documentation for both CLI options and Quadlets to clarify this behavior and mention that restarting the user's systemd manager (`loginctl terminate-user <user>`) resolves it.

- Fixes: #27876

title: ci: cache Go module/build caches and build binaries in Lima VM
body:
fixes - #28886 

#### Summary
Set up proper caching of Go module and build caches for Podman CI runs inside the Lima VM, and resolve the issue of `make` rebuilding binaries due to out-of-date timestamps on downloaded build artifacts in subsequent test jobs.

**Key Changes:**
1. **GitHub Workflows (`lima.yml`)**: Restores and saves Go build/module caches on the runner host using `actions/cache` before VM boot. Uncommented artifact download and upload steps to share the `bin/` directory between build and test tasks.
2. **Ignored directories (`.gitignore`)**: Added `/.gocache/` and `/.gomodcache/` so they are not tracked or reported as dirty files by git.
3. **CI environment setup (`ci.sh`)**: Touched all precompiled binaries in `/var/tmp/podman/bin` using `find` to update their modification times to the current time, preventing `make` from rebuilding them inside the VM. Standardized permissions of cache directories inside the VM, and copied `.gocache` and `.gomodcache` back to the host via `limactl copy`. Uncommented copying build binaries out of the VM for build tasks.
4. **Go Cache Environment (`runner.sh`)**: Exported `GOCACHE` and `GOMODCACHE` to point to `/var/tmp/podman/.gocache` and `/var/tmp/podman/.gomodcache` inside the VM, and added them to `PRESERVE_ENVS` to ensure that `sudo` invocations of test builders preserve these caches.

title: pkg/channel: add tests for the channel WriteCloser
body:
Adds unit tests for pkg/channel, which had no test coverage. The channel WriteCloser proxies each Write onto a chan []byte; the tests cover message queueing, the defensive buffer copy, ordering, Chan(), Close closing the channel, write-after-close failing, and the nil-receiver guard.

Pure test-only change, no behavior change. go test -race ./pkg/channel/ passes all

Fixes: #29281

title: pkg/channel: add test coverage for the channel WriteCloser
body:
`pkg/channel` provides a small `io.WriteCloser` (`writeCloser`) that proxies
each `Write` call onto a `chan []byte` as one message. It currently has no unit
tests despite a few behaviours worth pinning down:

- `Write` queues each buffer as a single channel message and returns `len(b)`.
- `Write` makes a defensive copy, so mutating the caller's slice after `Write`
  does not change the queued message.
- `Write` on a nil receiver returns an error pointing at `channel.NewWriter()`.
- `Close` closes the channel; a subsequent `Write` fails with
  "the channel is closed for Write".

Add table/behaviour unit tests covering these. Pure-Go, no behaviour change,
`go test ./pkg/channel/` passes all

fixes - [#28870](https://github.com/podman-container-tools/podman/issues/28870)

title: libpod: do not fail prune when build container is already gone

labels.name: No New Tests
labels.description: Allow PR to proceed without adding regression tests

body:
podman system prune --build lists the containers first, then works through them one at a time. A build that got killed is still cleaning up its own stage containers in the background, so one can disappear in between.

When that happened the prune bailed out with exit 125 and "identifier is not a container", even though the container was already gone, which is what we wanted anyway. So treat ErrContainerUnknown and ErrNotAContainer as success there.

I could not reproduce the flake locally, this is worked out from the log in the issue. No test either, I could not see a way to hit the race on purpose.

Seen in #28868, though from the discussion here that flake is really about the server side build not stopping when the remote client is killed, which is what nalind is fixing in buildah#7007.

#### Does this PR introduce a user-facing change?

```release-note
Fixed `podman system prune --build` failing when a build container was removed while the prune was already running.
```

title: Libpod/compat API RestartContainer defaults to 0 second timeout, overriding container StopTimeout

labels.name: kind/bug
labels.description: Categorizes issue or PR as related to a bug.

body:
### Issue Description

When using the compat API (e.g. `podman compose` with the `docker-compose` backend) the `restart` command ignores the container's `StopTimeout` value, replacing it with 0 if the caller did not specify a value. This results in containers being killed with an immediate `SIGKILL`. The `stop` command works as expected.

[containers_stop.go](https://github.com/podman-container-tools/podman/blob/e36e1a41c69ea9f6096ed628a71920f315f34514/pkg/api/handlers/compat/containers_stop.go#L42-L52) only sets `options.Timeout` from `query` (where values default to 0) if the argument appears to have been specified, [containers_restart.go](https://github.com/podman-container-tools/podman/blob/e36e1a41c69ea9f6096ed628a71920f315f34514/pkg/api/handlers/compat/containers_restart.go#L40-L46) instead sets `options.Timeout` from `query` fields without regard to whether the caller had set them.

### Steps to reproduce the issue

Steps to reproduce the issue
1. Write the following compose file:
```
services:
  test:
    image: docker.io/library/busybox
    command: sh -c "sleep inf"
```
2. Run compose (e.g. `podman compose -f compose.yaml up`)
3. In another shell, determine the PID of `sh` running inside the container. Then trace it using `strace -p $PID_HERE`
4. In another shell, use compose to restart the container (e.g. `podman compose -f compose.yaml restart test`)

### Describe the results you received

`strace` indicates the process was `killed by SIGKILL` immediately, without ever receiving `SIGTERM`.

### Describe the results you expected

The process should first receieve `SIGTERM` (`sleep` doesn't seem to exit on `SIGTERM`, so `SIGKILL` should be sent only after a delay)

title: Remove unnecessary length check for container hostname ID
body:
**Summary**

Since container IDs are validated to always be exactly 64 characters long upon creation, the `< 11` length check when determining the short ID hostname is dead code. 

This PR removes the unnecessary boundary check and unconditionally returns the truncated 12-character ID `c.ID()[:12]`.

### Issue Description


The `--detach-keys` flag help text for `podman exec` is inconsistent with `podman run`, `podman start`, and `podman attach`.

- `podman exec --help` describes only a single character or a single `ctrl-<value>`.
- It lists allowed ctrl values as `a-z, @, ^, [, , or _` (double comma, and missing `\` and `]`).
- `podman run`, `podman start`, and `podman attach` correctly document **comma-separated** sequences (e.g. `ctrl-p,ctrl-q`).

However, `podman exec` **does accept** comma-separated detach keys in practice, so the help text is misleading.

The flag description is defined in `cmd/podman/containers/exec.go` and should match `cmd/podman/containers/run.go`.



### Steps to reproduce the issue

 1. Compare help text across commands:
  ```bash
   podman exec --help | grep detach-keys
   podman run --help | grep detach-keys
   podman attach --help | grep detach-keys
   ```

2. Confirm comma-separated detach keys work on exec despite help not documenting them:
   ```bash
   cid=$(podman run -d docker.io/library/alpine sleep 120)
   podman exec --detach-keys='ctrl-a,ctrl-b' $cid echo success
   podman rm -f $cid
   ```

### Describe the results you received

**Exec help:**
```
--detach-keys string     Select the key sequence for detaching a container. Format is a single character [a-Z] or ctrl-<value> where <value> is one of: a-z, @, ^, [, , or _ (default "ctrl-p,ctrl-q")
```

**Run help (for comparison):**
```
--detach-keys [a-Z]   Override the key sequence for detaching a container. Format is a single character [a-Z] or a comma separated sequence of `ctrl-<value>`, where <value> is one of: `a-cf`, `@`, `^`, `[`, `\`, `]`, `^` or `_` (default "ctrl-p,ctrl-q")
```

Exec help omits comma-separated sequences and has an incomplete/incorrect character list, but:
```bash
podman exec --detach-keys='ctrl-a,ctrl-b' $cid echo success
# prints: success
```


### Describe the results you expected

`podman exec --detach-keys` help text should match `podman run` / `podman attach` / `podman start` and document comma-separated `ctrl-<value>` sequences.

title: compat: support digests parameter in /images/json endpoint

labels.name: kind/api-change
labels.description: Change to remote API; merits scrutiny

body:
When using the Docker-compat endpoint /images/json with the digests query parameter set to true, the server returned an empty response body with HTTP 200 status. This was caused by an early return that logged the unsupported parameter without writing any HTTP response.

In Docker's API, the digests parameter controls whether RepoDigests is included in the response. Podman already populates RepoDigests for every image in the normal listing path, so the fix is simply to remove the blocking early return and let the request proceed normally. No additional logic is needed since the digest information is already exposed through the RepoDigests field.

Closes #29210

title: [replaced] compat: return HTTP 400 when digests parameter is passed to /images/json

labels.name: kind/api-change
labels.description: Change to remote API; merits scrutiny

body:
When using the Docker-compat endpoint `/images/json` with the `digests` query parameter set to `true`, the server returned an empty response body with HTTP 200 status. This was caused by `utils.UnSupportedParameter` only logging an info message without writing any HTTP response, so the early return left the client with a 200 and no body.

This fix replaces the silent log call with a proper HTTP 400 Bad Request error response, matching the behavior expected by Docker-compatible clients. The digest information is already exposed through the `RepoDigests` field in the normal response, so there is no need to support the parameter separately.

Closes #29210

title: Fix remote podman start silently ignoring missing containers with --f…
body:
Fix remote podman start silently ignoring missing containers with filter

ContainerStart incorrectly passed len(options.Filters) > 0 as the ignore flag to getContainersAndInputByContext. Nonexistent container names were skipped instead of returning an error on remote clients.

## Summary

Remote podman start treated any use of `--filter` as ignore mode when resolving explicit container names. A typo or missing name exited 0 with no message on Windows, macOS, and podman remote. Local podman returned exit 125 with a no such container error.

This PR passes false for ignore in ContainerStart, matching ContainerRestart and local behavior.

## Test plan

Added e2e test podman start --filter with nonexistent container name in test/e2e/start_test.go

Manual check on Windows Podman 5.8.5

```
podman create --name testctr-filterbug alpine sleep 3600
podman start --filter name=testctr-filterbug nonexistent-container-xyz123
```

Before the fix exit 0 and no output. After the fix exit 125 and no such container error.

Replace ISSUE_NUMBER with your GitHub issue number before opening the PR.

Fixes containers/podman#29266

title: podman-remote start --filter silently succeeds when container name does not exist

labels.name: kind/bug
labels.description: Categorizes issue or PR as related to a bug.

labels.name: remote
labels.description: Problem is in podman-remote

labels.name: windows
labels.description: issue/bug on Windows

body:
### Issue Description

When using `podman start` (or `podman-remote start`) with a `--filter` and an explicit container name/ID that **does not exist**, the command exits with code **0** and produces **no output or error message**.

This is incorrect. The same command without `--filter` correctly returns exit code **125** with an error like `no container with name or ID "..." found: no such container`.

This affects the **remote/tunnel** code path used by:

- Windows Podman (via Podman Machine)
- macOS Podman (via Podman Machine)
- `podman --remote` / `podman-remote` against a system service

Local Podman (Linux ABI path) behaves correctly and returns an error.

**Root cause (suspected):** In `pkg/domain/infra/tunnel/containers.go`, `ContainerStart` passes `len(options.Filters) > 0` as the `ignore` parameter to `getContainersAndInputByContext()`. When `ignore` is true, missing containers are silently skipped instead of returning an error. Other commands such as `ContainerRestart` pass `false` for this parameter.

### Steps to reproduce the issue


1. Ensure Podman Machine is running (Windows/macOS) or start a Podman system service (Linux remote testing):

   ```bash
   podman machine start
   ```

2. Create a test container:

   ```bash
   podman create --name testctr-filterbug docker.io/library/alpine:latest sleep 3600
   ```

3. Run start with a **nonexistent** container name **without** a filter (baseline — works correctly):

   ```bash
   podman start nonexistent-container-xyz123
   echo exit:$?
   ```

4. Run start with a **nonexistent** container name **with** a filter (bug):

   ```bash
   podman start --filter name=testctr-filterbug nonexistent-container-xyz123
   echo exit:$?
   ```

5. Optional - compare with local Podman on Linux (no `--remote`), same commands. Local returns 125 for step 4; remote exits 0 silently.

**Alternative remote reproducer (Linux + system service):**

```bash
podman system service --time=0 unix:///tmp/podman-test.sock &
export CONTAINER_HOST=unix:///tmp/podman-test.sock
podman create --name testctr-filterbug docker.io/library/alpine:latest sleep 3600
podman --remote start --filter name=testctr-filterbug nonexistent-container-xyz123
echo exit:$?

### Describe the results you received


**Without filter (step 3):**

```
Error: no container with name or ID "nonexistent-container-xyz123" found: no such container
exit:125
```

**With filter (step 4) — bug:**

```
(no output)
exit:0
```

Verified on:

- **Windows 11**, Podman **5.8.5**, Podman Machine (WSL2, rootless)
- **WSL Ubuntu 24.04**, Podman **4.9.3**, `podman --remote` via system service socket

---

### Describe the results you expected

When a user specifies a container name/ID that does not exist, `podman start` should fail regardless of whether `--filter` is also used:

```
Error: no container with name or ID "nonexistent-container-xyz123" found: no such container
exit:125
```

**Note:** Silent exit 0 when an **existing** container does not match the filter (e.g. `podman start --filter status=running mystoppedcontainer`) appears to be intentional and is covered by existing e2e tests. This report is only about **nonexistent** container names.


### podman info output

```yaml

  Built: 1783536053

  GitCommit: 6d48b6f12f793176f3f6bc808b5a440984c14eb2

  cpus: 10

      crun version 1.28

```

### Podman in a container

No

### Privileged Or Rootless

Rootless

### Upstream Latest Release

Yes

### Additional environment details

- **Host OS:** Microsoft Windows 11 Home (10.0.26200), amd64
- **CPU:** 11th Gen Intel Core i5-11400H
- **Podman Machine:** WSL2 backend, Fedora 44 container VM
- **Install method:** Official Windows MSI installer (`podman-installer-windows-amd64.msi`, v5.8.5)


### Additional information

- **Affected code:** `pkg/domain/infra/tunnel/containers.go` line ~793 — `ContainerStart` passes `len(options.Filters) > 0` as the `ignore` argument to `getContainersAndInputByContext()`.
- **Related FIXME:** `pkg/domain/infra/tunnel/helpers.go` lines 15–17 notes the `ignore` parameter is likely misused.
- **Comparison:** `ContainerRestart` in the same file passes `false` for `ignore` and does not exhibit this bug for missing names.
- **Impact:** Scripts and automation that check exit codes will treat a failed start as success when `--filter` is combined with a typo'd or missing container name. Especially affects Windows/macOS users where all CLI commands use the remote client path.
- **Suggested fix:** Pass `false` instead of `len(options.Filters) > 0` for the `ignore` parameter in `ContainerStart`, and add a remote e2e/system test asserting exit 125 for `start --filter <valid-filter> <nonexistent-name>`.

title: LFX Mentorship Program: Agentic CI Flake Categorization and Analysis
body:
## Description
Continuous Integration (CI) pipelines are the backbone of our development, but "flaky" tests—tests that exhibit both false positive and false negative outcomes randomly—severely degrade developer velocity and erode trust in the CI system.
Currently, our project relies on GitHub Actions for its CI/CD processes. Manually digging through extensive GitHub Actions logs to identify, categorize, and troubleshoot these flaky failures is a massive, time-consuming burden for maintainers.
This internship aims to solve this by building an intelligent, automated toolchain that monitors our GitHub Actions workflows for flaky behavior and leverages an agentic AI workflow to handle the heavy lifting of analysis. The intern will build a system that automatically extracts failing logs, uses AI agents to reason about the failure (differentiating between infrastructure blips, race conditions, network timeouts, etc.), and surfaces actionable mitigation strategies directly to the maintainers.

## Expected Outcomes
Data Ingestion Pipeline: A mechanism to automatically fetch, filter, and parse flaky CI run data and logs directly from the GitHub Actions API.
Agentic Analysis Engine: An integration with an AI/LLM framework designed to read failure logs, categorize the root cause of the flake, and generate a plain-English analysis.
Mitigation & Reporting: A reporting layer that takes the agent's findings and seamlessly integrates them into the developer workflow (e.g., auto-generating GitHub Issues, compiling weekly flake reports, or posting PR comments with suggested fixes).
Documentation: Comprehensive documentation covering the architecture of the tool, how to deploy it, and how maintainers can tweak the agent's prompts and behaviors.

## Recommended Skills
Proficiency in Python or Go (for scripting and API interactions).
Familiarity with GitHub Actions, CI/CD concepts, and log analysis.
Interest or experience in Generative AI, LLMs, and agentic workflows (prompt engineering, AI tool calling).
Experience with the GitHub API is a strong plus.
Familiarity with Local AI is a plus

title: Ensure log level is applied before loading configuration
body:
Podman loads its configuration during global initialization, before the `--log-level` option is processed. As a result, debug and trace messages emitted while reading configuration files are suppressed, making invalid or unknown configuration keys difficult to diagnose.

This change applies the requested log level before configuration initialization, ensuring that configuration-loading diagnostics are visible when commands are executed with `--log-level=debug` or `--log-level=trace`.

Fixes: #25362

### Feature request description

Currently #25902 handles using templated volumes [doc](https://docs.podman.io/en/latest/markdown/podman-systemd.unit.5.html#referencing-other-template-quadlets), however, that is not very dynamic.
We would have to create a new volume template for config, data, cache, etc...

I would like to support `Volume=volume@volume-name.volume:/path`.

### Suggest potential solution

I want to create a single volume template:
```ini
[Unit]
Description=Volume for %I
Documentation=https://docs.podman.io/en/stable/markdown/podman-systemd.unit.5.html#volume-units-volume

[Volume]
# Troubleshoot generation with:

[Service]

[Install]
# Rootful
WantedBy=multi-user.target
# Rootless
# WantedBy=default.target
```

Then in my `.container`, I can call it dynamically such as:
```ini
Volume=volume@%N-config.volume:/config
Volume=volume@%N-data.volume:/data
Volume=volume@%N-cache.volume:/cache
```

Using `%N` is another issue as currently Quadlet does not like that in my testing, but I believe that can be resolved in #29113.

### Have you considered any alternatives?

Alternatively, I would need to define `volume-data@.volume`, `volume-config@.volume`, etc...
And any one-off volumes would need to be defined manually.

title: pasta networking breaks with passt 2026_07_16 snapshot on Podman 6.0.1 (regression from 2026_01_20)

labels.name: kind/bug
labels.description: Categorizes issue or PR as related to a bug.

labels.name: pasta
labels.description: pasta(1) bugs or features

body:
### Issue Description

I run rootless Podman 6.0.1 (released 2026-07-07) on Ubuntu 26.04, using pasta for networking (default rootless backend). My distro-packaged passt/pasta was from the 2026_01_20.386b5f5 snapshot.

Today I built passt from the (most recent) official 2026_07_16.090d739 source tarball (https://passt.top/passt/snapshot/passt-2026_07_16.090d739.tar), packaged it as a .deb, and installed it in place of the older build. After this upgrade, pasta/passt networking for my Podman containers started failing. Containers that were running stayed running, but those that were stopped couldn't restart with the new pasta/passt with the following error message - 
```
Error: pasta failed with exit code 1:

Couldn't open network namespace /run/user/1000/netns/netns-67ad4bef-95e8-f72e-ec61-eb62abf96884: Permission denied
```
I stopped all containers and networks, rebooted the computer, and started up the networks and then tried to start up the containers again.  Same error.

Reverting to the 2026_01_20.386b5f5 build restored normal operation without needing a reboot or needing to restart .networks.  I haven't tried the June 2026 pasta/passt version on passt.top yet to see if this worked or throws a similar error.

Podman 6.0.1 was released before the 2026_07_16 passt snapshot existed, so it's possible this newer passt build changed something in the fd-passing/isolation contract that Podman's pasta invocation relies on, that Podman 6.0.1 wasn't tested against. I haven't yet bisected the exact commit between the January and July snapshots responsible but over the past 1-2 weeks the git commits on passt alludes to changes in fd.

### Steps to reproduce the issue

Steps to reproduce the issue
1. download July 2026 passt from passt.top
2. compile it
3. replace older pasta/passt with the july 2026 version
4. stop running containers and try to restart


### Describe the results you received

```
Error: pasta failed with exit code 1:

Couldn't open network namespace /run/user/1000/netns/netns-67ad4bef-95e8-f72e-ec61-eb62abf96884: Permission denied
```

I expected the container to start up normally

title: Podman-remote 6+ non-functional inside a Flatpak sandbox

labels.name: kind/bug
labels.description: Categorizes issue or PR as related to a bug.

labels.name: remote
labels.description: Problem is in podman-remote
Breaking changes for Podman 6.0

labels.name: triaged
labels.description: Issue has been triaged

body:
### Issue Description

`podman-remote` 6+ crashes when run inside a Flatpak sandbox. I'm using it to access the host's Podman engine.

The root cause seems to be the check added in https://github.com/podman-container-tools/podman/commit/e860773c0d9d3a9cbe8637ed459bf7e68e257a57 which crashes the CLI when Cgroups v2 is not mounted locally. The Flatpak sandbox does not mount `/sys/fs/cgroup` ([cite](https://docs.flatpak.org/en/latest/sandbox-permissions.html#reserved-paths)).

### Steps to reproduce the issue

```bash
flatpak run --filesystem=host --filesystem=xdg-run/podman \
  --command=$(realpath .../podman-remote) <any Flatpak app> ps
```

Or, using an explicit `bwrap` command:
```bash
bwrap --ro-bind "$HOME" "$HOME" \
  --bind /run /run \
  --proc /proc --dev /dev \
  --unshare-all --die-with-parent \
  "$HOME"/.../podman-remote ps
```


### Describe the results you received

```
FATA[0000] Error determining cgroups mode
```

### Describe the results you expected

The same output as a normal `podman ps`:
```
$ podman ps
CONTAINER ID  IMAGE       COMMAND     CREATED     STATUS      PORTS       NAMES
...
```

Or an error message of the form:
```
Cannot connect to Podman. Please verify your connection to the Linux system using `podman system connection list`, or try `podman machine init` and `podman machine start` to manage a new Linux VM
Error: unable to connect to Podman socket: Get "http://d/v6.0.1/libpod/_ping": dial unix /run/user/.../podman/podman.sock: connect: connection refused
```

title: .conf file is not picked up from `%APPDATA%\containers\containers.conf.d` folder on Windows

labels.name: kind/bug
labels.description: Categorizes issue or PR as related to a bug.

labels.name: remote
labels.description: Problem is in podman-remote

labels.name: windows
labels.description: issue/bug on Windows

body:
### Issue Description

`%APPDATA%\containers\` resolves to `C:\Users\<username>\AppData\Roaming\containers` on my machine.

devcontainers often have file permission issues on my machine which I have to work around with
```json
"runArgs": [
    "--userns=keep-id"
],
```

In order to keep my `devcontainer.json` files independent of the container engine (compatibility with docker), I want to put that in a separate podman configuration file.

I created `%APPDATA%\containers\containers.conf.d\1-userns-keep-id.conf` with the following content:
```toml
[containers]
userns = "keep-id"
```

After restarting the podman machine, my devcontainers still only work properly with the runArgs in the `devcontainer.json` file - it does not seem to pick up the setting from the .conf file.

### Steps to reproduce the issue

Steps to reproduce the issue
1. Create `%APPDATA%\containers\containers.conf.d\1-userns-keep-id.conf`
2. Restart podman machine
3. Run devcontainer from repository cloned in windows filesystem


### Describe the results you received

devcontainers do not work properly (without file ownership issues) without the runArgs in the `devcontainer.json` file - it does not seem to pick up the setting from the .conf file.

### Describe the results you expected

devcontainers work properly without the `runArgs` in the `devcontainer.json` file

title: .github/workflows/issue_pr_lock.yml: run for the full org
body:
This workflow is used and called by buildah and skopeo, however due this new if it will just get skipped there as the context on a action reuse will still be set to the proper repo which calls the action.

The point of this new if from commit 32f987fc8c
("ci: restrict specific workflows to the upstream repository") was to avoid running our actions on forks where they will fail due to missing secrets, etc...

So by limiting the scope to our org here we can reuse it from buildah and skopeo and still prevent it running on forks from users.

body:
This issue was posted before (https://github.com/podman-container-tools/podman/issues/17644); however it was closed without a solution.

The suggestion to look in the man pages did not solve the issue because it is not documented there.
See https://github.com/podman-container-tools/container-libs/blob/main/common/docs/containers.conf.5.md

The question is still: how to properly configure podman using a configuration file on Windows?

I added the configuration file below to `%APPDATA%\Roaming\containers\containers.conf.d` and it does not seem to be picked up.

1-userns-keep-id.conf
```toml
[containers]
userns = "keep-id"
```

I wanted to add this setting as a configuration file instead of as `runArgs` setting in my `devcontainer.json` files to prevent breaking their compatibility with docker.

title: fix(kube): gate SELinux volume warning note on host SELinux state
body:
Fixes #17743

`podman kube generate` always printed a NOTE about SELinux volume
permissions whenever a pod had volumes, even on non-SELinux hosts or
rootful setups. This added noise for most users.

This gates the warning so it only fires when it's actually relevant:
volumes exist AND SELinux is enabled on the host AND podman is running
rootless. The condition is inlined directly at the call site.

Coverage is added to the existing "with volume" e2e case in
generate_kube_test.go, checking the note shows up only when running
rootless with selinux enabled.

title: Add dnsnames field & fix alias field
body:
Docker now reserves alias specfically for user-defined aliases, and uses another field, dnsnames, to hold all aliases, including container ID and name.
Part of docker v1.45 compat work, but this touches the cli too, since they updated it there too.

```release-note
The NetworkSettings.Network.Aliases field in the `podman inspect` command and in returned in calls to GET /containers/{name:.*}/json API no longer contains the short container ID, and only contains user-provided network aliases. A new field, NetworkSettings.Network.DNSNames contains all aliases, container ID and name.
```

title: Quadlet: consider publishing a standalone, implementation-independent specification (compose-spec model)

labels.name: kind/feature
labels.description: Categorizes issue or PR as related to a new feature.

body:
### Feature request description

Right now the normative reference for Quadlet is podman-systemd.unit(5), documentation for the Podman CLI/generator itself. That's the right source of truth for Podman users. But for anyone trying to build against Quadlet from outside the Podman project — a third-party parser, a packaging format, or another specification that wants to reference Quadlet as a dependency — there isn't currently a standalone, versioned document to point to. You end up citing a man page tied to a specific Podman release rather than a spec artifact with its own identity and release cadence.

Would the maintainers be open to a standalone Quadlet specification, decoupled from the Podman codebase and versioned independently — similar to how the Compose Specification was split out from Docker Compose into its own repo/org in 2020? Podman's generator (pkg/systemd/quadlet/) would remain the reference implementation; the point would be to give the format a citable surface separate from any one implementation's version number.

**Is your feature request related to a problem? Please describe.**

We're contributing to the Linux Foundation's Margo project (an open standard for industrial edge workload orchestration). Margo already supports Helm and Compose as deployment profile types, and we've proposed Quadlet as a third profile — that proposal is under review with the Margo Technical Working Group and isn't ratified yet, so nothing here assumes it will be accepted. If it is, Margo's spec would need something concrete to cite for "what a conformant Quadlet component looks like" — ideally a document with its own version number and change history, not "whatever podman-systemd.unit(5) says as of Podman 5.x."

We're not the only ones parsing/generating Quadlet syntax outside podman itself — podlet and the Podman Desktop Quadlet extension already do — so external interest in the format doesn't seem unique to our use case.

[quadlet-spec-v1.0.0.md](https://github.com/user-attachments/files/30196056/quadlet-spec-v1.0.0.md)



### Suggest potential solution

A clear and concise description of what you want to happen.Open to whatever shape the maintainers think fits the project best, but two options that come to mind:

Standalone repo, e.g. containers/quadlet-spec, holding a versioned spec.md (unit types, grammar, generated-service defaults, conformance levels) with its own release tags — man pages stay as the day-to-day user reference and would defer to the spec for the underlying grammar.
In-tree but explicitly decoupled: keep the document inside containers/podman but give it its own version number, changelog, and a clear "reference implementation wins on conflict" statement, so external projects can pin to a spec version without pinning to a Podman release.




### Have you considered any alternatives?

Citing podman-systemd.unit(5) directly, pinned to a specific Podman version — works, but ties every external adopter's compatibility statement to Podman's release cadence rather than to the format itself.
Each external project reverse-engineering and vendoring its own description of Quadlet syntax from the generator source — duplicative and prone to drifting out of sync.

### Additional context

Either way, defined conformance levels (minimal parsing vs. full systemd-integration behavior vs. bit-identical output) would help third-party implementers know what they're signing up for.

### Issue Description

When building a container on Windows 11, mismatched path separators in a `podman-secret-XXXXXXXXXX` file path cause the build command to fail. It seems like `os.CreateTemp` is using the path separator for the host system (Windows 11) rather than the machine (WSL 2).

Here is the `Containerfile` I'm using:
```Dockerfile
ARG NODE_VERSION=24
ARG PORT=8080

FROM node:${NODE_VERSION}-alpine AS base
WORKDIR /app

FROM base AS deps
COPY package.json package-lock.json .npmrc ./
RUN --mount=type=secret,id=mysecret \
    MY_SECRET="$(cat /run/secrets/mysecret)" npm ci

FROM deps AS dev
ARG PORT

ENV NITRO_HOST=0.0.0.0
EXPOSE ${PORT}
CMD ["npm", "run", "dev"]

ENV NITRO_HOST=0.0.0.0

USER node

1. On Windows 11 Powershell, run:
```sh
podman machine init

title: feat(quadlet): add SocketActivationPort — systemd socket activation for containers and pods
body:
## Motivation

Containers in Podman lack native socket activation through Quadlet.
Currently, achieving on-demand container startup requires manually writing
three systemd units (.socket, proxy, .service) — the "OnlyOffice" pattern
documented in tutorials. This means dozens of boilerplate lines per port.

This PR adds the `SocketActivationPort` key to Quadlet — one line replaces
three manual units. Multiple ports are supported (like PublishPort), it works
in both rootless and root modes, and requires no container modification.

`SocketActivationPort` is fully compatible with and reuses `PublishPort`:
- Same syntax (`hostPort:containerPort`)
- Same parser (`specgenutil.CreatePortBindings`)
- Coexists in the same unit with collision detection
- PublishPort range conflict detection prevents runtime EADDRINUSE

## Design

systemd-socket-proxyd was chosen over direct fd-passing because:
- Works with ANY container image (no LISTEN_FDS support required)
- Supports port remapping (hostPort ≠ containerPort)
- Isolates the container from external networks (loopback-only internal port)

The proxy receives 14 hardening directives (SystemCallFilter, RestrictSUIDSGID,
etc.), a readiness probe with fallback chain (socat → python3 → bash), and
auto-allocates internal ports with floor=1024 for rootless safety.

## Limitations (v1 / known tradeoffs)

- TCP only (systemd-socket-proxyd limitation)
- No idle-shutdown — containers start on demand but are not auto-stopped
- Readiness probe depends on socat/python3/bash (Go wait-helper planned)

## Testing Done

- 30+ unit tests: all parse errors, multi-port, port collisions, hardening
- go build ./... ✅
- go vet ✅
- gofumpt ✅
- xref-quadlet-docs ✅
- Manual dry-run verification with various .container/.pod configurations

## Future Work (follow-up PRs)

- Go wait-port helper to replace socat/python3/bash readiness probe
- [Kube] group support
- Direct fd-passing when hostPort == containerPort (v2 hybrid)

title: feat(quadlet): add SocketActivationPort — systemd socket activation for containers and pods
body:
## Motivation

Enabling socket activation for a container in Quadlet currently requires manually writing three systemd units: `.socket`, `-proxy.service`, and `.service`. One port = ~30 lines of boilerplate. This is the documented "OnlyOffice pattern" — functional but tedious.

`SocketActivationPort=8080:80` replaces those three units with a single line. Uses the same syntax, parser, and collision detection as `PublishPort`.

## Why systemd-socket-proxyd

[systemd-socket-proxyd](https://www.freedesktop.org/software/systemd/man/latest/systemd-socket-proxyd.html) is a standard systemd component designed specifically for this: providing socket activation to applications that lack `LISTEN_FDS` support. From its man page: "a generic socket-activated proxy for services that do not natively support socket activation."

This approach works with any container image without modification, supports port remapping (`hostPort ≠ containerPort`), and isolates containers from external networks (internal port is loopback-only).

## v1 Limitations

- TCP only (systemd-socket-proxyd limitation)
- No automatic container shutdown on idle
- First request may fail for slow-starting apps (subsequent requests work — proxy retries per-connection)

## Testing

- 35 unit tests: parse errors, port collisions, multi-port, hardening
- gofumpt, go vet, go build — clean
- Verified on a real system: cold start, concurrent requests
