### Feature request description

Hi,

when working with podman, podman creates a heap of "anomymous" volumes with random hex-string names. podman volume inspect show something like


podman volume inspect 23dbf5a46d4cc628d53c4780ef6737bfc9dcb8254937890a5f304d66096de34e
[
     {
          "Name": "23dbf5a46d4cc628d53c4780ef6737bfc9dcb8254937890a5f304d66096de34e",
          "Driver": "local",
          "Mountpoint": "/home/hadmut/.local/share/containers/storage/volumes/23dbf5a46d4cc628d53c4780ef6737bfc9dcb8254937890a5f304d66096de34e/_data",
          "CreatedAt": "2026-05-22T00:09:51.145141641+02:00",

     }
]


but they don't have a label or option which can be selected by the prune command's filters. 

On the other hand, "Anonymous": true clearly identifies those volumes, but podman volume prune has no filter to select just them. 


It would, furthermore, be really important to have a dry-run option (as so many programs with possibly destructive effects do offer), to just list what would have been done, without actually doing it. For checking filter definitions. 


The main problem is, that podman creates a big heap of trash volumes, making deleting them manually annoying, while non-anomyous volumes might contain important data and could erroneously be deleted.

title: test system: increase nproc ulimit value to avoid flake
body:
RLIMIT_NPROC is enforced per user namespace, not per container. On remote with rootless, leaked conmon exec-session processes (which sleep ~300s) can push the process count in the shared user namespace high enough that a low nproc ulimit like 512 causes crun to fail with 'clone: Resource temporarily unavailable'. Bump the test value to 10000, with a comment explaining why, so it isn't quietly lowered again.

Verified locally with:
hack/bats --rootless 280:"podman update - set ulimits"

Fixes: #28940

title: Warn when device group is not mapped in rootless user namespaces
body:
<!--
Thanks for sending a pull request!

For more detailed information, please review our contributing guidelines:
https://github.com/containers/podman/blob/main/CONTRIBUTING.md#submitting-pull-requests 
-->
Fixes: #28364

#### Problem
When running a rootless container with `--device` `/dev/XXX` with `--userns=keep-id` `--group-add keep-groups` , devices that belong to groups not mapped in the user namespace silently appear as `nobody:nobody` inside the container and are completely inaccessible. There is no error message, no warning and the container just starts and the device doesn't work.
For example:
```bash
podman run -i --rm --userns=keep-id --group-add keep-groups --device /dev/input/ alpine ls -l /dev/input/event0
```
Output:
```bash 
crw-rw----  1 nobody  nobody  ...  event0
```
The root cause is that the device's group GID is not listed in `/etc/subgid`. When the rootless user namespace is created, only GIDs in `/etc/subgid` get mapped so anything else shows up as nobody.

I tried fixing this automatically using idmapped mounts and injecting GIDs directly into the namespace, but both approaches hit kernel-level limitations as you can't map a GID that isn't already in `/etc/subgid` without root privileges. Automatically editing system files like `/etc/subgid` was also ruled out because that's an admin decision, not something Podman should do silently.

#### Solution
Since I can't fix the mapping automatically, I made the failure visible and actionable.Before Podman enters the user namespace, it saves two things to a temporary file:
- The host supplementary groups of the current user
- The real host GIDs of any devices passed via `--device`

This is necessary because once inside the user namespace, GIDs get remapped and we lose track of what the original host GIDs were.Then when the device is being set up for the container, it check:
1. What is the real host GID of this device?
2. Is the current user a member of that group on the host?
3. Is that GID listed in `/etc/subgid`?

Based on this, one of two warnings are showed: If the user is not even a member of the device group:
lets say a group input and the device GID is 994
```bash
Device event0 is owned by group 'input' (GID 994).
You are not a member of this group on the host.
Access will be denied inside the container.
To fix run:
sudo usermod -aG input ubuntu
Then log out and log back in.
```
If the user is a member but the GID is not in `/etc/subgid`:
```bash
Device event0 is owned by group 'input' (GID 994).
You are a member of this group on the host, but GID 994 is not in /etc/subgid.
The device will appear as 'nobody:nobody' inside the container and access will be denied.
To fix this, run:
echo "ubuntu:994:1" | sudo tee -a /etc/subgid && podman system migrate
```
After the user runs the suggested fix and tries again, the device works correctly and no warning is shown.

#### A note on how devices appear inside the container
The ownership shown inside the container can be a little misleading. For example, on the host a device may be owned by:
`root:input` but after the required `/etc/subgid` mapping is added, the same device inside the container may appear as:
`nobody:bin` or, when viewed with numeric IDs `65534:1`
This is expected.
- The owner (`nobody` / UID `65534`) is the kernel's overflow UID because the device owner's UID (`root`) is not mapped into the rootless user namespace.
- The group (`bin` / GID `1`) is **not** the host's group name. It is simply the container's name for container GID `1`. In this case, container GID `1` is correctly mapped to the host's `input` group (GID `994`) through `/etc/subgid`.

In other words, the displayed **group name** inside the container is independent of the host's group name. As long as the numeric GID is mapped correctly, the device permissions work as expected. This PR only detects missing mappings and provides actionable warnings; it does not attempt to preserve host group names inside the container.

#### Files changed
`pkg/rootless/rootless_linux.go` : Before entering the user namespace, saves the user's host groups and the GIDs of all devices passed via `--device` to temporary files. This is the only place where the real host GIDs are available.
`pkg/specgen/generate/config_linux.go` : When adding a device to the container spec, checks whether the device's GID is accessible and emits the appropriate warning if not. 

#### Tests added
`pkg/specgen/generate/config_linux_test.go`:  Unit tests for `isGIDInSubgid()` covering: GID inside range, GID outside range, boundary values (first and last GID in range), GID explicitly added as a single entry, empty subgid file, and wrong username. 
`test/e2e/run_device_test.go` : This runs a rootless container with `/dev/input` and verifies that a warning is emitted mentioning either missing subgid mapping or missing group membership. The test is skipped automatically if not running in rootless mode or if /dev/input` is not available on the host.
- The e2e test depends on `/dev/input/` being present on the host. If there is a better way to test this in CI, I am open to suggestions.

title: RFC: move machine and bindings tests under test/
body:
Currently our main test suites are located in a subdirectory under test/, i.e. test/system or test/e2e.
The only exceptions are machine tests under pkg/machine/e2e/ and bindings tests under pkg/bindings/test/.

My proposal, move `pkg/machine/e2e` to `test/machine` and `pkg/bindings/test` to `test/bindings`.

The motivation for this is a to make the tests better grouped and easier to discover where to add actual integration test style tests. Unit tests of course stay the way they are right next to the main code in _test.go files.

In addition it is harder to special handle these paths in our our CI path skip rules,in fact since the CI rework they are not handled at all, see `.github/filters.yaml`. The rule `'!(test/**)**/*.@(go|c|h)'` will skip code changes under test/, I was unable to make this rule work for several directories, I likely could make it work somehow but it would create even more complicated to reason about skip rules. So right now a change in only pkg/machine/e2e will trigger the full CI which is just a waste of resources and time. Moving them under test/ would solve this naturally.

title: Allow podman load to import multiple named refs from an OCI archive

labels.name: kind/feature
labels.description: Categorizes issue or PR as related to a new feature.

labels.name: triaged
labels.description: Issue has been triaged

body:
## Feature request description

I would like `podman load` to support an OCI archive that contains multiple names for the same image.

In practical terms, I want one OCI archive to be able to restore both of these local image references:

```text
localhost/ko-layout-smoke:latest
localhost/ko-layout-smoke:stable
```

where both tags point to the same image or image index.

Today, Podman rejects this kind of archive.

## What I Tested

I created an OCI archive whose top-level `index.json` contains two entries. Both entries point to the same image index digest. The only meaningful difference is the image name annotation.

Simplified `index.json`:

```json
{
  "schemaVersion": 2,
  "manifests": [
    {
      "mediaType": "application/vnd.oci.image.index.v1+json",
      "digest": "sha256:...",
      "size": 1234,
      "annotations": {
        "org.opencontainers.image.ref.name": "localhost/ko-layout-smoke:latest"
      }
    },
    {
      "mediaType": "application/vnd.oci.image.index.v1+json",
      "digest": "sha256:...",
      "size": 1234,
      "annotations": {
        "org.opencontainers.image.ref.name": "localhost/ko-layout-smoke:stable"
      }
    }
  ]
}
```

Plain-language interpretation:

```text
There is one underlying image/index at sha256:...
Please import it as localhost/ko-layout-smoke:latest
Please also import it as localhost/ko-layout-smoke:stable
```

## Current Podman Behavior

`podman load -i layout-multi-ref.tar` rejects the archive:

```text
Error: unable to load image: payload does not match any of the supported image formats:
 * oci: open /var/tmp/libpod-images-load.tar3956958393/index.json: not a directory
 * oci-archive: loading index: more than one image in oci, choose an image
 * docker-archive: loading tar component "manifest.json": file does not exist
 * dir: reading version file "/var/tmp/libpod-images-load.tar3956958393/version": open /var/tmp/libpod-images-load.tar3956958393/version: not a directory
```

## Behavior In kind / ctr

The same archive works with kind v0.32.0 through `kind load image-archive`. Kind streams the archive into the node with `ctr images import`.

After import, both tags exist and point to the same image ID:

```text
localhost/ko-layout-smoke  latest  83ac692030a19  2.09MB
localhost/ko-layout-smoke  stable  83ac692030a19  2.09MB
```

Pods using either tag with `imagePullPolicy=Never` completed successfully.

## Why This Seems Reasonable

An OCI layout can contain multiple top-level entries in `index.json`. Each entry can have an `org.opencontainers.image.ref.name` annotation. That annotation is the image name to use when importing.

For this use case, multiple entries do not mean multiple unrelated images. They can be multiple names for the same image digest, like Docker tags.

`ctr images import` handles this by reading each top-level `index.json` entry and creating image records from the name annotations.

Relevant source references:

- kind streams image archives to `ctr images import --all-platforms --digests`: https://github.com/kubernetes-sigs/kind/blob/v0.32.0/pkg/cluster/nodeutils/util.go#L80-L90
- `ctr images import` creates an import stream and transfers it to an image store: https://github.com/containerd/containerd/blob/9e70782d9a0e92900f402b2c7a4e2aa30754503c/cmd/ctr/commands/images/import.go#L188-L193
- the transfer importer loops over each top-level `index.json` entry and marks it as nameable from annotations: https://github.com/containerd/containerd/blob/9e70782d9a0e92900f402b2c7a4e2aa30754503c/core/transfer/local/import.go#L79-L83
- the transfer importer stores each descriptor: https://github.com/containerd/containerd/blob/9e70782d9a0e92900f402b2c7a4e2aa30754503c/core/transfer/local/import.go#L131-L134
- the image store creates an image record from the annotation-derived name: https://github.com/containerd/containerd/blob/9e70782d9a0e92900f402b2c7a4e2aa30754503c/core/transfer/image/imagestore.go#L236-L267
- the name is read from `io.containerd.image.name` first, then `org.opencontainers.image.ref.name`: https://github.com/containerd/containerd/blob/9e70782d9a0e92900f402b2c7a4e2aa30754503c/core/transfer/image/imagestore.go#L480-L498

## Suggest potential solution

Allow `podman load` to import OCI archives that contain multiple top-level entries when those entries have usable image-name annotations.

A conservative first step could support only the case where:

- each top-level entry has `org.opencontainers.image.ref.name`
- repeated digests are allowed
- multiple names can point to the same digest
- ambiguous entries without image-name annotations can still be rejected

That would allow one OCI archive to preserve multiple tags for the same image or image index.

## Have you considered any alternatives?

The current workaround is to produce one OCI archive per tag:

```sh
podman save --format oci-archive -o app-v1.oci.tar localhost/app:v1
podman save --format oci-archive -o app-latest.oci.tar localhost/app:latest
```

That works, but duplicates the archive artifact and loses the natural relationship that `v1` and `latest` are just two names for the same image/index.

Another workaround is Docker archive format, but that is not ideal for workflows that specifically want OCI archive semantics, especially for multi-platform image-index workflows.

## Additional context

This came up while evaluating `oci-archive` output for ko and GoReleaser. The goal is a Docker-free and registry-free CI workflow where a multi-platform image index is built as a single portable OCI archive, scanned, loaded into kind for tests, and later published to an OCI registry.

Related docs:

- Podman documents `podman save --format oci-archive` as producing "a tar archive using the OCI Image Format": https://docs.podman.io/en/latest/markdown/podman-save.1.html#format-format
- Podman documents `podman load` as loading local tar archives: https://docs.podman.io/en/latest/markdown/podman-load.1.html#input-i-input

Tested with Podman v6.0.1 and kind v0.32.0 on darwin/arm64.

title: Podman fails to properly mount host /tmp directory on Macos

labels.name: kind/bug
labels.description: Categorizes issue or PR as related to a bug.

labels.name: remote
labels.description: Problem is in podman-remote

labels.name: macos
labels.description: MacOS (OSX) related

body:
### Issue Description

This was an issue opened on podman desktop repository, but we believe it is related to podman and hence opening it here. https://github.com/podman-desktop/podman-desktop/issues/13484

### Bug description

Podman fails to properly mount host /tmp directory on Macos. The pod commandline contains the mount parameter "-v /tmp:/tmp", the directory is mounted, but
not accessible from the pod. Listing the directory fails with "Permission Denied".

Expected behavior: 

Should see the content of the host `/tmp` directory. 
This way it works on Docker Desktop.

### Operating system

macOS Sequoia 15.5 M4

### Installation Method

Installer from website/GitHub releases

### podman desktop Version

1.20.2


### Additional context

Workaround

In MacOS `/tmp' is not a real directory, but a symlink to `/private/tmp`:

```
$ ls -dl /tmp
lrwxr-xr-x   1 root           wheel          11 2025-05-04 08:39 /tmp -> private/tmp
```
When I specify in the podman command line `-v /private/tmp:/tmp'
it works as expected.




### Steps to reproduce the issue

### Steps to reproduce

1. Install current version of podman 1.20.2 (cannot select this version from the dropdown menu above)for Mac on recent Macos/arm64 (15.5)  with default setting, just skipped installing the kubernetes tools and Compose).
2. Start Podman GUI and create a podman machine instance.
3. Run a container,  mounting Macos /tmp as /tmp in the container, expecting
to see contents of the MacOS host in the /tmp folder in the container:

```shell
 $ podman run -i -t -v "/tmp:/tmp" bash

Writing manifest to image destination
bash-5.3# 
```

4. In the container try to list the `/tmp` directory

```shell

ls: can't open '/tmp': Permission denied
```
5. See that /tmp exists, is a directory and it's mode looks OK:

```shell
bash-5.3# ls -l -d /tmp
drwxrwxrwt   10 root     root           200 Aug  2 23:11 /tmp
```

title: remote podman build host path propagation with out of context build files (nTar)

labels.name: kind/bug
labels.description: Categorizes issue or PR as related to a bug.

labels.name: remote
labels.description: Problem is in podman-remote

labels.name: triaged
labels.description: Issue has been triaged

labels.name: build
labels.description: Issue is in podman build/Buildah

body:
### Issue Description

A remote podman build tars the context dir and any out-of-context inputs and ships it to the server. These out-of-context inputs are tarred while retaining their absolute paths, leading to host path (_only the path_) leaks in the build context dir extracted on the server end. These paths can further end up in the image in presence of a `COPY . /` in the Containerfile.

### Steps to reproduce the issue

```
./bin/podman --root /tmp/proot --runroot /tmp/prun \
    system service --time=0 unix:///tmp/p.sock &
sleep 1

mkdir -p /tmp/ctx /tmp/outside
touch /tmp/ctx/somefile
printf 'FROM alpine\nCOPY . /testdir/\nRUN find /testdir/\n' > /tmp/outside/Containerfile

./bin/podman --url unix:///tmp/p.sock build -f /tmp/outside/Containerfile /tmp/ctx
```

### Describe the results you received

Server can "see" host paths that ideally shouldn't have propagated:

```
STEP 1/3: FROM alpine
Resolved "alpine" as an alias (/etc/containers/registries.conf.d/000-shortnames.conf)
Trying to pull docker.io/library/alpine:latest...
Getting image source signatures
Copying blob sha256:55afa1ecc21d2bb5e5045f32dafee56272ffd89860bac26f6c32123439af26a4
Copying config sha256:d529dd0c6e5597ac7e4a3e2dea65c3fcc6173f4cae713c409265c1dd9914a11b
Writing manifest to image destination
STEP 2/3: COPY . /testdir/
--> 3227d6dfbed5
STEP 3/3: RUN find /testdir/
/testdir/
/testdir/tmp
/testdir/tmp/outside
/testdir/tmp/outside/Containerfile
/testdir/somefile
COMMIT
--> e5ec40a2aacb
e5ec40a2aacba2140dbd7d59507e6606117792fd4bc61d1a17d1bde94c1c207c
```

### Describe the results you expected

For starters, not the absolute host paths while building on the server, and worst case, the built image.

For a fix, I tried playing around with prepending the basename with a constant path prefix and the input index (to avoid conflicts). For instance, in the above example, instead of tarring up the Containerfile as `/tmp/outside/Containerfile`, the client passes on `.podman-build-external/{index}/Containerfile`

Subsequently the server extracts these path prefixed to a new /tmp directory in order to avoid `COPY . /` polluting the image with out-of-context inputs, given that they weren't ever part of the context dir to begin with.

I'd like to discuss this issue, approach and other approaches I might've missed before raising a PR.

title: ci: gate releases on podman-machine-os release
body:
#### Summary

This wires an actual release gate into the Podman release workflow.

Right now the version-bump PR still gets the do-not-merge/wait-machine-os-build label, but that label no longer blocks anything on its own. Because of that, it's possible to cut a Podman release before the matching podman-machine-os release is out.

With this change, non-build-only runs of .github/workflows/release.yml check for a matching release in podman-machine-os before continuing. If that release is missing, the workflow stops before artifact builds and release creation.

I also updated RELEASE_PROCESS.md so the documented release steps match the current workflow behavior and label name.

Fixes #28920

#### Testing

- git diff --check
- Parsed .github/workflows/release.yml as YAML
- Manually reviewed the workflow flow to confirm:
  - build-only runs skip the new gate
  - release runs wait for the new gate before building artifacts

title: journald: support --log-opt labels (#28187)
body:
## Summary

Implement support for Docker-compatible `--log-opt labels=` with the `journald` log driver.

This allows users to promote selected container labels into structured journald fields, matching Docker's behavior.

Example:

```console
podman run \
  --log-driver=journald \
  --label team=payments \
  --label env=prod \
  --log-opt labels=team,env \
  alpine echo hello
```

The selected container labels are promoted to structured journald fields (after sanitizing field names for journald compatibility).

## Changes

* Add parsing support for `--log-opt labels=`
* Store promoted label keys in the container configuration
* Promote selected container labels in `getLogData()`
* Sanitize journald field names before passing them to conmon
* Add an end-to-end test covering the new functionality

## Testing

Successfully completed:

* `make podman`
* `go test ./pkg/specgen/...`
* `go test ./libpod/...`

Local verification confirmed that Podman generates the expected conmon arguments:

```text
--log-label TEAM=payments
--log-label ENV=prod
```

I was not able to complete end-to-end runtime verification locally because the installed `conmon` version does not support the `--log-label` option, and the local integration test environment encountered unrelated `netavark.lock` permission issues before executing the test suite.

Fixes #28187

title: fix: enable security.selinux extended attributes on tmpfs mounts
body:
## Summary
Fixes #29127.

When a container is run with `--tmpfs /b`, the tmpfs kernel driver does not enable the `security.*` extended attribute handler unless a SELinux context mount option is present. This means `setfattr -n security.selinux` fails with `EOPNOTSUPP` on tmpfs mounts.

## Changes
- **`libpod/container_internal_common.go`**: Add `hasSELinuxContextOption()` helper to detect existing SELinux mount options. For tmpfs mounts without explicit SELinux context, inject `fscontext=<label>` to enable the kernel's `security.*` xattr handler. Clear the global `Linux.MountLabel` and redistribute `context=<label>` to non-tmpfs mounts to prevent the OCI runtime from layering duplicate `context=` that would override per-mount options.
- **`libpod/container_internal_common_test.go`**: Unit test for `hasSELinuxContextOption()` covering all 4 SELinux prefix variants, mixed options, empty slices, and partial-prefix edge cases. OCI spec inspection test for `addSELinuxMountOptionsNonTmpfs()` verifying tmpfs gets `fscontext=`, non-tmpfs gets `context=`, and global label is cleared correctly.

## Why clear the global MountLabel?

Simply adding `context=` or `fscontext=` to the target tmpfs is not enough. runc unconditionally appends `context=<MountLabel>` to every mount, and crun similarly layers its global label. If we leave `Linux.MountLabel` set with a per-mount `fscontext=`, the runtime produces duplicate options (`context=,...fscontext=...`), which SELinux may reject with `EINVAL`. Using `context=` on the tmpfs puts it in mount-point labeling mode, which still blocks per-file `setfattr`. The only way to reliably enable `security.*` xattrs on tmpfs is: (1) use `fscontext=` for the tmpfs, (2) clear the global label so the runtime does not append `context=`, and (3) explicitly redistribute `context=` to all non-tmpfs mounts.

## Before/After (OCI spec mount options)

**Before** (`podman run --tmpfs /b`):
```
Mounts: [{Type: tmpfs, Destination: /b, Options: []}]
Linux.MountLabel: "system_u:object_r:container_file_t:s0:c1,c2"
```
→ runc appends `context=system_u:object_r:container_file_t:s0:c1,c2`
→ tmpfs in mount-point labeling mode → `setfattr` → EOPNOTSUPP

**After**:
```
Mounts: [{Type: tmpfs, Destination: /b, Options: [fscontext=system_u:object_r:container_file_t:s0:c1,c2]}]
Linux.MountLabel: ""
Non-tmpfs mounts get: context=system_u:object_r:container_file_t:s0:c1,c2
```
→ `security.selinux` xattr handler enabled → `setfattr` succeeds

## Limitations
- `/dev` tmpfs is excluded from `fscontext=` injection
- Nested containers (`LabelNested`) use `rootcontext=` instead
- Users needing full per-file labeling control should pass explicit `--tmpfs /mnt:fscontext="..."`

## Discussion
This is a best-effort fix for the common case. There are open questions I'd like maintainer input on:
1. Is there a preferred way to handle this in the OCI runtime (runc/crun) instead of at the Podman level?
2. Should we add an SELinux-gated integration test that runs `setfattr` inside a container?
3. The current approach clears `Linux.MountLabel` globally; is there a cleaner per-mount API we should use?

title: feat: journald log driver support for `--log-opt labels=` and `env=`

labels.name: kind/api-change
labels.description: Change to remote API; merits scrutiny

body:
Closes #28187

**- What I did**
Added support for `--log-opt labels=<comma-separated-labels>` and `--log-opt env=<comma-separated-env-vars>` when using the journald log driver. This promotes the specified container labels or environment variables as structured fields in journald, matching Docker's behavior.

**- How I did it**
In `pkg/specgenutil/specgen.go`, when iterating through `--log-opt` options, added cases for `labels` and `env`. These cases split the provided values by `,` and iterate through them. If the corresponding key is found in the container's labels (`s.Labels`) or environment (`s.Env`), the value is extracted and added to `logLabels`. The keys are automatically sanitized using `sanitizeLogKey` (replacing non-alphanumeric characters with `_` and converting to uppercase) to ensure compatibility with `journald` field name restrictions.

**- How to verify it**
```bash
podman run --log-driver=journald --log-opt labels=location --label location=west alpine echo test
journalctl -o json-pretty CONTAINER_NAME=...
# Should contain "LOCATION" : "west"
```

**- Description for the changelog**
Support for `--log-opt labels=` and `--log-opt env=` has been added to the journald log driver to promote container labels and environment variables as structured journal fields.

title: `podman exec --user` does not initialize supplementary groups in rootful container

labels.name: kind/bug
labels.description: Categorizes issue or PR as related to a bug.

body:
### Issue Description

Describe your issu### Issue description

In a rootful Podman container, `podman exec --user <user>` starts the process with an incorrect group list.

The user and supplementary groups are correctly defined in the container's NSS databases. `getent initgroups mario` returns the expected primary and supplementary GIDs, but a process launched using `podman exec --user mario` has only GID 0.

Entering the container as root and then using `su - mario` initializes the correct groups.

This affects a rootful Distrobox container, but the problem reproduces directly with Podman, without Distrobox being involved in the exec operation.

This appears closely related to #9986, but I am seeing it with Podman 5.8.3. It may also be related to #25610, although that issue concerns the implicit root user rather than an explicitly selected non-root user.

### Environment

Host OS: Aurora/Fedora Atomic Fedora 44

Packages:

```text
podman-5.8.3-1.fc44.x86_64
crun-1.28-1.fc44.x86_64
distrobox-1.8.2.5-1.fc44.noarch
```

The container is rootful and is normally entered using:

```console
/usr/bin/distrobox-enter --root -n arch
```


### Expected result

When an explicitly named container user is passed to:

```console
podman exec --user mario ...
```

Podman should resolve that user inside the container and initialize the process credentials using the equivalent of `initgroups()`.

The resulting group list should match:

```console
getent initgroups mario
```

### Additional information

The behavior is consistent across:

```console
sudo podman exec --user mario arch id
sudo podman exec --user mario:998 arch id
```

Only explicitly invoking `su - mario` from a root exec session results in the correct groups.

The container was created previously and has been upgraded over time. I have not recreated it because it contains an established development environment and multiple exported desktop applications.

I can provide the output of:

```console
sudo podman info --debug
sudo podman inspect arch
```

and any OCI runtime debug logs needed.
e

### Steps to reproduce the issue

Steps to reproduce the issue

Assuming:
- `arch` is a rootful container
- `mario` is a user within the container with uid 1000
- `mario` has additional groups added in `/etc/group` (in this case, groups `998` and `954`)

1. `sudo podman exec --user mario arch sh -c 'getent initgroups mario'` --> `mario 998 954`
2. `sudo podman exec --user mario arch id` --> `uid=1000(mario) gid=1000(mario) groups=1000(mario),0(root)`
3. `sudo podman exec --user mario:998 arch id -->
`uid=1000(mario) gid=998(wheel) groups=998(wheel),0(root)`
4. `sudo podman exec --user root arch su -s /bin/sh - mario -c id` --> `uid=1000(mario) gid=1000(mario) groups=1000(mario),954(docker),998(wheel)`

### Describe the results you received

`podman exec --user mario` does not apply the user's primary and supplementary groups from the container's user/group database.

In my case, the process is launched with GID 0 and group 0, even though `getent initgroups mario` reports GIDs 998 and 954.

This has practical consequences: applications launched through podman exec, including exported Distrobox desktop applications and scripts, run with incorrect group credentials.

It also caused PAM/faillock files to be accessible through the unintended GID 0 membership.

### Describe the results you expected

When an explicitly named container user is passed to:

`podman exec --user mario ...`

Podman should resolve that user inside the container and initialize the process credentials using the equivalent of `initgroups()`.

The resulting group list should match:

getent initgroups mario

### podman info output

```yaml
(pasting `sudo podman info --debug` since this is a rootful container)
```

title: Fix inspect template `.HostIp` for Docker compatibility
body:
Docker-compatible inspect templates using `{{.HostIp}}` fail in Podman because Go templates resolve by struct field name (`HostIP`), not JSON tag (`HostIp`). Add a `HostIp()` method so both notations work.

Note: this does not address the struct-vs-map difference that prevents `range` over individual port bindings (would require an API break).

Relates: https://github.com/podman-container-tools/podman/issues/29164

title: inspect template for .NetworkSettings.Ports inconsistent with docker

labels.name: kind/bug
labels.description: Categorizes issue or PR as related to a bug.

labels.name: triaged
labels.description: Issue has been triaged
Breaking changes for Podman 7.0

body:
### Issue Description

kind-load-balancer (part of github.com/kubernetes-sigs/cloud-provider-kind) fails to start with the error:

`"Failed to get external kubeconfig" err="failed to get api server port: command "docker inspect --format '{{ with (index (index .NetworkSettings.Ports "6443/tcp") 0) }}{{ printf "%s\t%s" .HostIp .HostPort }}{{ end }}' kind-control-plane" failed with error: exit status 125" cluster="kind"`

The inspect works under docker, but fails under podman with the docker compatibility command.

Attempting to iterate over the object shows the differences between docker and podman:

moby-engine docker:
```
$ docker inspect --format '{{ range $k, $v := (index .NetworkSettings.Ports "6443/tcp") }}{{ print $k " -> " $v "\n" }}{{end}}' kind-control-plane
0 -> map[HostIp:127.0.0.1 HostPort:4400]

$ docker inspect --format '{{ range $k, $v := (index (index .NetworkSettings.Ports "6443/tcp") 0) }}{{ print $k " -> " $v "\n" }}{{end}}' kind-control-plane
HostIp -> 127.0.0.1
HostPort -> 4400

$ docker inspect --format '{{ with (index (index .NetworkSettings.Ports "6443/tcp") 0) }}{{ printf "%s\t%s" .HostIp .HostPort }}{{ end }}' kind-control-plane
127.0.0.1	4400
```

podman docker:
```
$ docker inspect --format '{{ range $k, $v := (index .NetworkSettings.Ports "6443/tcp") }}{{ print $k " -> " $v "\n" }}{{end}}' kind-control-plane
0 -> {127.0.0.1 44481}

$ docker inspect --format '{{ range $k, $v := (index (index .NetworkSettings.Ports "6443/tcp") 0) }}{{ print $k " -> " $v "\n" }}{{end}}' kind-control-plane
Error: template: inspect:1:79: executing "inspect" at <0>: range can't iterate over {127.0.0.1 44481}

$ docker inspect --format '{{ with (index (index .NetworkSettings.Ports "6443/tcp") 0) }}{{ printf "%s\t%s" .HostIp .HostPort }}{{ end }}' kind-control-plane
Error: template: inspect:1:91: executing "inspect" at <.HostIp>: can't evaluate field HostIp in type define.InspectHostPort
```

As visible above, docker exposes NetworkSettings.Ports as a array of maps, but podman as an array of objects.  As a workaround, the values can be accessed in podman using the object definition of define.InspectHostPort with:
```
$ docker inspect --format '{{ with (index (index .NetworkSettings.Ports "6443/tcp") 0) }}{{ printf "%s\t%s" .HostIP .HostPort }}{{ end }}' kind-control-plane
127.0.0.1	44481
```

but the same command in moby-engine fails:
```
$ docker inspect --format '{{ with (index (index .NetworkSettings.Ports "6443/tcp") 0) }}{{ printf "%s\t%s" .HostIP .HostPort }}{{ end }}' kind-control-plane
template parsing error: template: :1:81: executing "" at <.HostIP>: map has no entry for key "HostIP"
```




### Steps to reproduce the issue

Steps to reproduce the issue
1. Install podman docker compatibility
2. Start a container `docker run --rm -d --name test --publish=127.0.0.1:4400:6443/tcp alpine sleep infinity`
3. Run: `docker inspect --format '{{ with (index (index .NetworkSettings.Ports "6443/tcp") 0) }}{{ printf "%s\t%s" .HostIp .HostPort }}{{ end }}' test`


### Describe the results you received

Error: template: inspect:1:91: executing "inspect" at <.HostIp>: can't evaluate field HostIp in type define.InspectHostPort


### Describe the results you expected

127.0.0.1	4400

title: Slower startup time with concurrent podman run

labels.name: kind/bug
labels.description: Categorizes issue or PR as related to a bug.

body:
### Issue Description In QEMU project, we use containers to cross compile tests for different architectures. As a result, for every test, we launch a container to run a cross-compiler. This is done as part of build process, and thus multiple `podman run` commands are executed in parallel. While working on it, I noticed that compiling with more or less cores had almost no impact on total time, which was surprising. Looking closer, podman run gets slower as we add more cores, and cpu usage barely increases. Time scale "almost" linearly with number of cores, with cpu being unused, which is usually the result of a lock contention. In practice, a normal podman run takes around 0.2s on my machine. When running concurrently with 4 cores, it takes around 0.5s on average. When running concurrently with 8 cores, it takes around 1s on average. When running concurrently with 16 cores, it takes around 2s on average. Note: my machine has 16 physical cores, so it should stay constant. The same can be observed with rootful and rootless podman. Interestingly, if mixing sudo and non sudo podman run, command is still slowed, but with less impact, suggesting it's definitely something on user side and not kernel related, as different users are not impacted. The same can be observed using --network=host or --privileged flag. The same can be observed with podman 5.4.2 (debian trixie) and 4.9.3 (ubuntu 24.04). Finally, I would like to add that same behavior happens with docker, but it's slower than podman in all cases, and I personally only have interest in podman. To reproduce it: ``` # benchmark tool apt install hyperfine parallel # pull image podman pull docker.io/debian # run with 1 core yes 'hyperfine "podman run --rm docker.io/debian true"' | head -n 1 | parallel -j 100 --bar # run with 4 cores and observe that average time increase yes 'hyperfine "podman run --rm docker.io/debian true"' | head -n 4 | parallel -j 100 --bar ``` This kind of performance analysis is always complex, because it requires to track what is happening during [off cpu](https://www.brendangregg.com/offcpuanalysis.html) time. I managed to create a flamegraph using offcputime-bpfcc. ``` sudo apt install bpfcc-tools git clone https://github.com/brendangregg/flamegraph # spawn many podman run yes 'hyperfine "podman run --rm docker.io/debian true"' | head -n 1000 | parallel -j 8 --bar # meanwhile, capture global offcpu time for 10 seconds sudo bash -c 'ulimit -n 1000000 && offcputime-bpfcc 10 -u -f > stack.folded' ~/flamegraph/flamegraph.pl stack.folded > off.svg ``` Full flamegraph: [download](https://github.com/user-attachments/files/29865547/off.svg.gz) && gzip -d && google-chrome off.svg Unfortunately, I have not been able to get call stacks, even after rebuilding podman from sources. This could be due to specificities with `go` routines when performing this kind of work, and I didn't really dive into it. I understand that speeding up startup time for containers is a niche use case, but it would still be interesting to understand what is going on, and how to remove this bottleneck. Does anyone with proper `go` experience could give some hints about how investigate further? Else, any idea where to take a look at on podman side? ### Steps to reproduce the issue Steps to reproduce the issue: ``` # benchmark tool apt install hyperfine parallel # pull image podman pull docker.io/debian # run with 1 core yes 'hyperfine "podman run --rm docker.io/debian true"' | head -n 1 | parallel -j 100 --bar # run with 4 cores and observe that average time increase yes 'hyperfine "podman run --rm docker.io/debian true"' | head -n 4 | parallel -j 100 --bar ``` ### Describe the results you received podman run gets slower and slower as we add more cores. ### Describe the results you expected podman run command time stays constant. ### podman info output

title: Machine-scope installation (ALLUSERS=1) writes PATH to installing user's HKCU instead of system PATH

labels.name: kind/bug
labels.description: Categorizes issue or PR as related to a bug.

body:
### Issue Description

For a machine-scope installation (ALLUSERS=1), the installer should add the Podman installation directory to the system PATH: _HKLM\SYSTEM\CurrentControlSet\Control\Session Manager\Environment\Path_
so that Podman is available for all users on the device, but Instead, the PATH entry is written to: _HKCU\Environment\Path_

### Steps to reproduce the issue

Steps to reproduce the issue
1. Install Podman MSI in System Context as machine-wide installation: _msiexec /i podman-installer-windows-amd64.msi **ALLUSERS=1**_
2. Try to run _podman info_ as different user - it will fail. 


### Describe the results you received

**Observed behavior**

- Podman installed to C:\Program Files\Podman
- MSI_Log: WriteEnvironmentStrings action completed successfully
- MSI_Log: EnvEntriesComponent was installed (Action: Local)
- No PATH update in HKLM system environment
- PATH update found in the installing user's HKCU environment

**Impact**
This affects enterprise deployments (Intune, MECM/SCCM, EPM, installations as SYSTEM, etc.), where Podman is installed successfully but is not available in PATH for end users without additional remediation.

### Describe the results you expected

For a machine-scope installation (ALLUSERS=1), the installer should add the Podman installation directory to the system PATH: _HKLM\SYSTEM\CurrentControlSet\Control\Session Manager\Environment\Path_ so that Podman is available for all users on the device.

labels.description: Categorizes issue or PR as related to a bug.

labels.name: windows
labels.description: issue/bug on Windows

body:
### Issue Description

On Windows 11 Pro with WSL2 installed and HyperV disabled trying to run
`podman machine init --provider wsl`
returns
`Error: HyperV namespace not found, is HyperV enabled?`
Podman version 6.0.0
On same system, with same settings with podman 5.8.3 command works.
When HyperV feature is enabled (podman 6.0.0) it also works.

### Steps to reproduce the issue

Steps to reproduce the issue
1. Windows 11 Pro host with WSL2 installed and HyperV disabled
2. Run podman machine init --provider wsl


### Describe the results you received

Command aborts
```
time="…" level=debug msg="Using Podman machine with `wsl` virtualization provider"
time="…" level=debug msg="socket length for C:\\Users\\[user]\\.config\\containers\\podman\\machine\\wsl is 53"
time="…" level=debug msg="socket length for C:\\Users\\[user]\\.local\\share\\containers\\podman\\machine\\wsl is 58"
time="…" level=debug msg="socket length for C:\\Users\\[user]\\.local\\share\\containers\\podman\\machine\\wsl\\cache is 64"
time="…" level=debug msg="socket length for C:\\Users\\[user]\\AppData\\Local\\Temp\\podman is 41"
time="…" level=debug msg="socket length for C:\\Users\\[user]\\.config\\containers\\podman\\machine\\wsl\\podman-machine-default.json is 81"
time="…" level=debug msg="socket length for C:\\Users\\[user]\\.config\\containers\\podman\\machine\\hyperv is 56"
time="…" level=debug msg="socket length for C:\\Users\\[user]\\.local\\share\\containers\\podman\\machine\\hyperv is 61"
time="…" level=debug msg="socket length for C:\\Users\\[user]\\.local\\share\\containers\\podman\\machine\\hyperv\\cache is 67"
time="…" level=debug msg="socket length for C:\\Users\\[user]\\AppData\\Local\\Temp\\podman is 41"
Error: HyperV namespace not found, is HyperV enabled?
time="…" level=debug msg="Shutting down engines"
```

### Describe the results you expected

Podman should have created podman machine with wsl provider without HyperV enabled.

### podman info output

```yaml
Client:
  APIVersion: 6.0.0
  Built: 1782322337
  BuiltTime: Wed Jun 24 19:32:17 2026
  GitCommit: a8ed4b6dd12992decf659cadfdfb3d0cb1937748
  GoVersion: go1.26.4
  Os: windows
  OsArch: windows/amd64
  Version: 6.0.0
```

### Podman in a container

No

### Privileged Or Rootless

None

### Upstream Latest Release

No

### Additional environment details

```
OS Name:                       Microsoft Windows 11 Pro
OS Version:                    10.0.26200 N/A Build 26200
OS Manufacturer:               Microsoft Corporation
OS Configuration:              Standalone Workstation
OS Build Type:                 Multiprocessor Free
System Type:                   x64-based PC
```

### Additional information

machine init probably fails when checking something on the hypervisor exists with the same name 
[cmd/podman/machine/init.go#L227](https://github.com/podman-container-tools/podman/blob/a8ed4b6dd12992decf659cadfdfb3d0cb1937748/cmd/podman/machine/init.go#L227)
but since HyperV is not enabled it returns error.

Issue #29053 is not related since it affects host with HyperV enabled and WSL not installed.

Podman's network fails DNS after some time. Ping works on host with domain name and ip, ping fails inside container with domain name, but succeeds with ip.
Have had this issue a few times atleast, all recent. The temporary solution I think is to kill the existing aarvark-dns process then bring down the container and recreate.
Maybe related I recently upgraded to podman 6.0.0.

title: docs/podman.1: clarify effective storage driver options
body:
Use of the `podman --root` option unexpectedly cleared the default storage options from the configuration file and environment variable. Make sure to document this behavior with the `--storage-opt` option. This behavior changed in commit 55f00bac02fc ("Clear the storage-options from the graphdriver if users specifies --root", v3.3.0).

Fix `--root` and `--storage-driver` docs, there is no `storage-opt` setting in `containers-storage.conf(5)`. Use `storage.options.<driver>` instead of `storage.options.*` to avoid implying that `storage.options.pull_options` would also be ignored.

title: Setting SELinux security attributes fails on --tmpfs (setfattr: Not supported)

labels.name: kind/bug
labels.description: Categorizes issue or PR as related to a bug.

body:
### Issue Description

Setting SELinux security attributes fails on --tmpfs:

```bash
$ setfattr -n security.selinux -v 'system_u:object_r:bin_t:s0' x
setfattr: x: Not supported
```

### Steps to reproduce the issue

Validate this works on the host:
```
touch /tmp/test
setfattr -n security.selinux -v 'system_u:object_r:bin_t:s0' /tmp/test
```

enter a container with:
```
-v /tmp:/a 
--tmpfs /b
```

Validate this works in the container:
```
# touch x
# touch /a/x
# setfattr -n security.selinux -v 'system_u:object_r:bin_t:s0' /x
# setfattr -n security.selinux -v 'system_u:object_r:bin_t:s0' /a/x
```

Issue:
```
# touch /b/x
# setfattr -n security.selinux -v 'system_u:object_r:bin_t:s0' /b/x
```

title: Using volume mount subpath with SELinux labelling

labels.name: kind/feature
labels.description: Categorizes issue or PR as related to a new feature.

body:
### Feature request description

I would like to mount a volume into a container. I need both the subpath feature and the automatic SELinux labelling feature. But there doesn't seem to be a way to do both, seemingly due to a limitation in CLI options.

To use subpath, I need to use the `--mount` flag with the `subpath` option; to use automatic SELinux relabelling, I need to use the `--volume` flag with the `z` or `Z` option. I want both.

### Suggest potential solution

Either:

- add a `subpath` option to the `--volume` flag
- or add `z` and `Z` options to the `--mount` flag

Or ideally both.

### Have you considered any alternatives?

Treat it as if those two features are completely incompatible and only use one of them at a time. Not ideal.

title: libpod: compare graph driver DB override against user config, not resolved value
body:
The `mergeDBConfig` function corrects runtime config values to match those stored in the database. Every sibling override in this function already uses `Debugf`: run root, graph root, static dir, tmp dir, and volume path. Only the graph driver override was logged at `Errorf`, despite having identical semantics (the DB value unconditionally wins).

A config mismatch alone is not an error condition — it simply means the user's config or compiled-in default differs from the DB-stored driver. The DB is the authoritative source; the override is intentional.

This change is consistent with the existing `Debugf` pattern used for all other `mergeDBConfig` overrides on lines 1106, 1115, 1132, 1139, and 1146 of `libpod/runtime.go`.

title: File permissions issue in multistage builds

labels.name: kind/bug
labels.description: Categorizes issue or PR as related to a bug.

labels.name: remote
labels.description: Problem is in podman-remote

body:
### Issue Description

There appears to be some kind of a race condition in multistage builds.
Directories containing mounts from another stage sometimes end up having incorrect permissions.

### Steps to reproduce the issue

Here is a minimal reproducer:

```
FROM docker.io/alpine AS base

FROM docker.io/alpine
USER nobody:nogroup
WORKDIR /tmp
RUN touch 1
RUN --mount=from=base,source=/tmp,target=/tmp/x \
    touch 2
RUN echo -n "$(stat -c "mode = %A " /tmp)"; touch 3 && echo "OK" || echo "FAIL"
```

title: Add `memAvailable` field to `/libpod/info` host response

labels.name: kind/feature
labels.description: Categorizes issue or PR as related to a new feature.

labels.name: triaged
labels.description: Issue has been triaged

labels.name: storage
labels.description: Issue is in containers/storage

body: ### Feature request description The `GET /libpod/info` endpoint currently returns `host.memTotal` and `host.memFree` but does not expose `host.memAvailable`. Consumers of this API compute e.g. "used memory" as `memTotal - memFree`. On Linux, `MemFree` from `/proc/meminfo` represents only truly unused pages — it does **not** include reclaimable memory (buff/cache). This causes memory usage to appear significantly higher than it actually is. The memAvailable accounts for reclaimable page cache and reclaimable slab. ### Example The buff/cache is immediately reclaimable by applications but counted as "used" with the current fields ### Suggest potential solution _No response_ ### Have you considered any alternatives? A clear and concise description of any alternative solutions or features you've considered. ### Additional context https://github.com/podman-desktop/podman-desktop/issues/17488

title: quadlet: expand %N specifier in the Pod key
body:
The Pod key of a .container unit accepts systemd specifiers, `handlePod` looked the referenced pod up in the units map using the raw value, a `"Pod=%N.pod"` failed with `"quadlet pod unit %N.pod does not exist"` instead of resolving to the pod named after the container.

this expand %N to the container's service name before the lookup, matching the existing handling in`GetContainerResourceName`.

title: Podman v6.0.0 default machine does not support rootful

labels.name: kind/bug
labels.description: Categorizes issue or PR as related to a bug.

labels.name: remote
labels.description: Problem is in podman-remote

labels.name: windows
labels.description: issue/bug on Windows

body:
### Issue Description

The default podman machine for WSL on windows does not support rootful mode on podman v6.0.0, most probably due to removed support for iptables.

I'm new to using podman so I installed the latest version 6.0.0 on my windows 11 machine. I then installed podman-desktop and created a default podman machine to run containers. After this I noticed I couldn't run most of the commands listed in the [Podman for Windows](https://github.com/podman-container-tools/podman/blob/main/docs/tutorials/podman-for-windows.md) due to the following error:
```
> podman run ubi9-micro date
Cannot connect to Podman. Please verify your connection to the Linux system using `podman system connection list`, or try `podman machine init` and `podman machine start` to manage a new Linux VM
Error: unable to connect to Podman socket: Get "http://d/v6.0.0/libpod/_ping": ssh: rejected: connect failed (open failed)
> podman ps
Cannot connect to Podman. Please verify your connection to the Linux system using `podman system connection list`, or try `podman machine init` and `podman machine start` to manage a new Linux VM
Error: unable to connect to Podman socket: Get "http://d/v6.0.0/libpod/_ping": ssh: rejected: connect failed (open failed)
```

After some googling I realized this was due to the fact that system `podman.socket` was inactive, so I started it:
```
# sudo systemctl enable podman.socket
# sudo systemctl start podman.socket
OR
# sudo systemctl reset-failed
```

After this I was able to run built-in commands, but still no containers:
```
> podman run ubi9-micro date
Error: preparing container dda553ff98b6f9e68dc5ac24f802ecc61962bf7bfb732bd17e77955cc014e7ab for attach: netavark (exit code 1): nftables error: "nft" did not return successfully while applying ruleset:
> podman ps
CONTAINER ID  IMAGE       COMMAND     CREATED     STATUS      PORTS       NAMES
```

Which after some more googling led me to the conclusion that the issue is likely caused by dropped support for iptables, while WSL still does not support nftables by default, see: [https://github.com/microsoft/WSL/issues/13479](https://github.com/microsoft/WSL/issues/13479)

I'm not sure whether these are separate issues or not, but I kept them as 1 issue so you get the full context.

### Steps to reproduce the issue

Steps to reproduce the issues without podman-desktop:
1. Install podman v6.0.0 on windows 11 with WSL2 installed.
2. Run `podman machine init --provider wsl`.
3. Run `podman machine start`.
4. Run `podman machine stop`.
5. Run `podman machine set --rootful`.
6. Run `podman machine start`.
7. Observe issue 1 with i.e. `podman ps` or `podman run ubi9-micro date` or `podman info`.
8. SSH into the podman machine.
9. Run `sudo systemctl reset-failed`
10. Exit the SSH session.
11. Observe issue 2 with i.e. `podman run ubi9-micro date`.

Steps to reproduce issue 2 only:
1. Install podman v6.0.0 on windows 11 with WSL 2 installed.
2. Run `podman machine init --provider wsl --rootful`
3. Run `podman machine start`.
4. Observe issue 2 with i.e. `podman run ubi9-micro date`.

### Describe the results you received

Cannot use most commands other than ssh into the machine:
```
> podman run ubi9-micro date
Cannot connect to Podman. Please verify your connection to the Linux system using `podman system connection list`, or try `podman machine init` and `podman machine start` to manage a new Linux VM
Error: unable to connect to Podman socket: Get "http://d/v6.0.0/libpod/_ping": ssh: rejected: connect failed (open failed)
> podman ps
Cannot connect to Podman. Please verify your connection to the Linux system using `podman system connection list`, or try `podman machine init` and `podman machine start` to manage a new Linux VM
Error: unable to connect to Podman socket: Get "http://d/v6.0.0/libpod/_ping": ssh: rejected: connect failed (open failed)
> podman info
OS: windows/amd64
provider: wsl
version: 6.0.0

Cannot connect to Podman. Please verify your connection to the Linux system using `podman system connection list`, or try `podman machine init` and `podman machine start` to manage a new Linux VM
Error: unable to connect to Podman socket: Get "http://d/v6.0.0/libpod/_ping": ssh: rejected: connect failed (open failed)
```

Systemd is in a degraded state:
```
# systemctl status
● <ommited>
    State: degraded
    Units: 343 loaded (incl. loaded aliases)
     Jobs: 0 queued
   Failed: 1 units
    Since: Fri 2026-07-03 11:26:17 CEST; 35min ago

# systemctl --failed

● podman-mnt-bindings.service loaded failed failed Bind mount for system podman sockets

        ACTIVE → The high-level unit activation state, i.e. generalization of SUB.
        SUB    → The low-level unit activation state, values depend on unit type.

1 loaded units listed.
```

After fixing the initial issues the remaining error is:
```
> podman run ubi9-micro date
Error: preparing container dda553ff98b6f9e68dc5ac24f802ecc61962bf7bfb732bd17e77955cc014e7ab for attach: netavark (exit code 1): nftables error: "nft" did not return successfully while applying ruleset:
```

title: Rootless overlay-on-btrfs: post-reboot state refresh spends ~30-90s in per-file unlinkat() removing a --rm container's layer, blocking the first podman command
body:
### Issue Description

On a rootless setup with the `overlay` graph driver on a **btrfs** backing filesystem, the **first** podman command after an unclean shutdown (or any reboot with an autoremove container that was still running) blocks for tens of seconds. libpod runs its one-time per-boot state refresh on that first command (missing `runtimeAliveFile`, cf. #13240). The refresh removes containers created with `--rm`, and that removal deletes the container's writable layer **file by file, synchronously, inside the first command** - a plain `podman ps` does not return until it finishes.

strace of the refresh shows the cost is almost entirely `unlinkat()`:

```
% time     seconds  usecs/call     calls    errors syscall
------ ----------- ----------- --------- --------- ----------------
 98.01   34.532826         416     82911     16604 unlinkat
  1.99    0.700678          42     16620         1 openat
  0.00    0.000906         906         1           unlink
  0.00    0.000243          18        13         6 newfstatat
------ ----------- ----------- --------- --------- ----------------
100.00   35.234694         353     99547     16611 total
```

A second, independent capture of the same scenario shows the same shape (98.6% unlinkat, 57985 calls, 28.9s), so the profile is stable across runs.

~83k `unlinkat()` calls at ~0.4 ms each on btrfs = ~35s of kernel time (45s wall) to delete one container's rw layer (a kernel source tree unpacked into the container as the test payload). Wall-clock time scales with rw-layer content: an empty alpine is instant, the kernel-tree layer takes ~30-45s, and the original field incident (a development container after a work session) took ~89s. The failing unlinkat calls are not waste from a duplicated pass: their count matches the openat count almost exactly (16604 vs 16620 here; 9445 vs 9474 in the second capture), which is the signature of a plain recursive remove (Go os.RemoveAll style): one openat per directory to list it, one unlinkat that fails with EISDIR, then unlinkat(AT_REMOVEDIR). So the cost is simply N_files + 2*N_dirs sequential unlink/rmdir syscalls, each ~0.4 ms on btrfs, executed synchronously inside the refresh.

This is the same btrfs removal slowness as #26975 ("Cleanup after podman build takes forever with btrfs driver"), reached via a different path: here it runs inside the per-boot state refresh and therefore serializes the first podman command of the session - which on desktop systems is often issued by tooling (GNOME's Ptyxis terminal runs `podman ps` at startup; the ~89s stall made the terminal fail to launch, see the linked Ptyxis issue).

### Steps to reproduce the issue

Reproducible without a reboot by simulating one (kill the container's processes so no cleanup runs, then clear the volatile state libpod uses for reboot detection):

```
# 1. an autoremove container with a large rw layer (~58k files):
git -C ~/linux archive --format=tar HEAD > /tmp/linux.tar
podman run -d --rm --name bigrw -v /tmp/linux.tar:/src.tar:ro,Z \
  docker.io/library/alpine sh -c 'mkdir /src && tar xf /src.tar -C /src && touch /READY && sleep infinity'
# wait until /READY exists: podman exec bigrw ls /READY

# 2. simulate the unclean reboot:
kill -9 $(podman inspect -f '{{.State.ConmonPid}}' bigrw) $(podman inspect -f '{{.State.Pid}}' bigrw)
rm -f "$XDG_RUNTIME_DIR"/libpod/tmp/alive* /dev/shm/libpod_rootless_lock_1000

# 3. time the first podman command:
/usr/bin/time -v podman --log-level=debug ps
```

A real hard reset (`echo b > /proc/sysrq-trigger`) with the container running reproduces the same thing on actual boot.

To capture the syscall profile on rootless (strace cannot spawn podman directly because ptrace blocks the setuid newuidmap): attach to the re-exec'd child by PPID within the first seconds:

```
strace -f -c -e trace=%file -o refresh.strace -p $(pgrep -P $(pgrep -nx podman))
```

### Describe the results you received

`podman ps` blocked for ~21-45s in different runs (~89s in the original incident), with system time dominating:

```
Elapsed (wall clock) time: 0:21.55     (smaller rw layer run)
User time (seconds): 0.12
System time (seconds): 19.52
File system inputs: 149192
```

Debug log of the refresh (note the gap between the cleanup lines and completion; metacopy is probed once and cleanly disabled, it is unrelated):

```
backingFs=btrfs, projectQuotaSupported=false, useNativeDiff=false, usingMetacopy=false
12:23:08  Podman detected system restart - performing state refresh
12:23:08  Removing container 9ec1b90d...
12:23:08  Cleaning up container 9ec1b90d...
[empty ps output]
12:23:53  Called ps.PersistentPostRunE     <-- ~45s later
```

strace summary of that window: see above (98.6% unlinkat).

### Describe the results you expected

Removing an autoremove container's writable layer should not serialize the first podman command after boot for tens of seconds. Options that would fix or mitigate:

- rename the layer directory into a staging/garbage area atomically and delete
it in the background or lazily (deferred removal), instead of a synchronous recursive per-file unlink inside the refresh;
- or run the refresh's container removal asynchronously so that read-only
commands like `podman ps` do not wait for it;
- independently, the ~1/6 failing unlinkat calls suggest a duplicated removal
pass worth eliminating.

Even granting that per-file unlink on btrfs is inherently expensive (#26975), paying that cost synchronously inside the first `podman ps` of the session is the part that hurts.

### podman info output

Key fields (full output attached):

```

graphStatus.Backing Filesystem: btrfs

distribution: fedora 45 (rawhide), rootless
```

title: machine/wsl: fix config mount logic

labels.description: Breaking changes for Podman 6.0

body:
The current systemd service to mount /etc/containers is not working right. The Before=podman.socket causes a ordering conflict which causes the socket to be disabled and thus all podman remote connections fail.

The problem is the unit is wanted by the default.target while the socket is wanted by sockets.target which can be before the default.target is triggered. That means that the Before= line cannot be fulfilled and sometimes systemd thus seems to not start the socket. It is unclear to me why this is racy as it is sometimes also works.

This was reported by Vladimir Lazar from the PD team, our CI did not caught this as we use rootless machines by default and the problem only happens for the rootful socket so we do not see connection failures. To fix this add at least one rootful socket check.

We do however have a different CI flake that was also caused by the incorrect mount dependencies. The mount could happen after sshd or other programs run. So to fix this we must hook the podman-mnt-config.service into the local-fs.target which runs much earlier and is used for all the mounts.

Fixes: #29003

title: test coverage for pkg/specgenutilexternal FindMountType
body:
`FindMountType` in `pkg/specgenutilexternal` parses the `--mount` string — it
pulls out `type=<bind|tmpfs|volume|...>` and returns the remaining tokens, or
defaults the type to `volume` when none is given. It has no unit tests despite
a few non-obvious behaviors: the `type=` token can appear anywhere (not just
first), only the first `type=` is used, and malformed input (empty, or multiple
CSV records) is an error.

title: Configure IP Token on the network interface ("ip token set")

labels.name: kind/feature
labels.description: Categorizes issue or PR as related to a new feature.

labels.name: network
labels.description: Networking related issue or feature

body:
### Feature request description

## Purpose
An IP Token is useful when a container wants to use SLAAC and privacy addresses but still needs some predictable interface identifier. This is useful for example for services that need direct connection reachability (for example media or http servers) but are in a residential network where the IPv6 prefix regularly changes (for example: in Germany it is common to get a new prefix every 24hours).  Firewalls (like in the popular FRITZ!Box models) allow configuring the port-forwarding/firewall to allow specify an interface-id in that is allowed to reach from the outside.

However, without an IP token (and EUI64 or stable-privacy generated SLAAC addresses), this interface-id is random and therefore not reachable by clients as the firewall of the router will not allow incoming connections there.

### Suggest potential solution

Ability to specify an IP token on the container, for example via a new `token=` `OPTION` when specifying network. For example:

`--network systemd-macvlan:mac=aa:bb:cc:dd,token=::aaaa:cccc:dddd:eeee`

### Have you considered any alternatives?

Right now this is difficult to achieve, current workarounds i use (i run quadlets):

(Enable autoconf via sysctl in `ExecStartPost=`, like: `ExecStartPost=bash -c "nsenter -t $(podman inspect --format '{{.State.Pid}}' systemd-plex) -n sysctl -w net.ipv6.conf.eth0.autoconf=1"`) - see https://github.com/containers/netavark/issues/783#issuecomment-3407193971

###  Run `ip set token` via ExecStartPost and `nsenter`
#### Drawbacks
* Does not work with SELinux and --userns=auto out of the box
* Does require the `ip` binary to be available inside the image

### Use sidecar container that joins the network namespace
#### Drawbacks
* Clunky to setup and configure
* IP token gets configured some time after container startup, which can be problematic for some applications to pick it up in time

### Additional context

Add any other context or screenshots about the feature request here.

title: add logformatter back and provide better github log output
body:
Adapt the logformatter script to run again to produce nicely formatted
html logs. Because github cannot upload and show raw html files we can
only add it to the log archive which must be downloaded and viewed
locally.

To improve the online experience however github does have the
GITHUB_STEP_SUMMARY logic which allows us to produce markdown which will
be shown on the summary page for a given test run.

The problem is even though github markdown supports some html is does
not support CSS and out custom style of the logformatter, in addition
the output size is limited so I wrote another script parsing the html
output again and turning it into plain test for only the failed tests
and then show this as plain text inside codeblocks in the markdown.

With this we have a short failure summary which should display all
failures at once in the run page so maintainers can see if the failed
log was just some flake or an actual problem with the PR.

Fixes: #28828

title: libkrun: macOS resource limits cause periodic VM reboots (~every 60 min)

labels.name: kind/bug
labels.description: Categorizes issue or PR as related to a bug.

body:
### Issue Description

The podman machine VM reboots every ~60 minutes. macOS flags krunkit for exceeding disk write (2.1 GB in ~4h vs 2.1 GB/24h limit) and CPU wake limits (~550 wakes/sec). The VM receives a "Reboot key pressed short" via systemd-logind, triggering a clean reboot. `journalctl --list-boots` shows 20+ consecutive ~60 min sessions.

The heaviest stack in the macOS diag report is `BlockWorker::work -> pwritev` - normal VM root disk I/O, not a bug. Journald alone holds 2.6 GB. The problem is macOS treating krunkit as a regular background process subject to resource policing.

### Steps to reproduce the issue

Steps to reproduce the issue
1. Start podman machine with libkrun provider
2. Run containers with moderate disk I/O (e.g. PostgreSQL + web app)
3. Wait ~60 minutes
4. VM reboots; `podman machine ssh -- journalctl -b -1 | grep "Reboot key"` shows Reboot key pressed short


### Describe the results you received

Describe the results you received

### Describe the results you expected

VM journal (every boot ends the same way):
```
systemd-logind: Reboot key pressed short.
systemd-logind: Rebooting...
```
macOS diag report `(/Library/Logs/DiagnosticReports/krunkit_*.diag)`:
```
Event:        disk writes
Action taken: none
Writes:       2147.84 MB over 14584 seconds, exceeding limit of 24.86 KB/s over 86400 seconds
```

```
process krunkit caught waking the CPU 45002 times over ~81 seconds, averaging 551 wakes/second
```

title: fix: quadlet generator emits diagnostics to stderr under systemd-analyze verify
body:
Running `sudo systemd-analyze --generators verify <unit>` against a broken quadlet printed no generator diagnostics, even though the same command without `sudo` (and `podman-system-generator -dryrun`) did. The cause is in `cmd/quadlet/main.go`: `Logf` wrote each line to `/dev/kmsg` and only fell back to stderr when that write failed or `-dryrun` was set. As root the kmsg write succeeds, so nothing was written to stderr, and `systemd-analyze verify` captures stderr rather than kmsg.

`Logf` now writes to `/dev/kmsg` best-effort (preserving the early-boot and journal logging that root services rely on at `daemon-reload`) and additionally always copies the same `quadlet-generator[pid]: ...` line to stderr, so `systemd-analyze verify` and interactive `sudo` runs surface the diagnostics. Rootless behavior, where kmsg is unavailable, is unchanged.

title: make the operation status more detailed

labels.name: kind/feature
labels.description: Categorizes issue or PR as related to a new feature.

body:
### Feature request description

Currently, when I run a command in Podman—no matter what happens—it just returns the container name, so I can’t tell if the operation was successful or not. It doesn’t give an error code or any other information—just the container name. What exactly am I supposed to do with the container name if I was the one who typed “podman rm ctr”?

```bash
$ podman rm ctr # ctr doesn't exist
ctr
```

### Suggest potential solution

In addition to the container name, you should include a description of what happened, such as "error: container 'ctr' was not deleted" or "ok: container 'ctr' successfully deleted," for each operation.

### Have you considered any alternatives?

I don't think there are any alternatives to adding verbosity

### Additional context

Nothing

title: fix: update packit failure-notification team to new org
body:
<!--
Thanks for sending a pull request!

For more detailed information, please review our contributing guidelines:
https://github.com/containers/podman/blob/main/CONTRIBUTING.md#submitting-pull-requests
-->

The Packit failure-notification comment in `.packit.yaml` tagged `@containers/packit-build`, a team under the old `containers` org that no longer resolves now that the repo lives in `podman-container-tools`. As a result the mention is dead and maintainers are not pinged when Packit jobs fail.

This points the mention at `@podman-container-tools/packit-build`. The message is defined once on the `&packit_generic_failure_notification` YAML anchor (`.packit.yaml` line 56) and reused by reference on lines 71, 85, and 106, so the single edit covers every job that uses it. The individual `@`-handles on the Cockpit and tmt failure comments are untouched.

cc @lsm5 to confirm the exact team slug exists under the new org.

title: Backport workflow-hardening fix (unpinned-uses) to 5 release branches
body:
### Summary The default branch already hardened `.github/workflows/check_cirrus_cron.yml` against the issue(s) below, but **5** release branches still carry it. This proposes the same, minimal, scanner-verified fix for each. ### What's flagged (by [zizmor](https://github.com/woodruffw/zizmor)) - `unpinned-uses` — actions referenced by mutable tag/branch instead of a pinned commit SHA Already resolved on the default branch in: - https://github.com/containers/podman/commit/914e9b3f7057394401b45bbb732fb573414356ff ### Affected release branches (5) - **`v5.6`** (still present as of HEAD `3529cd31`) - **`v5.5`** (still present as of HEAD `87c980c6`) - **`v5.3`** (still present as of HEAD `a47daff7`) - **`v5.4`** (still present as of HEAD `5ca84ef7`) - **`v5.7`** (still present as of HEAD `ec1b7c98`) ### Suggested per-branch patches Each diff below was checked locally with **zizmor** and **actionlint**: the flagged finding(s) are cleared on the affected construct and no new lint or security findings are introduced. (Whitespace is normalized; only security-relevant lines change.)

title: Rootless UDP port publishing rewrites source IP before delivering packets to the container

labels.name: kind/bug
labels.description: Categorizes issue or PR as related to a bug.

labels.name: network
labels.description: Networking related issue or feature

body:
### Issue Description

When publishing an UDP port from a rootless Podman container, the application inside the container does **not** receive the real client IP address.

Instead, `recvfrom()` reports an internal Podman network address (`10.92.0.x`).

This breaks applications that need the original client IP, such as:

- Pi-hole
- DNS servers
- DHCP servers
- RADIUS
- Syslog
- Any UDP service performing client identification

### Steps to reproduce the issue

## Minimal reproducer

### Python UDP server

```python
#!/usr/bin/env python3

import socket

sock = socket.socket(socket.AF_INET, socket.SOCK_DGRAM)
sock.bind(("0.0.0.0", 1053))

print("Listening", flush=True)

while True:
    data, addr = sock.recvfrom(4096)
    print(addr, flush=True)
```

Dockerfile:

```Dockerfile
FROM python:3.12-alpine

COPY server.py /server.py

CMD ["python3", "-u", "/server.py"]
```

Build:

```bash
podman build -t udp-test .
```

Run:

```bash
podman run --rm \
  --network dns \
  -p 1053:1053/udp \
  localhost/udp-test
```

---

## Test

From another machine on the LAN:

```bash
dig @192.168.10.2 -p 1053 example.com
```

(The server does not implement DNS, so `dig` times out. This is expected.)


### Describe the results you received

## Observed result

The Python server prints:

With default configuration:

```
FROM=('10.92.0.2', 51390)
```

After configuring:

```toml
[network]
rootless_port_forwarder="pasta"
```

the source changes to:

```
FROM=('10.92.0.3', 57807)
```

However, **the original client IP is never received**.


### Describe the results you expected

## Expected result

The application should receive the real client IP.

For example:

```
FROM=('192.168.10.100', 51390)
```

---


### podman info output

```yaml
## Environment

Host:

- Oracle Linux 10
- Podman rootless
- Podman network backend: netavark
- netavark 1.16.0
- aardvark-dns 1.16.0
- OCI runtime: crun

Network:

- Bridge network
- Subnet: 10.92.0.0/24
- Gateway: 10.92.0.1

`podman info`:


networkBackend: netavark
rootless: true
rootlessNetworkCmd: pasta


I also tested with:


[network]
rootless_port_forwarder="pasta"


The observed behavior changes slightly (different internal source IP), but the original client IP is still lost.
```

### Podman in a container

No

### Privileged Or Rootless

Rootless

### Upstream Latest Release

Yes

### Additional environment details

## Environment

Host:

- Oracle Linux 10
- Podman rootless
- Podman network backend: netavark
- netavark 1.16.0
- aardvark-dns 1.16.0
- OCI runtime: crun

Network:

- Bridge network
- Subnet: 10.92.0.0/24
- Gateway: 10.92.0.1

`podman info`:

```
networkBackend: netavark
rootless: true
rootlessNetworkCmd: pasta
```

I also tested with:

```
[network]
rootless_port_forwarder="pasta"
```

The observed behavior changes slightly (different internal source IP), but the original client IP is still lost.

### Additional information

## Additional evidence

Running tcpdump on the host proves that the host receives the correct source address:

```bash
sudo tcpdump -ni wlp3s0 udp port 53
```

Example capture:

```
192.168.10.100.50368 > 192.168.10.2.domain
```

Therefore the source IP is correct when arriving at the host.

The source address appears to be rewritten before being delivered to the application inside the rootless container.

## Real-world impact

This issue was initially discovered while deploying Pi-hole rootless.

Pi-hole identifies clients using the source IP address of incoming DNS requests.

Because the original source address is replaced by an internal Podman address, Pi-hole attributes all DNS requests to itself instead of to the actual clients.

This makes per-client statistics, groups and policies unusable.

However, the issue is not Pi-hole specific.

The attached reproducer demonstrates the same behavior with a plain Python UDP socket using only `recvfrom()`.

title: compat: skip AppArmor profile assignment when service runs inside a container

labels.name: kind/api-change
labels.description: Change to remote API; merits scrutiny

body:
## Problem

On kernel 6.17, starting a container via the Docker-compat API
(`docker compose` / `docker` CLI pointed at the podman socket) from
inside a **systemd/Quadlet-launched** container fails with:

The container is created but stuck in `Created` state. Native
`podman run` on the host works fine. `podman --remote` also works.
Only the compat API path from inside a confined systemd/Quadlet
container fails.

**Root cause:** when no `apparmor=` SecurityOpt is sent by the Docker
client, the compat path falls through to the `containers-default-*`
profile from `containers.conf`. On kernel 6.17, crun's write to
`/proc/thread-self/attr/apparmor/exec` is blocked by the outer
container's AppArmor policy, which does not permit `change_profile`.

## Fix

When `/run/.containerenv` is present (podman sets this inside every
container) and the client sent no explicit `apparmor=` SecurityOpt,
inject `apparmor=unconfined` so crun skips the profile-assignment
write entirely.

Users who need a specific AppArmor profile can still pass
`--security-opt apparmor=<profile>` explicitly.

The proper upstream fix (adding `change_profile -> **,` to the
`containers-default` profile template) is in containers/common:
**containers/common#2548** 
**containers/common/pull/2548**
## References
- Fixes: #28992
- Downstream report: https://github.com/moghtech/komodo/issues/1488
- containers/common fix: containers/common#2548
https://github.com/containers/common/pull/2548
https://github.com/podman-container-tools/container-libs/pull/942

title: pkg/domain: return an error instead of nil on remote event parse failure
body:
## What
In remote mode, `podman events --format json` could print the literal `null`
instead of an event object. `ConvertToLibpodEvent` returned `nil` on a parse
failure and the tunnel forwarded it as an event with no error set, so the nil
event was marshalled to `null`.

This returns an error from `ConvertToLibpodEvent` and sends it on the event
channel (which the CLI already handles) instead of a nil event.

## Test
`pkg/domain/entities/events_test.go`: a valid event converts correctly, and
unknown status, unknown type, and an invalid `containerExitCode` each return an
error instead of nil.
