title: UBI9/RHEL PAM account checks fail in rootless Podman on Ubuntu host, causing crontab/pam_unix to reject a valid container user
body:
### Issue Description

Inside a rootless Podman container based on registry.access.redhat.com/ubi9/ubi, PAM account management fails for a valid normal container user when using RHEL/UBI9 PAM stacks such as crond and login.

The failure appears when running commands such as:

``` 
crontab -l
``` 

as a non-root user inside the container. crontab fails with a PAM error indicating that the user is not allowed to access crontab.

The same UBI9 image/PAM setup works on a RedHat-like Podman host with SELinux enabled. An Ubuntu container image using Debian cron/PAM also works on the same Ubuntu host where UBI9 fails.

This looks like a possible interaction between:

- UBI9/RHEL userspace PAM/cronie
- rootless Podman
- Ubuntu 24.04 host, kernel 6.8.0-111-generic

Testing points specifically to pam_unix.so failing during the PAM account phase. pam_access.so alone succeeds, pam_permit.so succeeds, but pam_unix.so fails.

The failing operation is equivalent to:

```
pam_start("crond", "iskylims", ...)
pam_acct_mgmt(...)
```

On the failing Ubuntu/rootless Podman host, this returns:

```
pam_acct_mgmt=9 Authentication service cannot retrieve authentication info
```

On the working RedHat-like/SELinux Podman host, the same test returns:

```
pam_acct_mgmt=0 Success
```

This does not appear to be caused by the application, Django, django-crontab, UID/GID mismatch, broken /etc/shadow, or a generic setuid failure. A custom setuid-root test binary can successfully read /etc/shadow on the failing Ubuntu host.

### Steps to reproduce the issue

Run the following on the Ubuntu host using rootless Podman:

``` 
podman run --rm -it registry.access.redhat.com/ubi9/ubi bash -lc '
set -eux
dnf -y install cronie pam shadow-utils gcc

useradd -m -u 1212 -s /sbin/nologin iskylims || true

echo "User:"
id iskylims
getent passwd iskylims
grep "^iskylims:" /etc/shadow

echo "PAM crond:"
cat /etc/pam.d/crond
cat /etc/pam.d/system-auth

echo "crontab as iskylims:"
su -s /bin/bash iskylims -c "crontab -l"
echo "exit=$?"
'
``` 

Observe that crontab -l fails for the valid container user iskylims.

Replace the crond PAM account stack with pam_permit.so:

``` 
cat > /etc/pam.d/crond <<EOF
auth       include    system-auth
account    required   pam_access.so
account    required   pam_permit.so
session    required   pam_loginuid.so
session    include    system-auth
EOF
``` 

Run again:

``` 
su -s /bin/bash iskylims -c "crontab -l"
``` 

Observe that crontab -l now works.

### Describe the results you received

Running crontab -l as the valid container user fails:

``` 
You (iskylims) are not allowed to access to (crontab) because of pam configuration.
``` 

The default UBI9 /etc/pam.d/crond is:

``` 
auth       include    system-auth
account    required   pam_access.so
account    include    system-auth
session    required   pam_loginuid.so
session    include    system-auth
``` 

system-auth includes:

``` 
account     required      pam_unix.so
``` 

Testing showed:

pam_access.so alone succeeds.
pam_permit.so succeeds.
pam_unix.so fails.

Replacing account include system-auth with account required pam_permit.so makes crontab -l work.

A direct setuid-root PAM test calling:

``` 
pam_start("crond", "iskylims", ...)
pam_acct_mgmt(...)
``` 

fails on the Ubuntu host:
``` 
as root:
uid=0 euid=0 gid=0 egid=0
pam_start=0 Success
pam_acct_mgmt=9 Authentication service cannot retrieve authentication info

as iskylims:
uid=1212 euid=0 gid=1212 egid=1212
pam_start=0 Success
pam_acct_mgmt=9 Authentication service cannot retrieve authentication info
``` 

The same direct PAM test succeeds on a RedHat-like/SELinux Podman host:

``` 
as root:
uid=0 euid=0 gid=0 egid=0
pam_start=0 Success
pam_acct_mgmt=0 Success

as iskylims:
uid=1004 euid=0 gid=1004 egid=1004
pam_start=0 Success
pam_acct_mgmt=0 Success
``` 

Other PAM services on the failing Ubuntu host with the UBI9 image:

``` 
as root:
crond pam_acct_mgmt=9 Authentication service cannot retrieve authentication info
su    pam_acct_mgmt=0 Success
login pam_acct_mgmt=9 Authentication service cannot retrieve authentication info
other pam_acct_mgmt=7 Authentication failure

as iskylims:
crond pam_acct_mgmt=9 Authentication service cannot retrieve authentication info
su    pam_acct_mgmt=9 Authentication service cannot retrieve authentication info
login pam_acct_mgmt=9 Authentication service cannot retrieve authentication info
other pam_acct_mgmt=7 Authentication failure
``` 

The following were equivalent or checksum-identical between the failing Ubuntu host container and the working RedHat-like/SELinux host container:

``` 
pam-1.5.1-28.el9.x86_64
cronie-1.5.7-16.el9.x86_64
shadow-utils-4.9-16.el9.x86_64
/usr/bin/crontab
/usr/sbin/unix_chkpwd
/usr/lib64/security/pam_unix.so
/lib64/libpam.so.0
/lib64/libcrypt.so.2
/lib64/libc.so.6
/lib64/libnss_files.so.2
``` 

The following files are effectively the same except for UID/GID values:

``` 
/etc/passwd
/etc/shadow
/etc/pam.d/crond
/etc/pam.d/system-auth
/etc/nsswitch.conf
``` 

A setuid-root test binary can successfully read /etc/shadow on the failing Ubuntu host, so generic setuid and generic shadow access appear to work.

On the same Ubuntu host/rootless Podman runtime, an Ubuntu image works:

``` 
podman run --rm -it ubuntu:24.04 bash -lc '
apt-get update
DEBIAN_FRONTEND=noninteractive apt-get install -y cron passwd
useradd -m -u 1212 -s /usr/sbin/nologin iskylims || true
su -s /bin/bash iskylims -c "crontab -l"
'
``` 

Output:

``` 
no crontab for iskylims
``` 

So this seems specific to UBI9/RHEL PAM/cronie behavior under this Ubuntu rootless Podman runtime.

### Describe the results you expected

expected crontab -l to succeed for the valid container user.

For a user without a crontab, the expected output would be something like:

```
no crontab for iskylims
```

or an equivalent successful crontab listing if a crontab already exists.

I did not expect pam_unix.so account checks to fail with:

```
pam_acct_mgmt=9 Authentication service cannot retrieve authentication info
```

especially because:

- The same UBI9 PAM/cronie setup works on a RedHat-like/SELinux Podman host.
- A Debian/Ubuntu cron/PAM setup works on the same Ubuntu rootless Podman host.
- The relevant UBI9 PAM/cronie binaries and libraries are checksum-identical between the failing and working containers.
- Generic setuid and generic /etc/shadow access via a custom setuid-root test binary work on the failing host.

When the validate-source job is re-run manually after adding a label,
it uses stale labels (from the "pull_request" event that originally
triggered it), and so the steps that check labels don't see new labels.

Fix by querying the labels live (similar to how it was done before
commits 6e597af6dc and 1da154117c).

Note the logic differs slightly between hack/ci/make-and-check-size.sh
and hack/ci/pr-should-include-tests. This is because
pr-should-include-tests is also executed locally as well as on non-PRs,
while make-and-check-size is run strictly in CI for PRs only.

title: Pasta fails to start when IPv6 is completely disabled (no kernel module loaded) - "L4 socket: Address family not supported by protocol"

labels.name: kind/bug
labels.description: Categorizes issue or PR as related to a bug.

labels.name: network
labels.description: Networking related issue or feature

labels.name: pasta
labels.description: pasta(1) bugs or features

labels.name: triaged
labels.description: Issue has been triaged

body:
### Issue Description

When IPv6 is fully disabled at the kernel level (i.e. the ipv6 module is not loaded, so /proc/sys/net/ipv6/ does not exist), Pasta fails to start rootless containers with the following error:

```
pasta failed with exit code 1:
L4 socket: Address family not supported by protocol
Failed to bind port 9201 (Address family not supported by protocol) for option '-t 9201-9201:9200-9200'
```


### Steps to reproduce the issue

Steps to reproduce:
1. Disable IPv6 completely:
* Do not load the ipv6 kernel module (common on servers for reduced attack surface).
* Confirm with: sysctl net.ipv6.conf.all.disable_ipv6 -> returns "No such file or directory"
2. Attempt to run any container that uses port publishing:

title: machine: escape % as %% in proxy values written to systemd unit conf

labels.name: locked - please file new issue/PR
labels.description: Assist humans wanting to comment on an old issue or PR with locked comments.

body:
## Problem

systemd treats `%` as a specifier character in unit configuration files
(e.g. `%H` → hostname, `%40` → `@` in percent-encoded strings).
When proxy environment variables contain URL-percent-encoded characters
(common in credentials: `http://user%40example.com@proxy:3128`), the
generated `/etc/systemd/system.conf.d/default-env.conf` contains
bare `%` sequences that systemd tries to expand as specifiers, leading to:

```
system.conf.d/default-env.conf:2: Failed to resolve specifiers in
HTTP_PROXY=http://user%40example.com@proxy:3128
```

## Fix

Introduce a bash variable substitution `${proxy//%/%%}` that doubles
every `%` to `%%` before writing to the systemd-specific conf files.
The `%%` is then decoded by systemd back to a literal `%`, preserving
the original value.

The `/etc/profile.d/default-env.sh` and `/etc/environment.d/default-env.conf`
destinations do not perform specifier expansion, so they continue to use the
original value without escaping.

A new test case covering a proxy value with a percent-encoded character
is added alongside the update to the existing expected output.

Fixes #28698

There are two more things to share.

The workflow that leads to this issue is using a container to build historical firmware releases.  We're pulling sources from git using git-archive and extracting them in the container.  During one phase of the work, we mount the build directory on the host so we can more easily edit and analyze the sources.  We started this work a few months ago and had no trouble with the un-archiving of the sources.

We were able to work-around the issue without too much inconvenience.  We extract the archive into container directory (overlay) and then move it to the working directory, links and all.

title: cmd/podman: don't warn on `podman run -ti -d` from not a tty

labels.name: locked - please file new issue/PR
labels.description: Assist humans wanting to comment on an old issue or PR with locked comments.

body:
`podman run -ti` warns when stdin is not a tty, but if the container is run in detached state that warning does not make much sense: we just need the environment where podman attach will be run to be a tty.

Running with `-ti` even in detached state can make sense to avoid applications buffering their output (for realtime logs) or allowing later interaction and should not warn users.

-------------

This can be easily reproduced with `podman run --name foo -ti -d --rm docker.io/alpine /bin/sh </dev/null` or similar

-------------

title: fix: Handle healthcheck log corruption gracefully
body:
The healthcheck log could be corrupted if the
podman heathcheck process was interrupted mid-write leading to Podman crashing when trying to read it.

### Steps to reproduce

```sh
# Run a container with a health check.
TMPDIR=$(mktemp -d)
podman run -d --name hc-test \
  --health-cmd "true" \
  --health-interval 1s \
  --health-log-destination "$TMPDIR" \
  alpine sleep infinity

# Run a health check.
podman healthcheck run hc-test

# Corrupt the log.
CID=$(podman inspect --format '{{.Id}}' hc-test)
echo "{invalid json{" > $TMPDIR/${CID}-healthcheck.log

# The podman healthcheck command fails.
podman healthcheck run hc-test 
# so does podman ps
podman ps
```

*Output:*

```
➜  podman git:(main) ✗ podman ps
Error: unable to get healthcheck log for 405cdfae215c478036f7f6cc7eed08fb866076654995fc70e14ec59c08164197: failed to unmarshal existing healthcheck results in /tmp/tmp.OvthY1k4nP/405cdfae215c478036f7f6cc7eed08fb866076654995fc70e14ec59c08164197-healthcheck.log: define.HealthCheckResults.ReadString: expects " or n, but found i, error found in #2 byte of ...|{invalid jso|..., bigger context ...|{invalid json{
|...
```

```
➜  podman git:(main) ✗ podman healthcheck run hc-test

Error: unable to update health check log /tmp/tmp.OvthY1k4nP/405cdfae215c478036f7f6cc7eed08fb866076654995fc70e14ec59c08164197-healthcheck.log for 405cdfae215c478036f7f6cc7eed08fb866076654995fc70e14ec59c08164197: failed to unmarshal existing healthcheck results in /tmp/tmp.OvthY1k4nP/405cdfae215c478036f7f6cc7eed08fb866076654995fc70e14ec59c08164197-healthcheck.log: define.HealthCheckResults.ReadString: expects " or n, but found i, error found in #2 byte of ...|{invalid jso|..., bigger context ...|{invalid json{
```

- Alternatively, it can be reproduced by killing the health check command when it writes to the log. I couldn't get "lucky" with this way, but it should be achievable with creating many systemd units like this script does:
```python
#!/usr/bin/python3
for x in range(50):
  with open(f'/etc/containers/systemd/marshall-{x}.container', 'w') as f:
    f.write(f'''
[Unit]
Description=The marshall container {x}
After=local-fs.target
[Container]
Image=registry.access.redhat.com/ubi9-minimal:latest
Exec=sleep infinity
HealthCmd=printf '%%01000d' 0
HealthInterval=1s
PodmanArgs=--health-max-log-size 0 --health-max-log-count 100
[Install]
WantedBy=multi-user.target default.target
''')
```

Running them:
```sh
python create-quadlets.py
systemctl daemon-reload
systemctl start marshall-{0..49}
```
and trying to kill the healtcheck repeatedly until it corrupts the log:
```sh
pkill -9 -f "podman.*healthcheck"
```

### Fix
- Uses [ioutils.AtomicWriteFile](https://pkg.go.dev/go.podman.io/storage@v1.63.0/pkg/ioutils#AtomicWriteFile) to write the health check logs to handle atomic writes with tmpfiles/renames and flushing.
- It also changes the behavior when reading a corrupted log file in `readFromFileHealthCheckLog` and instead of a hard error, it logs a warning and continues with an empty log. The corrupted one gets overwritten on a next write. The error could be propagated in `readFromFileHealthCheckLog` and handled by callers, but this change is localized to a single place instead of multiple callers.
- **Testing**: it adds a new system test that intentionally corrupts the log file and checks that Podman recovers (fails with the `main` version ).

Fixes: https://redhat.atlassian.net/browse/RHEL-178222

body:
Pause the container by default during commit.  It is safer as it avoids conflicts, and potentially security issues, when another process is accessing the container rootfs.

Originally this was not done because it was a breaking change and rootless containers weren't able to use the freezer cgroup controller. Now that we support only cgroup v2, there is no gap anymore with root (exotic configurations can still use --pause=false).

title: podman kube play mis-scales fractional BinarySI memory limits (e.g. 1.5Gi) by 10⁹ in quantityToInt64

labels.name: kind/bug
labels.description: Categorizes issue or PR as related to a bug.

labels.name: triaged
labels.description: Issue has been triaged

body:
# `podman kube play` mis-scales fractional BinarySI memory limits (e.g. `1.5Gi`) by 10⁹

## Issue Summary

When a Kubernetes-style YAML passed to `podman kube play` declares a container
memory limit using a **fractional BinarySI** quantity such as `1.5Gi`, podman
stores the limit as `1610612736000000000` bytes (≈ 1.43 EiB) instead of the
expected `1610612736` bytes (1.5 GiB).

Because the resulting cgroup `memory.max` value is far above the host's physical
memory, the kernel effectively treats the container as unlimited. This in turn
breaks any in-container component that auto-sizes itself from the cgroup memory
limit (JVM container-awareness, Paketo Liberica buildpack JVM memory calculator,
.NET GC heap sizing, etc.).

Integer suffixes (`1536Mi`, `2Gi`) are not affected.

---

## Reproducer

### Environment

```
podman version 4.9.4-1.module+el8.10.0+21632+761e0d34
containers-common-1-81.module+el8.10.0+21340+c6c7475a
OS: RHEL 8.10 (cgroups v2, systemd cgroup manager)
```
(Also reproduces against `main` — see code analysis below.)

### Minimal `pod.yaml`

```yaml
apiVersion: v1
kind: Pod
metadata:
  name: memtest
spec:
  containers:
    - name: app
      image: docker.io/library/alpine:3.20
      command: ["sleep", "infinity"]
      resources:
        requests:
          memory: "1.5Gi"
        limits:
          memory: "1.5Gi"
          cpu: "1"
```

### Steps

```bash
podman kube play pod.yaml
podman inspect memtest-memtest --format '{{.HostConfig.Memory}}'
```

### Expected

```
1610612736
```
(= 1.5 × 2³⁰)

### Actual

```
1610612736000000000
```
(= 1.5 × 2³⁰ × 10⁹ — the value has been multiplied by 1 000 000 000)

### Workaround that works

Changing the YAML to:

```yaml
        limits:
          memory: "1536Mi"
```

yields the correct `1610612736` in `HostConfig.Memory`. Any integer BinarySI
(`Mi`, `Gi`, `Ki`) value is fine; only **fractional** BinarySI values trigger
the bug.

---

## User-visible impact

Observed on a Spring Boot workload built with the Paketo Liberica buildpack.
The buildpack's JVM memory calculator reads the cgroup memory limit, divides it
by the page size, decides the container has roughly 64 TiB of RAM, and emits:

```
Container memory limit unknown. Configuring JVM for 64T container.
JVM Memory Configuration: -XX:MaxDirectMemorySize=10M -Xmx68718816276K
  -XX:MaxMetaspaceSize=82390K -XX:ReservedCodeCacheSize=240M -Xss1M
...
# There is insufficient memory for the Java Runtime Environment to continue.
# Native memory allocation (mmap) failed to map 2199002152960 bytes ...
```

The JVM then dies during native commit because the host obviously does not have
2 TiB of RAM to give. Switching the YAML from `1.5Gi` → `1536Mi` resolves it
completely (same bytes, integer suffix).

---

## Root cause (code analysis)

The culprit is `quantityToInt64` in
`pkg/specgen/generate/kube/kube.go`
([main, lines 1039–1050](https://github.com/containers/podman/blob/main/pkg/specgen/generate/kube/kube.go#L1039-L1050)):

```go
func quantityToInt64(quantity *resource.Quantity) (int64, error) {
    if i, ok := quantity.AsInt64(); ok {
        return i, nil
    }

    if i, ok := quantity.AsDec().Unscaled(); ok {   // <-- bug
        return i, nil
    }

    return 0, fmt.Errorf("quantity cannot be represented as int64: %v", quantity)
}
```

This helper is called by `setupContainerResources`
([kube.go#L885-L910](https://github.com/containers/podman/blob/main/pkg/specgen/generate/kube/kube.go#L885-L910))
for both memory limit and memory reservation:

```go
limit, err := quantityToInt64(containerYAML.Resources.Limits.Memory())
...
memoryRes, err := quantityToInt64(containerYAML.Resources.Requests.Memory())
```

### Why `1.5Gi` breaks

`ResourceList.Memory()` returns a `Quantity` in `BinarySI` format
(`pkg/k8s.io/api/core/v1/resource.go`):

```go
func (rl *ResourceList) Memory() *resource.Quantity {
    return rl.Name(ResourceMemory, resource.BinarySI)
}
```

In `ParseQuantity`
([quantity.go#L366-L381](https://github.com/containers/podman/blob/main/pkg/k8s.io/apimachinery/pkg/api/resource/quantity.go#L366-L381)),
when a value cannot be exactly represented as `int64 × 2^k`, the amount is
rounded up to `Nano` scale (10⁻⁹):

```go
if v, ok := amount.Unscaled(); v != int64(0) || !ok {
    amount.Round(amount, Nano.infScale(), inf.RoundUp)
}
```

So `1.5Gi` ends up internally as `inf.Dec{ unscaled: 1610612736000000000,
scale: 9 }` — i.e. 1 610 612 736 × 10⁹ nano-bytes.

In `quantityToInt64`:

1. `AsInt64()` returns `false` because the value is not representable as an
   exact integer at scale 0.
2. The fallback calls `AsDec().Unscaled()`, which returns **only the unscaled
   mantissa** (`1610612736000000000`) and **discards the scale (`9`) entirely**.
3. That mantissa is handed straight to `spec.LinuxMemory.Limit` and propagates
   through the OCI runtime into `HostConfig.Memory`.

The correct accessor is `quantity.Value()` (or `quantity.AsApproximateFloat64()`
followed by rounding), which honours the scale and returns the byte count.

### Why integer BinarySI works

For `1536Mi` (or `2Gi`, etc.), `ParseQuantity` keeps the value as
`int64Amount{value: 1610612736, scale: 0}`, so `AsInt64()` succeeds on the first
branch and `AsDec().Unscaled()` is never reached.

### Why `1.5G` (DecimalSI) also works

Same reason: `1.5G` = `1500000000` exactly, representable as `int64` at scale 0.
The bug is specifically the combination of **fractional** + **BinarySI** (which
forces sub-integer scaling).

---

## Suggested fix

Replace `AsDec().Unscaled()` with `quantity.Value()` (which already handles
sub-integer scale by rounding to the nearest integer byte):

```go
func quantityToInt64(quantity *resource.Quantity) (int64, error) {
    if i, ok := quantity.AsInt64(); ok {
        return i, nil
    }
    return quantity.Value(), nil
}
```

`Quantity.Value()` returns `int64` and is the canonical way upstream Kubernetes
itself reads byte counts out of `Quantity`. It cannot fail for valid memory
quantities in the realistic range, but a sanity overflow check can be added if
desired.

---

## Test gap

The existing e2e coverage in `test/e2e/play_kube_test.go`
(`It("allows setting resource limits", ...)`, around L4224) only exercises
integer DecimalSI byte values:

```go
expectedMemoryRequest = "10000000"
expectedMemoryLimit   = "20000000"
```

No test feeds a fractional BinarySI value like `1.5Gi` through `kube play` and
asserts that `HostConfig.Memory` equals the expected byte count. Adding such a
case would have caught this immediately and should accompany the fix.

Suggested assertion (pseudo-code):

```go
// memory: "1.5Gi"  → expect HostConfig.Memory == 1610612736
inspect := podmanTest.PodmanExitCleanly("inspect", ctr, "--format", "{{.HostConfig.Memory}}")
Expect(inspect.OutputToString()).To(Equal("1610612736"))
```

---

## Checklist

- [x] Reproducible with the YAML above on podman 4.9.4 (RHEL 8 module stream).
- [x] Source code on `main` still contains the same `quantityToInt64`
      implementation as of the time of filing.
- [x] Workaround available (use integer `Mi` instead of fractional `Gi`).
- [ ] Fix + regression test pending.

title: ci: restrict specific workflows to the upstream repository
body:
#### What does this PR do?
Fixed #28757 

All GitHub workflows fail because they require secrets. The only exception is `zizmor.yaml`, which runs a static analysis security check on GitHub Actions.

Here is the corrected list of workflows that should be restricted to upstream(`containers/podman`), categorized by why they will fail or act improperly in a fork:

1. Require Custom Upstream Secrets
They rely on secrets that are only available in the upstream repository:
* `check_cirrus_cron.yml`: Uses `ACTION_MAIL_*` secrets for alerting.
* `cherry-pick.yml`: Uses `CHERRY_PICK_TOKEN` to automate pushing to release branches.
* `dev-bump.yml`: Uses `PODMANBOT_TOKEN` to push version bumps.
* `first_contrib_cert_generator.yml`: Uses `CERTIFICATES_REPO_TOKEN` to commit to the external contributor certificates repo.
* `issue_pr_lock.yml`: Uses `STALE_LOCKING_APP_PRIVATE_KEY` and `ACTION_MAIL_*` secrets.
* `machine-os-pr.yml`: Uses `PODMANBOT_TOKEN` to push updates.
* `release.yml`: The primary release pipeline; requires Apple signing (`MACOS_*`), Azure signing (`AZ_*`), `ACTION_MAIL_*`, and `PODMANBOT_TOKEN`.
* `update-podmanio.yml`: Uses `PODMANBOT_TOKEN` to push updates to the `containers/podman.io` repository.

2. Manage Upstream Issue/PR Tracker State 
These workflows require write permissions to automatically manage issues, labels, and assignments. 
* `assign.yml`: Self-assigns issues.
* `issue-labeler.yml`: Automatically applies labels to new issues.
* `labeler.yml`: Automatically applies labels to PRs based on changed file paths.
* `needs-info-labeler.yaml`: Automates comments when the `needs-info` label is added.
* `stale.yml`: Marks older issues and PRs as stale and closes them.


➕  Additional Details
I refactored several complex `if` conditions using YAML multi-line strings (`|`) to improve readability and maintainability.

#### Does this PR introduce a user-facing change?

```release-note
None
```

title: `podman machine`: fail `init` / `set --disk-size` when size exceeds available host storage

labels.name: kind/feature
labels.description: Categorizes issue or PR as related to a new feature.

labels.name: macos
labels.description: MacOS (OSX) related

body:
### Feature request description

`podman machine init` and `podman machine set --disk-size` accept any `--disk-size` value (in **GiB**, per `podman-machine-init(1)`) without checking host storage. Users can request far more disk than the machine volume can hold. For example `--disk-size 102400` when they meant ~100 GB.

In [#28675](https://github.com/containers/podman/issues/28675), that misconfiguration showed `100TiB` in `podman machine list` and led to macOS kernel panics on shutdown (`vfs shutdown in progress`). The reporter fixed it by recreating the machine with `--disk-size 100`.

Podman should fail early with a clear error instead of allowing init/resize to succeed.

### Suggest potential solution

Before creating or growing the VM disk (`podman machine init` and `set --disk-size` where supported), compare the requested size (GiB) to **free space** on the filesystem that stores machine images (from `GetMachineDirs`), minus a small safety margin.

Example error:

```text
Error: machine disk size 102400 GiB exceeds available space on /Users/me/.local/share/containers/podman/machine/applehv (available: 412 GiB).
```

### Have you considered any alternatives?

A clear and concise description of any alternative solutions or features you've considered.

### Additional context

Add any other context or screenshots about the feature request here.

title: Docker-compat /containers/{id}/stats reports inflated CPU% for containers inside pods (cgroup v2, rootless, systemd)

labels.name: kind/bug
labels.description: Categorizes issue or PR as related to a bug.

labels.name: triaged
labels.description: Issue has been triaged

body:
### Issue Description

The Docker-compatible stats endpoint (`GET /containers/{id}/stats`) returns CPU usage data that produces inflated and unstable CPU% values for containers running inside a Podman pod, while `podman stats` (which uses a separate code path) reports correct and stable values for the same containers. Standalone (non-pod) containers behave correctly via both interfaces.

This was originally reported as a Beszel monitoring bug: henrygd/beszel#1953. Beszel reads `cpu_stats` and `precpu_stats` from the Docker-compat endpoint and applies the standard formula

```
CPU% = (delta_container_cpu / delta_system_cpu) * online_cpus * 100
```

For containers inside a pod, this produces values inflated by a roughly constant ~3.5x factor against `podman stats`, with occasional large spikes.


### Steps to reproduce the issue

1. Create a rootless pod with several containers (e.g. a Quadlet-based pod) on a system using cgroup v2 + systemd.
2. Open two terminals and run, in parallel, the same diagnostic against one standalone container and one pod container:

```bash
curl -s --unix-socket /run/user/$(id -u)/podman/podman.sock \
  "http://localhost/containers/<id>/stats?stream=true" | python3 -c "
import sys,json,time
t0 = time.time()
for line in sys.stdin:
    line = line.strip()
    if not line: continue
    d = json.loads(line)
    delta_sys = d['cpu_stats']['system_cpu_usage'] - d['precpu_stats'].get('system_cpu_usage', 0)
    delta_cpu = d['cpu_stats']['cpu_usage']['total_usage'] - d['precpu_stats']['cpu_usage']['total_usage']
    pct = (delta_cpu / delta_sys * 6 * 100) if delta_sys > 0 else 0
    print(f't={time.time()-t0:.1f}s  delta_cpu={delta_cpu:>12,}  delta_sys={delta_sys:>13,}  CPU%={pct:6.2f}%')
    if time.time()-t0 > 60: break"
```
3. Compare against `podman stats <container> --no-stream` polled at the same time.

### Describe the results you received

For an idle pod container (`paperless-broker`, ~3.3% steady-state CPU per `podman stats`):

```
t=10.0s  delta_cpu=           0  delta_sys=    9,138,000  CPU%=  0.00%
t=10.0s  delta_cpu=  11,799,000  delta_sys=3,495,295,000  CPU%=  2.03%
t=30.8s  delta_cpu=  11,573,000  delta_sys=3,216,776,000  CPU%=  2.16%
t=30.8s  delta_cpu=  16,697,000  delta_sys=1,624,403,000  CPU%=  6.17%
t=30.8s  delta_cpu=  16,789,000  delta_sys=1,664,114,000  CPU%=  6.05%
t=45.8s  delta_cpu=2,324,840,000  delta_sys=3,034,315,000  CPU%=459.71%
t=45.8s  delta_cpu=  14,667,000  delta_sys=  707,226,000  CPU%= 12.44%
t=45.8s  delta_cpu=  17,392,000  delta_sys=  454,051,000  CPU%= 22.98%
t=55.8s  delta_cpu=  17,126,000  delta_sys=  511,774,000  CPU%= 20.08%
t=55.8s  delta_cpu=  11,190,000  delta_sys=1,499,132,000  CPU%=  4.48%
t=70.8s  delta_cpu=  13,929,000  delta_sys=  945,633,000  CPU%=  8.84%
```

`podman stats` for the same container in the same time window:

```
t=3m34.337265s  CPU%=3.37%
t=3m34.369373s  CPU%=3.36%
t=3m34.388126s  CPU%=3.36%
t=3m34.42091s   CPU%=3.35%
t=3m36.905244s  CPU%=3.38%
```

For an idle standalone container (`navidrome`), the same diagnostic produces stable, plausible values throughout (0.5%–3.2%, matching `podman stats`).

Observations:

1. `delta_sys` is highly inconsistent across samples within a single stream — ranging from ~10ms to ~3.5s of "system CPU time" between consecutive samples that arrive within tens of milliseconds of each other. Multiple samples often arrive at the same wall-clock timestamp.
2. For pod containers, a `delta_cpu` jump of ~2.3s of CPU time in a single sample is observed — physically impossible for an idle ~3% container.
3. After such a jump, subsequent samples report inflated values for the rest of the session.
4. `system_cpu_usage` is the same order of magnitude for pod and standalone containers (~2×10¹² ns), so the issue is not the `system_cpu_usage` baseline.
5. `cpu_usage.total_usage` matches the container's `libpod-payload-*/cpu.stat` cgroup file exactly when checked directly — the raw value appears correct; the inconsistency is in how it interacts with `precpu_stats` in the streaming response.


### Describe the results you expected

The Docker-compat stats endpoint should return `cpu_stats`/`precpu_stats` pairs whose deltas yield CPU% values consistent with `podman stats` (and `docker stats` on Docker), for both pod and standalone containers.

title: Improvements for hack/golangci-lint.sh

labels.name: locked - please file new issue/PR
labels.description: Assist humans wanting to comment on an old issue or PR with locked comments.

body:
_(useful bits extracted from #28740)_

1. hack: reuse already installed golangci-lint
    
    When a specific version of golangci-lint is already available in $PATH,
    use it instead of installing one locally.

2. hack/golangci-lint.sh: default GOARCH=arm64 for darwin
    
    Since commit f87cefc262 (Remove Intel MacOS support), Mac builds are
    arm64-only and pkg/machine/libkrun is gated on darwin && arm64. When
    linting darwin from an amd64 host (e.g. an ubuntu-latest GitHub
    Actions runner), the default GOARCH=amd64 leaves libkrun with no
    files for the build constraints, which trips a typecheck error:
    
    `pkg/machine/provider/platform_darwin.go: could not import go.podman.io/podman/v6/pkg/machine/libkrun (-: build constraints exclude all Go files in pkg/machine/libkrun)`
    
    Cirrus's Mac task runs on actual arm64 hardware so GOARCH is
    implicitly arm64 there, masking the issue. To make the script work
    identically on any host, force GOARCH=arm64 when GOOS=darwin and
    the caller hasn't set GOARCH.

```release-note
None
```

title: Disable `check_cirrus_cron` workflow on forked repositories
body:
**Description**
Currently, the check_cirrus_cron GitHub Actions workflow (.github/workflows/check_cirrus_cron.yml or similar) can be triggered on forked repositories if a contributor enables GitHub Actions.

**The Problem**
Because forked repositories do not have access to the upstream repository's secrets (such as SECRET_CIRRUS_API_KEY, ACTION_MAIL_SERVER, ACTION_MAIL_PASSWORD, etc.), the workflow inevitably fails. This causes unnecessary workflow failure notifications and clutters the Actions tab for contributors, creating confusion.

**Proposed Soltion**
To prevent this, we should restrict the cron_failures job so that it only runs on the upstream repository. We can easily achieve this by adding an if condition at the job level.

```
jobs:
  cron_failures:
    # Add this condition to prevent execution on forks
    if: github.repository == 'containers/podman'
    runs-on: ubuntu-latest
    steps:
      - uses: actions/checkout@v6
        with:
# ... remaining code ...
```

labels.name: kind/api-change

body:
_(inspired by the discussion at https://github.com/containers/podman/pull/28733#discussion_r3272731084 as well as by https://github.com/opencontainers/runc/pull/5061)._

1. Replace os.Is* error checks with errors.Is
    
    Using os.Is{Exist,NotExist,Permission} checks is not recommended in the
    new code (see official documentation). While using it in the existing
    code is OK, it may still result in a subtle errors later (for a specific
    example of that, see [1]).
    
    Replace those with errors.Is.
    
    Generated by:
    
            gofmt -r 'os.IsExist(a) -> errors.Is(a, os.ErrExist)' -w .
            gofmt -r 'os.IsNotExist(a) -> errors.Is(a, os.ErrNotExist)' -w .
            gofmt -r 'os.IsPermission(a) -> errors.Is(a, os.ErrPermission)' -w .
            goimports -w .
            git diff vendor test/tools/vendor | patch -p1 -R
    
    [1]: https://github.com/opencontainers/runc/pull/5061

2. .golangci.yml: deny using obsoleted os.Is... checks
    
    They were replaced by errors.Is by the previous commit, and shall not
    crawl back in.

3. ci: rm contrib/cirrus/check_go_changes.sh
    
    This functionality is superseded by golangci-lint.

title: Healthcheck fails/hangs if containers started through a different storage configuration

labels.name: kind/bug

body:
### Issue Description

If podman is configured to use a different storage configuration file (e.g. through the `CONTAINERS_STORAGE_CONF` environment variable), any containers with healthchecks will hang with status "starting" because the systemd service for the healthcheck doesn't include the different storage configuration file, so the healthcheck service won't find the container.

The healthcheck service only configures the `PATH` environment variable, so any extra environment variables that change podman's behaviour, such as `CONTAINERS_CONF`, `CONTAINERS_REGISTRIES_CONF`, and `CONTAINERS_STORAGE_CONF` aren't included and can cause healthchecks to fail and/or hang indefinitely.

Running the exact same command in the healthcheck service on the same shell with the environment variables works.

This is a blocking issue for podman-compose with healthchecks.

See the repro for more details.

### Steps to reproduce the issue

```

cd /tmp/repro
cat >storage.conf <<EOF
[storage]
driver="overlay"
graphroot="/tmp/repro/podman/storage"
rootless_storage_path="/tmp/repro/podman/storage"
EOF
export CONTAINERS_STORAGE_CONF="/tmp/repro/storage.conf"
container_id=$(podman run -d --health-cmd='true' docker.io/library/httpd)
sleep 10 && podman inspect -f '{{.State.Health}}' $container_id
# Output: {starting 0 []}

systemctl --user --no-pager status $timer_unit
# Check that it's active and running, trigger is working.
```

`podman build dir` follows `Dockerfile.dockerignore`, `Containerfile.dockerignore` and `Containerfile.containerignore`  symlinks to a file outside the context directory.

This does not match the behavior of `docker build dir` (using docker 29.4.0 and buildkit 0.30.0).

### Steps to reproduce the issue

Steps to reproduce the issue
1. Create file `~/test.bash` containing

   ```
   #!/bin/bash
   set -o errexit
   set -o nounset
   command=$1
   containerfile=$2
   symlink=$3
   dir=$(mktemp -d)
   mkdir $dir/context
   
   cat <<EOF > $dir/context/$containerfile
   FROM docker.io/library/alpine
   COPY * /dir/
   EOF
   
   touch $dir/context/ign
   touch $dir/context/file
   (cd $dir/context && ln -s ../ign $symlink)
   echo file > $dir/ign
   $command build -q --no-cache -t test $dir/context > /dev/null
   $command run --rm test ls -l /dir/file
   ```
2. Test arguments `podman Dockerfile Dockerfile.dockerignore`
   ```
   $ bash test.bash podman Dockerfile Dockerfile.dockerignore
   ls: /dir/file: No such file or directory

   $
   ```

4. Test arguments `podman Containerfile Containerfile.dockerignore`

5. Test arguments `podman Containerfile Containerfile.containerignore`
   ```
   $ bash test.bash podman Containerfile Containerfile.containerignore
   ```

title: podman machine start fails for libkrun machines on macOS ARM64: gvproxy exits during ignition reboot, not restarted

labels.name: macos
labels.description: MacOS (OSX) related

labels.name: locked - please file new issue/PR
labels.description: Assist humans wanting to comment on an old issue or PR with locked comments.

body:
## Issue Description

> **Note:** This issue was filed by an AI agent (Claude Sonnet) after an
> extended debugging session on a real system. All version strings, error
> messages, and traces are from actual observed behavior.

`podman machine start` for libkrun machines on macOS ARM64 always fails with:

```
Error: machine did not transition into running state: ssh error: machine is not listening on ssh port
```

The failure occurs when running `podman machine start` directly from the CLI
(not via Podman Desktop). The machine has `LastUp: Never` after multiple days
of attempts with a freshly initialized machine.

## Steps to reproduce the issue

1. `CONTAINERS_MACHINE_PROVIDER=libkrun podman machine init --cpus 1 --memory 38912 --disk-size 250 --rootful my-libkrun`
2. `CONTAINERS_MACHINE_PROVIDER=libkrun podman machine start my-libkrun`

Note: `--cpus 1` is required because 2+ CPUs trigger a separate kernel SMP
lockup in libkrun's GIC emulation (filed against containers/libkrun).

## Describe the results you received

```
Starting machine "my-libkrun"
Error: machine did not transition into running state: ssh error: machine is not listening on ssh port
```

The startup sequence was traced by monitoring process lifetimes and running with
`--log-level debug`:

1. `podman machine start` correctly spawns gvproxy (`-listen-vfkit unixgram://...`) and krunkit.
2. gvproxy immediately begins receiving Ethernet frames from the VM — ARP
   requests from the VM at `192.168.127.1` seeking `192.168.127.2`. Debug output
   shows gvproxy sending **0 bytes back to the VM**.
3. After approximately 30–45 seconds, gvproxy exits with exit code 0.
4. `podman machine start` does not restart gvproxy. It eventually times out and
   returns the error above.

When gvproxy is manually restarted after it exits, it still cannot route SSH:

```
tcpproxy: for incoming conn 127.0.0.1:..., error dialing "192.168.127.2:22":
  connect tcp 192.168.127.2:22: no route to host
```

Two related problems appear to be at play:

**Problem A — gvproxy exits during first-boot ignition reboot:**
CoreOS runs ignition provisioning on first boot and then reboots. When the VM
reboots, its virtio-net connection drops momentarily, causing gvproxy to exit
cleanly. `podman machine start` does not restart gvproxy for this expected
first-boot reboot event, so the VM comes back on its second boot without network
forwarding and SSH never becomes reachable.

**Problem B — IP routing mismatch when gvproxy is restarted:**
gvproxy targets `192.168.127.2` for SSH forwarding, but the VM's IP as seen in
ARP source addresses is `192.168.127.1`. gvproxy has no DHCP state from the
previous session, sends 0 bytes to the VM, and the VM's ARP never resolves.
This suggests the VFKit/libkrun networking mode assigns IPs differently than the
QEMU mode that gvproxy's SSH forwarding target assumes.

## Describe the results you expected

`podman machine start` should handle the ignition-triggered first-boot reboot
for libkrun machines — either by keeping gvproxy alive through the reboot, or
by restarting it after the VM comes back on its second boot.

## podman info output

```yaml
host:
  arch: arm64
  kernel: 6.19.7-200.fc43.aarch64
  os: linux
  distribution:
    distribution: fedora
    variant: coreos
    version: "43"
version:
  APIVersion: 5.8.2
  BuildOrigin: brew
  GoVersion: go1.26.2
  OsArch: darwin/arm64
  Version: 5.8.2
```

(Full `podman info` from the running applehv machine — libkrun machine could not be started to collect this.)

## Podman in a container

No

## Privileged Or Rootless

Privileged (rootful machine: `--rootful`)

## Upstream Latest Release

Yes — podman 5.8.2 is the latest Homebrew release at time of filing.

## Additional environment details

- MacBook Pro, Apple M4 Pro, 14 cores (10P + 4E), 48 GB RAM
- macOS 26.5 (Build 25F71)
- krunkit 1.1.1 (`slp/homebrew-krunkit` tap), libkrun-efi 1.16.0
- gvproxy v0.8.8 (bundled at `$(brew --prefix podman)/libexec/podman/gvproxy`)
- Guest OS: Fedora CoreOS 43.20260316.3.1 (kernel 6.19.7-200.fc43.aarch64)
- `CONTAINERS_MACHINE_PROVIDER=libkrun` set in environment
- `CONTAINERS_MACHINE_PROVIDER=applehv` works correctly on the same system

## Additional information

The `--cpus 1` workaround for the libkrun SMP bug (see containers/libkrun) does
not help — the machine still fails to start due to this issue. The combination
of the two bugs means libkrun machines are completely unusable on this system
with current software.

Related: #20122 (Zincati auto-update reboot breaks running VM — similar gvproxy
lifecycle class of issue).

title: aardvark-dns exits unexpectedly during `podman-compose up` for 4-6 service projects on Windows/WSL2 (podman 5.8.2)

labels.name: kind/bug
labels.description: Categorizes issue or PR as related to a bug.

labels.name: remote
labels.description: Problem is in podman-remote

labels.name: windows
labels.description: issue/bug on Windows

labels.name: locked - please file new issue/PR
labels.description: Assist humans wanting to comment on an old issue or PR with locked comments.

body:
### Issue Description

`podman-compose up --build -d` consistently fails for a specific class of multi-container projects with:
Error: unable to start container "<id>": netavark (exit code 1): error while applying dns entries: aardvark-dns exited unexpectedly without error message

Containers stay stuck in `Created` state. The crash leaves no aardvark-dns log message — `netavark`'s wrapper line is the only signal.

The failure is reproducible from a clean state (after `podman machine rm -f` + `podman machine init` + `podman machine start`) and persists across host reboots and VM rebuilds. Single-container projects work fine on the same machine. The failure clusters on projects that have **4-6 services AND include bare `postgres` + `clickhouse` service names in the same compose**.

Smaller/larger composes work on the same machine — only this specific shape fails.

### Steps to reproduce the issue

1. Fresh podman machine (no prior compose state):
podman machine stop
podman machine rm -f podman-machine-default
podman machine init
podman machine start

2. Verify basic networking works (this should succeed):
podman network create sanity-net
podman run --rm --network sanity-net docker.io/library/alpine:latest sh -c "echo ok"
podman network rm sanity-net

3. Create a minimal failing compose file `repro-compose.yaml`:
```yaml
   name: repro-aardvark-bug

   services:
     postgres:
       image: docker.io/postgres:16.13-alpine
       environment:
         POSTGRES_USER: app
         POSTGRES_PASSWORD: app
         POSTGRES_DB: app

     clickhouse:
       image: docker.io/clickhouse/clickhouse-server:26.3
       environment:
         CLICKHOUSE_USER: app
         CLICKHOUSE_PASSWORD: app

     app1:
       image: docker.io/library/alpine:latest
       command: ["sleep", "infinity"]
       depends_on:
         - postgres
         - clickhouse

     app2:
       image: docker.io/library/alpine:latest
       command: ["sleep", "infinity"]
       depends_on:
         - app1
```

4. Attempt to start:
podman-compose -f repro-compose.yaml up -d

5. Observe `aardvark-dns exited unexpectedly` errors for app1 + app2; both containers stuck in `Created` state.

### Describe the results you received

- `postgres` and `clickhouse` start successfully and reach Up state.
- `podman-compose up` then fails to start `app1` and `app2` with:
Error: unable to start container "<sha>": netavark (exit code 1): error while applying dns entries: aardvark-dns exited unexpectedly without error message
Error: unable to start container "<sha>": netavark (exit code 1): error while applying dns entries: aardvark-dns exited unexpectedly without error message

- `podman ps -a` shows:
postgres    | Up 30 seconds (healthy)
clickhouse  | Up 30 seconds
app1        | Created
app2        | Created

- Subsequent `podman-compose up` retries on the same machine continue to fail.
- Tearing down (`podman stop -a; podman rm -af; podman volume prune -f; podman network prune -f`) and re-running produces identical failures.
- The aardvark-dns crash leaves no error message in podman/netavark logs — only the wrapper line above.

### Describe the results you expected

### Privileged Or Rootless

### Upstream Latest Release

Yes

### Additional environment details

- **Host OS**: Windows 10 Pro 25H2 build 26200.8457
- **Podman machine backend**: WSL2 (Hyper-V backend)
- **podman version**: 5.8.2
- **podman-compose version**: please run `podman-compose version` and replace this line with the output (likely 1.0.x or 1.5.x)
- **Network backend**: netavark
- **DNS plugin**: aardvark-dns (default, bundled with podman 5.x)
- **Container storage driver**: overlay (podman default)

The bug reproduces from a freshly-initialized podman machine (no prior images, no prior networks, no prior compose runs). Not specific to any one repo's images — alpine + postgres + clickhouse from official docker.io tags reproduces it.

### Additional information

## Pattern observed

We've run ~40 multi-container compose projects on the same machine during a recent audit cycle. Failures cluster on a specific shape:

| Project shape | Result |
|---|---|
| Single-container compose (1 service, no network DNS lookups) | Works |
| 3-service compose (e.g., `postgres` + `redis` + `worker`) | Works (10+ samples) |
| 4-6 service compose with bare `postgres` + `clickhouse` + N other services | **Fails** (3 distinct projects, ~10 attempts each) |
| 10+ service compose with prefixed service names (e.g., `lf-postgres`, `gw-postgres`) | Works |

The pattern: bare service name `postgres` AND bare service name `clickhouse` in the same compose project, combined with a moderate (4-6) total service count.

Hypothesis: aardvark-dns may have an interaction where it accumulates state for common-named hosts across compose-project boundaries (even after `network prune`), and the registration for a SECOND project trying to register `postgres` + `clickhouse` in a fresh network conflicts with stale state. The actual crash message gives no diagnostic detail, so this is speculation — but it would explain why 3-service composes (or composes with prefixed service names) work consistently while the 4-6 service `postgres`+`clickhouse` shape fails consistently.

## What I tried (none of which fixed it)

- Host reboot (full Windows restart).
- `podman machine stop` + `podman machine start`.
- `podman machine rm -f` + `podman machine init` + `podman machine start` (full VM rebuild — verified by `podman info` reporting fresh state).
- `podman system prune -af --volumes`.
- `podman network prune -f` between each compose attempt.
- Manual `podman network create <name>` + container-on-network — works fine standalone, confirming aardvark-dns CAN function. Only fails for the specific compose shape above.
- Explicit DNS warmup: create + destroy a custom network with an alpine container before the failing compose runs.
- Single-retry-after-warmup logic (wait 5s, re-run compose-up) — second attempt fails identically.

## Diagnostic gap (small upstream improvement request)

aardvark-dns crashes "without error message" per the netavark log line. The only signal is netavark's exit-code-1 wrapper. There's no aardvark-dns stderr/stdout in the logs, no core dump, no info on which DNS entry triggered the crash. **A more verbose aardvark-dns log mode (or capturing stderr from the aardvark-dns subprocess into podman's standard log) would help diagnose this kind of issue.**

If there's a way to enable verbose aardvark-dns logging that I'm missing, please point me at it and I'll re-run the reproducer with logs attached.

## Workaround currently in use

I'm running an audit on a third-party library that has ~86 multi-container compose projects across 26 exemplars. Three of those projects consistently hit this issue. My workaround is to mark them "static-tier verified; empirical boot-tier deferred" — analogous to how I treat GPU-gated options that I can't run on a non-GPU PC. The source-side fixes are verifiable by file inspection; CI/CD environments (which generally aren't Windows/WSL2 podman) verify empirically.

Other projects in the same library (smaller composes, or larger composes with prefixed service names) work fine on the same machine. Adopters of the library who run on Windows/WSL2 podman 5.8.2 may hit the same wall.

title: Fix file descriptor leaks in remote import, save, and checkpoint operations
body:
## What does this PR do?

Fixes four file descriptor leaks across remote operations and checkpoint:

1. **`tunnel/images.go` Import**: `os.Open(opts.Source)` opens the import source file but never closes it. Added `defer f.Close()`.

2. **`tunnel/images.go` Save**: For `oci-dir`/`docker-dir` formats, a second `os.Open(f.Name())` reopens the temp file but the handle is never closed. Added `defer f.Close()`.

3. **`bindings/checkpoint.go` Restore**: `os.Open(i)` opens the checkpoint archive, but the result is assigned to an `io.Reader`, hiding the `*os.File`. Introduced a typed variable with `defer Close()`.

4. **`container_internal_common.go` exportCheckpoint**: Inside a `for` loop, `os.Create()` opens a volume tar file. The explicit close at the end is only reached on the happy path; five error returns skip it. Added explicit `Close()` on each error path.

Same class of bug as #28723 and #28724.

## How was this tested?

All fixes are minimal close/defer additions with no behavioral change. `go vet` and `go build` pass on all affected packages. The affected remote packages have no existing test files. Requesting `No New Tests` label.

**Does this PR introduce a user-facing change?**

No.

title: consolidate `ps` behavior between `podman ps` and `podman pod ps`
body:
`podman ps` applies a default "running" filter and by default prints a list of running containers. This is said to have been done for Docker compat:

https://github.com/containers/podman/blob/90f38bc91141d4ff8de614e50e627a630c44c0ac/pkg/ps/ps.go#L55-L66

Whereas `podman pod ps` has no such filter and so, by default, it prints a list of pods in any state.

It might be worthwhile to have the same behavior for both. Docker doesn't have pods, so there's no 1-1 compat and perhaps that's the reason for the inconsistency.

Follows from #28707

title: Close leaked file handles in container config, CRIU stats, and playbook read

labels.name: locked - please file new issue/PR
labels.description: Assist humans wanting to comment on an old issue or PR with locked comments.

labels.name: No New Tests
labels.description: Allow PR to proceed without adding regression tests

body:
### What does this PR do?

Adds missing `defer Close()` calls in four locations where file handles are opened but never closed:

1. **`libpod/container.go` (`specFromState`)**: `os.Open(c.state.ConfigPath)` reads the container config but the file handle `f` is never closed, leaking one fd per call. Introduced in #2114 (2019-01-09).

2. **`libpod/container_internal_common.go` (`checkpoint`)**: `os.Open(c.bundlePath())` opens the bundle directory for CRIU dump statistics but the `statsDirectory` handle is never closed, leaking one fd per checkpoint operation. Introduced in #15632 (2022-08-27).

3. **`libpod/container_internal_common.go` (`restore`)**: Same pattern as checkpoint; `statsDirectory` opened for CRIU restore statistics is never closed. Introduced in #15632 (2022-08-27).

4. **`pkg/machine/shim/host.go` (`Init`)**: `os.Open(opts.PlaybookPath)` reads the playbook file but the handle `f` is never closed after `io.ReadAll`. Introduced in #25043 (2025-01-17).

### How was this tested?

These are mechanical `defer Close()` additions following the same pattern as #28723 (which was accepted for the same class of fix in `pkg/trust/registries.go`). The functions involved require complex runtime state (Container with CRIU, machine providers) that makes isolated unit testing impractical. Requesting the `No New Tests` label.

### Release note

```release-note
Fixed file handle leaks in container config parsing (`specFromState`), CRIU checkpoint/restore statistics, and machine playbook reading.
```

title: pkg/trust: fix directory handle leak in loadAndMergeConfig

labels.name: locked - please file new issue/PR

body:

```release-note
NONE
```

#### How Has This Been Tested?

- `go build ./pkg/trust/...` passes
- `go vet ./pkg/trust/...` passes
- `gofmt` clean

#### Description

`loadAndMergeConfig()` in `pkg/trust/registries.go` opens a directory with `os.Open()` to read YAML config file names via `Readdirnames()`, but never closes the directory handle. This leaks one file descriptor per invocation.

The fix adds `defer dir.Close()` immediately after the error check, following the standard Go pattern for resource cleanup.

body:
### Feature request description

## description
i have been using Podman for more than two year,  recently i tried podman container auto-retart again, 
My requirement is for all containers to start automatically when the system boots, but containers that I stop manually will not start automatically at boot.
I am very frustrated because I did a lot of work but still couldn't succeed. Besides looking at new documents, I tried writing scripts to configure systemctl or use podman generate. The most disappointing thing is, I came across quadlet, but after I tried to understand it, it didn't work (podman version is 5.4.3) and was difficult to use.



### Suggest potential solution

## user-stop label and daemon command
I hope to add a user-stop status bit to check whether it was manually stopped by the user. The activation of this status can be done by adding a parameter to the stop command or by directly adding a new command, with the status name using 'user-stop' to prevent ambiguity and possible future conflicts. 
Once we have the user-stop status bit, we can use the daemon command to automatically create a system service. Its function is to check all existing containers, and if the policy is 'unless-stopped' and the status is not 'user-stopped', it will start that container. The daemon command uses the -user parameter to write and enable it for the current user.

### Have you considered any alternatives?


## Some thoughts
I think the need for automatic startup on boot is quite necessary. Because this feature is not supported, several of my servers and NAS are still using Docker, even though I have been using Podman on my personal computer for many years without any other problems. 
In addition, I think this also affects the support for Podman on other server panels. Containers that you neither want to start nor want to delete will start again when the system restarts. Beginners will not consider the drawbacks of the daemon and will care more about convenience.
Believe me, most people do not pay attention to and often start and stop the services they commonly use (so it's necessary to enable auto-start in batches), but they will indeed stop a service they do not want to start casually.

### Additional context

Add any other context or screenshots about the feature request here.

title: host.containers.internal unreachable from rootless bridge containers: shared rootless-netns pasta missing --map-host-loopback

labels.name: locked - please file new issue/PR
labels.description: Assist humans wanting to comment on an old issue or PR with locked comments.

body:
# `host.containers.internal` unreachable from rootless bridge containers: shared rootless-netns pasta missing `--map-host-loopback`

## Issue Description

Podman writes `169.254.1.2 host.containers.internal` into every container's
`/etc/hosts` and passes `--map-guest-addr=169.254.1.2` to the shared
rootless-netns pasta, but never passes the outbound counterpart
`--map-host-loopback=169.254.1.2`. The `host.containers.internal` contract is
half-wired:

- inbound (host → container at 169.254.1.2): handled by `--map-guest-addr`
- outbound (container → host via 169.254.1.2): **not handled** — packets to
  `169.254.1.2` fall through to the default route and die

For rootless bridge containers (the common case for any custom network) this
makes `host.containers.internal` unreachable, despite podman's own
`/etc/hosts` entry promising it works.

## Reproducer

```sh
# host: any TCP service on loopback
python3 -m http.server 9100 &

# fresh rootless container on a podman-created bridge network
podman run --rm --network=podman docker.io/alpine \
  wget -qO- --timeout=3 http://host.containers.internal:9100/

# actual:   wget: download timed out
# expected: directory listing from the python server
```

`/etc/hosts` inside the container correctly contains:

```
169.254.1.2     host.containers.internal host.docker.internal
```

The shared rootless-netns pasta launched by podman has:

```
/usr/bin/pasta --config-net --pid ... --dns-forward 169.254.1.1 \
  -t none -u none -T none -U none --quiet \
  --netns /run/user/$UID/containers/networks/rootless-netns/rootless-netns \
  --map-guest-addr 169.254.1.2
```

`--map-host-loopback` is missing. pasta has full support for the flag; podman
just doesn't pass it.

## Workaround (confirms the root cause)

```ini
# ~/.config/containers/containers.conf
[network]
pasta_options = ["--map-host-loopback=169.254.1.2"]
```

Then stop all rootless containers using the shared rootless-netns so the
long-running pasta exits, and let the next container spawn re-launch pasta
with the new argv. Verify:

```sh
ps -eo cmd | grep -F /usr/bin/pasta
# /usr/bin/pasta --config-net --map-host-loopback=169.254.1.2 ... --map-guest-addr 169.254.1.2
```

`host.containers.internal:<port>` then reaches host services from bridge
containers as the `/etc/hosts` entry implies.

## Suggested Fix

In the rootless-netns pasta launcher
(`containers/common/libnetwork/pasta/pasta_linux.go` `createPastaArgs`), add
`--map-host-loopback` symmetrically with the existing `--map-guest-addr`
default. The two are both halves of the same `host.containers.internal`
contract and should never be split.

Rough sketch:

```go
if len(mapGuestAddrIPs) == 0 {
    cmdArgs = append(cmdArgs, mapGuestAddrOpt, mapGuestAddrIpv4)
    mapGuestAddrIPs = append(mapGuestAddrIPs, mapGuestAddrIpv4)
}
// outbound counterpart: without this the /etc/hosts entry podman writes for
// host.containers.internal is unreachable from bridge containers
if !containsArg(cmdArgs, "--map-host-loopback") {
    cmdArgs = append(cmdArgs, "--map-host-loopback", mapGuestAddrIpv4)
}
```

The IP picked should track `host_containers_internal_ip` so a custom contract
IP stays consistent across `/etc/hosts`, `--map-guest-addr`, and
`--map-host-loopback`.

## Environment

| component   | version                          |
|-------------|----------------------------------|
| podman      | 5.8.2                            |
| netavark    | 1.17.2                           |
| pasta       | 2026_05_07.1afd4ed               |
| kernel      | 7.0.6-1-cachyos                  |
| distro      | CachyOS (Arch-based)             |

## Related Issues

- #22653 — *Host unreachable from container with bridge network on Podman v5*
  (closed). Same user-visible symptom; the discussion settled on
  "rootlessport vs pasta" as a design trade-off, but that frame only applies
  to inbound port mapping. The outbound path for bridge containers actually
  goes through pasta already — the workaround above is direct proof.
- #24970 — *host.containers.internal non functional when host address changes*
  (open). Same area; same broken contract.
- #26581 — *rootlessport is still used instead of pasta when running a
  container connected to a bridge network* (closed as expected). About
  inbound port mapping only; doesn't cover the outbound side this issue is
  about.
- #8193 — long-term tracker for rootless port-handler redesign. Largely
  orthogonal: that's about inbound. This issue is one missing flag on the
  outbound side that doesn't require any redesign.

title: Incoherent Interface -- Expansion of %h

labels.name: kind/bug
labels.description: Categorizes issue or PR as related to a bug.

labels.name: locked - please file new issue/PR
labels.description: Assist humans wanting to comment on an old issue or PR with locked comments.

body:
### Issue Description

```
[Container]
Volume=%h/.config/[...]:[...]
EnvironmentFile=%h/.config/[...]
```
`EnvironmentFile` is a systemd directive where `%h` will be expanded.
`Volume`, on the other hand, is (as far as I know) parsed by `podman-system-generator` and does not expand `%h`.

So, while `%h` is fine for one directive, the next requires an absolute path.

I think this expects more underlying knowledge from the user than it should.


```yaml
podman version 5.8.2
```

labels.name: kind/api-change

body:
Add CDI information to podman info and podman system info.

The host info now includes the configured CDI spec directories and the currently discovered CDI devices. The devices are resolved when the info endpoint is called and there is no need to refresh these in the background.

title: Combining `--internal`&`--disable-dns` creates network without gateway

labels.name: kind/bug
labels.description: Categorizes issue or PR as related to a bug.

labels.name: network
labels.description: Networking related issue or feature

labels.name: locked - please file new issue/PR

body:
### Issue Description

When creating a network with both `--internal`&`--disable-dns` podman creates it without assigning a gateway address.
This is not an immediate problem but can become one down the line, for example, regarding docker compatibility. (see below)

### Steps to reproduce the issue

Steps to reproduce the issue
1. `podman network create testgw --internal --disable-dns`
2. `podman network inspect testgw | jq -r '.[].subnets'`
3. `podman container run -d --rm --net testgw alpine sleep 600`
4. `curl -s --unix-socket /var/run/user/$UID/podman/podman.sock http://localhost/containers/json | jq -r '.[-1].NetworkSettings.Networks.testgw.Gateway'`

### Describe the results you received

The testgw network does not have a gateway address field in the created network config.
When querying the api for the gateway address of a container that is part of the testgw network, a value of `<nil>` is returned.

### Describe the results you expected

With docker/moby it is not possible to create a network that does not have a gateway address.
This causes an incompatibility with docker or applications that are expecting dockers behavior, like the [moby client for the Docker Engine API](https://github.com/moby/moby/tree/master/client#readme) because this module does not handle the `<nil>` value returned by podman. (see below)

An example where this becomes problematic is [traefik:v3.6.16+ migrating to github.com/moby/moby modules](https://github.com/traefik/traefik/commit/8f99bbcfba10fd4a6a036d7f1c284b1e8ec9cba4).

title: Forwarded env vars not escaped in /etc/systemd/system.conf.d/proxy-default-environment.conf

labels.name: kind/bug
labels.description: Categorizes issue or PR as related to a bug.

body:
### Issue Description

Windows wsl2/ubuntu 26.04
```
podman version
Client:        Podman Engine
Version:       5.7.0
API Version:   5.7.0
Go Version:    go1.25.0
Built:         Mon Feb 23 16:35:32 2026
Build Origin:  Ubuntu
OS/Arch:       linux/amd64
```

Environment variables forwarded to containers are not escaped for systemd usage.

When using this:
`/etc/containers/containers.conf`:
```
[containers]
http_proxy=true

[network]
firewall_driver="iptables"
```

environment variables related to proxy are added, as-is, to:
```
/etc/systemd/system.conf.d/proxy-default-environment.conf
```

The content of the originals variables should be escaped to conform to systemd,
in my case there are modulos (%), for html chars escaping, which needs to be doubled (%%) to play well in systemd.

A one liner found to quick and dirty fix:
```
`cat /etc/systemd/system.conf.d/proxy-default-environment.conf | sed -e 's/%/%%/g' > /etc/systemd/system.conf.d/99_proxy-default-environment.conf`
```

### Steps to reproduce the issue

Steps to reproduce the issue
1. Host: /etc/environment: `PROXY=http://my%40email.com@mydomain.com`

### Describe the results you received
 podman logs: `/etc/systemd/system.conf.d/proxy-default-environment.conf:2: Failed to resolve specifiers in HTTP_PROXY=http://...`

title: api: emit aux trailer with manifest digest on image push

labels.name: kind/api-change
labels.description: Change to remote API; merits scrutiny

labels.name: locked - please file new issue/PR
labels.description: Assist humans wanting to comment on an old issue or PR with locked comments.

body:
#### Checklist

- [x] Commits signed (`git commit -s`); sign-off email matches author.
- [ ] Tests — happy to add an integration test asserting the `aux` JSON appears in the push stream if you'd like that before merge.
- [ ] Docs — no doc changes needed.
- [ ] `make validatepr` — will run if requested.
- [x] Release note below.

#### Description

Match Docker's push behaviour by emitting a final `{"aux":{"Tag","Digest","Size"}}` JSON object at the end of the stream from `/images/{name}/push`. Docker-API clients use this to recover the registry-side manifest digest without an extra registry round-trip.

Concrete consumer impact: the Pulumi and Terraform docker providers parse `aux.Digest` to populate their pushed-image outputs. Without the trailer they fall back to inspecting the local image, which hits the digest divergence tracked in #14779. Together with [pulumi-docker#846](https://github.com/pulumi/pulumi-docker/issues/846#issuecomment-4432420705) (where the Pulumi side is being asked to consume `aux` directly rather than inspect locally) this gives those clients a deterministic source for the registry digest.

`pushReport.ManifestDigest` is already populated at `pkg/domain/infra/abi/images.go:425` with the on-the-wire manifest digest from `manifest.Digest(pushedManifestBytes)`; this PR just wraps it into the same JSON shape Docker emits.

#### Does this PR introduce a user-facing change?

```release-note
The Docker-compat image push endpoint (/images/{name}/push) now emits the final aux JSON trailer with Tag/Digest/Size, matching Docker's behaviour.
```

title: Allow running exec with no attach streams requested

labels.name: kind/api-change
labels.description: Change to remote API; merits scrutiny

body:
This is a small Docker compat fix with the API exec endpoints. With Docker, sending a bare Exec Create (command only, nothing else set) and then an Exec Start without Detach set performs a detached exec. With Podman, we threw an error that at least one stream must be attached to. Fix is trivial; look up the session before start, check the config for attach streams, and force detach on if none are set.

title: Cannot shadow volume subtree via a tmpfs mount

labels.name: kind/bug
labels.description: Categorizes issue or PR as related to a bug.

labels.name: locked - please file new issue/PR
labels.description: Assist humans wanting to comment on an old issue or PR with locked comments.

labels.name: triaged
labels.description: Issue has been triaged

body:
### Issue Description

A tmpfs mounted inside the mounted tree of a persistent filesystem never occludes the subtree under its own mount point. The parent filesystem remains fully visible regardless of argv order.

### Steps to reproduce the issue

Steps to reproduce the issue
```shell
$ podman volume create repro  # or use a directory on the host filesystem
$ podman run --rm --volume repro:/data alpine sh -c 'mkdir -p /data/sub && echo hello > /data/sub/file'
$ podman run --rm --volume repro:/data --tmpfs /data/sub alpine sh -c 'cat /data/sub/file'
hello
$ podman run --rm --tmpfs /data/sub --volume repro:/data alpine sh -c 'cat /data/sub/file'
hello
```

### Describe the results you received

The canary file is always accessible by path. The `--tmpfs` mount is always the one shadowed by its parent.

### Describe the results you expected

The canary file should be shadowed, and trying to read it should fail with
```shell
cat: can't open '/data/sub/file': No such file or directory
```
This should be the case either in both call orders (mounts automatically ordered by specificity) or at least in the first one (mounts created according to argv order).

body:
### Issue Description

My Macbook restarts after 3 or 4 minutes when it was shutdown and a Podman machine was running just before shutting down the Mac. The same issue was reported in [Q&A](https://github.com/containers/podman/discussions/25307) but never answered.

### Steps to reproduce the issue

Steps to reproduce the issue

1. Start up the Macbook
2. Open a terminal window
3. Start Podman machine with the command "podman machine start"
4. Wait until the machine is started succesfully
5. Stop Podman machine with the command "podman machine stop"
6. Shutdown the Macbook (Apple icon on the leftcorner of the screen -> Shut Down...) 

### Describe the results you received

It looks like the Mac has shutdown but after 3 or 4 minutes it is restarting
When I log in, there is a message "your computer was restarted because of a problem", when I click details, this is the comment:

---

panic(cpu 2 caller 0xfffffe00355812c8): watchdog timeout: no checkins from watchdogd in 130 seconds (41 totalcheckins since monitoring last enabled), shutdown in progress, vfs shutdown in progress, last vfs completion time: 124 seconds ago

Memory ID: 0xff
OS release type: User
OS version: 25E253
Kernel version: Darwin Kernel Version 25.4.0: Thu Mar 19 19:31:17 PDT 2026; root:xnu-12377.101.15~1/RELEASE_ARM64_T6020

### Describe the results you expected

When I shut down the Mac, I don't want it to reboot automaticity due to an issue with Podman.

```console
Volumes that would be pruned:

validatepr-gomodcache
validatepr-lintcache
validatepr-precommitcache

DRIVER      VOLUME NAME
```

title: [Bug]: Rootless custom network ignores MTU setting in Quadlet (.network) and defaults to 65520

labels.name: kind/bug
labels.description: Categorizes issue or PR as related to a bug.

labels.name: network
labels.description: Networking related issue or feature

labels.name: locked - please file new issue/PR
labels.description: Assist humans wanting to comment on an old issue or PR with locked comments.

labels.name: triaged
labels.description: Issue has been triaged

body:
### Issue Description

In Podman 5.7.0 (rootless), custom bridge networks created via Quadlet ignore the mtu option. Even when `Options=mtu=1500` is specified in a `.network` file and `Network=name:mtu=1500` is used in a .container file, the container's interface defaults to 65520.

This causes significant issues for UDP-based real-time applications (specifically FlightAware PiAware MLAT) that require a standard 1500 MTU for internet-bound timing packets. The MTU inside the container "flaps" between 1500 and 65520, causing connection instability.

Attempting to manually set the MTU inside the container via `Exec=` fails with "Operation not permitted" (unless `CAP_NET_ADMIN` is added), and even with that capability, it often interferes with the container's init system (`s6-overlay`).

### Steps to reproduce the issue

Steps to reproduce the issue
Create a Quadlet network file (`adsb.network`) with:

```
[Network]
NetworkName=adsb
Options=mtu=1500
```

Create a Quadlet container file linking to that network.

Start the service and run: `podman exec -it <container> ip link show eth0`

Observe that MTU is `65520` instead of `1500`.

Note that podman network inspect adsb may show the option is set, but the actual interface in the rootless namespace does not honor it.


### Describe the results you received

Describe the results you received
The container interface stays at 65520. Application logs show:
`mlat-client: Route MTU changed to 65520`
This leads to packet fragmentation and loss for UDP traffic destined for the WAN.

### Describe the results you expected

Describe the results you expected
The container interface should honor the MTU specified in the Quadlet `.network` or `.container` file, especially when using the bridge driver in rootless mode.

title: Unmask in containers.conf

labels.name: kind/feature
labels.description: Categorizes issue or PR as related to a new feature.

body:
### Feature request description

Running rootful-in-rootless requires something like this:

    $ podman run --device /dev/fuse --security-opt unmask=ALL podman sh -c 'id; podman run --mount type=bind,source=/dev/null,target=/dev/mqueue alpine id'

The `--device` can be specified in containers.conf like this:

```
[containers]
devices=["/dev/fuse:/dev/fuse:rwm"]
```

And the `/dev/mqueue` stuff is containers/crun#2080. However, I can't seem to find a way to specify `--security-opt unmask=ALL` as a default in `containers.conf`, to make it all work without manual overrides. It would be nice to have that.

### Suggest potential solution

Add an option to `containers.conf` to specify unmask options, similar to `--security-opt unmask=`

### Have you considered any alternatives?

I haven't been able to find any other way to do this. The goal is to make this work with `forgejo-runner`, which hits the Docker API of the podman daemon and there's no way to pass in something like `--security-opt unmask=ALL` through that stack.
